Start trims the in point (the end stays), End and Duration the out point, Source in / out the in / out point by the typed source time at the clip's speed; regular trims (no ripple) with linked partners while Linked selection is on, clamped by the media and the neighbors with the keyboard trims' toasts. With several clips each is trimmed to the typed time, one undo step. (Batch 25)
- Multi-selection (§11 "shared properties"): Transform and Opacity show when any selected clip is a layer and edit the layers (a linked audio partner is skipped); the name field renames every selected clip; a mixed switch sits halfway and a click turns them all on. (Batch 25)
- Resolution changes go through the conversion flow's placeholder (`changeResolution`) and scale the layout (positions per axis, scale by the smaller ratio, locked tracks too), replacing Batch 03's "keep" (the Batch 25 Build). The frame rate still changes only without clips or markers until Batch 42. The Project section's default durations, default transition duration and cache size / Clear cache are disabled rows naming Batch 42 (its settings panel; §11 lists them). (Batch 25) Resolved in Batch 42: a new size asks Scale layout or Keep when the timeline has layers, the frame rate converts every frame value, and those rows are live.
- Duplicate (`edit.duplicate`, Mod+D in the timeline and preview scopes) copies the primary clip alone, unlinked and ungrouped, onto its own track in the next free span after it, and selects the copy (the Batch 25 single-clip command). The canvas menu's Duplicate row stays a placeholder (Batch 39: +20 px). (Batch 25)
- The one-click transforms are `transform.fit/fill/center/flipH/flipV/reset` for the quick row and the canvas menu (one id per action, §3.6) on every selected layer, not only those at the playhead; `canvas.resetTransform` is gone. The clip menu's Enable/Disable (`clip.toggleEnabled`, §6.16) is built with the Clip section's switch, ahead of Batch 41's TODO: Disable while any selected clip is enabled. (Batch 25)
- The color picker's recent colors are a global app setting (`recentColors` in IndexedDB `settings.v1`), like the proxy settings. (Batch 25)
- Crop to frame (§11) keeps the transform: the visible area is the frame when the layer covers it, else the largest area with the frame's aspect inside the part of the frame the layer covers (Fill then fills the frame with it exactly); turned layers get the largest such rectangle centered in the turned frame, then inside the media, with the aspect of the nearest quarter turn. (Batch 26)
- Crop mode (§7.3, Build "crop tool chip"): entered from the Crop section header or by a double-click on a video or image layer (selected alone), shown by a chip over the canvas (Crop · Reset · Done); one layer at a time; it ends on Esc (after a running gesture), Done, a double-click on the layer, a selection that is not that layer alone, or the clip leaving or locking. Body drags still move the layer; Alt is the symmetric crop (no anchor marker or measure mode); no rotate zones. (Batch 26)
- The crop aspect lock is the Crop section's toggle, shared with the canvas handles; Shift inverts it during a handle drag. It keeps the current visible aspect in media px (an edge moves the other axis around its center, a corner scales from the opposite corner or, with Alt, the center). (Batch 26)
- Crop edges snap to the frame's edges, center and thirds (thirds always, not only while the Thirds grid shows), while snapping is on and the layer is axis-aligned; no other layers or safe zones. (Batch 26)
- Crop units are media px of the media as shown or % of its side (px by default, per session, not persisted); a crop always leaves at least 1 media px on each axis. A crop handle drag writes `liveEdit.crops` like a Crop field scrub, so the fields follow it live. (Batch 26)
- Clip speed (§11, §14): kept exactly as asked (0.25x..4x). Linked (default), `in`/`out` stay and the duration follows, rounded. Unlinked, the duration stays and `out` follows; media shorter than that is clamped with a toast (§6.19). Without ripple, a slower clip stops at the next clip with its out point brought in (the speed stays). Ripple shifts what follows as a ripple trim of the out point does (a left shift stops at the first overlap, leaving a gap). The Speed section's link and Ripple are per session, both on by default; Ripple is the DS switch. Speed field scrubs apply once on release (no live retiming, P1/P2). The section's Duration is a rate stretch when linked, a trim otherwise. "Speed..." (§6.16) opens the section on its field. (Batch 27)
- Freeze frames (Batch 27 Build) are video clips with `speed = 0`: `in` is the frozen source time, `out` one project frame later; only video clips may have speed 0. Freeze frame always splits the clip's linked partners and ripples every unlocked track by 2 s from the playhead (clips spanning it stay). It acts on the selected video under the playhead, else the topmost targeted visible one. Freezes trim like images, never slip, stretch as a trim, and split into two holds. (Batch 27)
- Punch zoom multiplies the right pieces' `scale` / `scaleY` by the app setting `punchZoomScale` (1.2, 1.05..3) around their anchor. It splits linked partners while Linked selection is on, and acts on the selected layers under the playhead, else the topmost video or image. A clip starting at the playhead is zoomed whole. `punchZoomAnimated` is reserved (false) until Batch 35. (Batch 27)
- Text (Batch 28): the box lives in `TextContent` (`{ value, box }`); `Gradient` (`{ from, to }`, vertical) is defined for text fills. The vertical anchor (and the alignment) name the edge that stays in place when a text's box changes size: text edits move the position to keep it. Rasters are drawn at the render scale times the layer's own scale, rounded up to 2^(1/8) steps, clamped to 0.25..4, at most 4096 px. Glyph hit areas are padded by 4 project px and include the background boxes; text snaps with its content box. The Text section follows Clip. Rasterization runs on the main thread in the preview render. System fonts are listed on a click; only the faces used are copied into `fonts/` (with `fonts.json`). Bundled fonts carry latin and latin-ext only. Details under the batch. (Batch 28)
- Text UX (Batch 29): `+ Title` / `+ Subtitle` go on the topmost video track when it is free there, else on a new top track; a Title made with a text clip selected sits 40 px under it, a Subtitle always in the lower third (bottom edge at 78%). Inline editing draws the caret on the overlay from the rasterizer's geometry and the selection highlight in the raster; Esc commits like Mod+Enter; one "Edit text" step; the properties panel and popovers keep an edit open. Text box corners size the font (and every px value), sides set a fixed box width; no top or bottom handles. Details under the batch. (Batch 29)

- Text presets (Batch 30): project presets are files in `presets/text/<id>.json` (spec §9.7 and the batch), not `Project.textPresetsLocal` (§5.2: kept, always empty); preset changes are not undoable (only Save as preset's link and Apply are commands). Sizes are stored for a 1080 px short side and scale with the project. `TextPreset` adds `applyPosition` and `updatedAt`; applying replaces style, box and animations and keeps content, duration and position (unless Apply position). The library folder sync is a union (the newer copy wins). The Presets header keeps New from selection, Import and Export; the Global / Project toggle and the search sit in a tool row under it. Details under the batch. (Batch 30)
- Text animations (Batch 31): an animation's `duration` is the whole animation, every unit's delay included; without a `stagger` the units overlap (each takes 2.5 delays). Each plays over at most half the clip (in and out never overlap); the stored value stays as typed. Out animations play the units last first and keep the direction their name says (slideUp out moves up). Whole-text animations move the layer raster; per-unit ones draw an atlas cell per unit over a raster of the background boxes alone (at the leading unit's opacity); a typewriter reveals graphemes by count, cut out of its line atlas cells. Eases: linear, easeIn, easeOut, easeInOut (absent: the animation's own). Presets store animations in milliseconds. Text clips within 5 s of the playhead are rasterized ahead. A text edited inline shows at rest; the gizmo and hit testing use the text at rest. Details under the batch. (Batch 31)
- Captions (Batch 32): `captionTracks[trackId]` holds the style only (the cue ids are the track's `clipIds`, one source of truth); cues are selected as clips (kind `clips`; the `cue` kind is never made). Word timings are frames relative to the cue start. Cues never overlap: a cue move stops at the cues that stay, an Alt-drag copy goes to the nearest free spot within its length (else the drop is refused), a cue's trims are regular (no push, Ripple mode or not); insert moves and ripples from other tracks still shift (and split) cues to keep sync. The cue list types into a live draft committed as one "Edit caption" step; Enter splits by the share of characters (at the first right word with word timings), Shift+Enter breaks the line, Esc reverts. Import replaces the track's cues; export picks SRT or VTT from the file name; VTT inline timestamps are read as word timings. A cue wraps at the max width and draws smaller (to half size) to keep within the max lines. The highlight is drawn from two word atlases (the other words, the active word), the box mode with square corners until Batch 34. Details under the batch. (Batch 32)
- Solids and images (Batch 34): gradients stay vertical (the Batch 28 `Gradient`), turning with the layer, flips mirror them; a line is the rounded-box shape with its height as thickness. Animated images always loop from the clip's in point (a GIF's loop count is ignored); an in trim moves `in` (wrapped into one loop); images still have no slip or speed. Each animation keeps at most 128 MB of frame textures (frames at most 2048 px): past it every k-th frame is kept (lower fps); the frame list is decoded again each session (not persisted). SVG rasters follow the size they are drawn at, both ways (at rest, in half-octave steps, at most the 4096 px detail cap of §7.1). `+ Solid` and `+ Image` make 5 s clips; one solid's size handles change its size (a group still scales). Details under the batch. (Batch 34)
- Transcription (Batch 33): Transcribe opens a dialog (model with its download size and cache status, language, range) and the result is always reviewed before it goes in (the review is §10.6's confirmation; Discard or Esc drops it, nothing is dispatched before). The cues overlapping the range are replaced, also one crossing its edge. The mix renders at 48 kHz mono on an OfflineAudioContext with the playback scheduler, and the worker resamples it to 16 kHz with a windowed sinc. The worker detects the language itself (transformers.js assumes English) and moves Whisper's word times 0.15 s earlier (measured lag). Lines per cue follow the caption track's max lines. The ONNX Runtime WASM is bundled (no CDN). Base runs at about 0.5 x realtime on the dev laptop's WebGPU. Details under the batch. (Batch 33)
- Keyframes (Batch 35): a section's keys share their frames (spec §11's stopwatch is per section): the stopwatch keys every property of the section at the playhead, and every edit with it on writes all of them there (Transform: x, y, scale, scaleY (= scale when uniform), rotation; the anchor and flips are not animated), so "a Transform keyframe at frame f" is one thing on the lane, in the navigator and on the gizmo. A key's ease shapes the segment after it; new keys take the ease of the segment they land in (linear past the ends). Edits with the playhead outside the clip key its nearest frame. Stopwatch off removes the section's keys and keeps the look at the playhead as the base values; deleting the last keys keeps the look of the first deleted one. An anchor moved on a keyed layer (the Anchor fields, the gizmo's Alt drag) and a text growing around its anchored point shift every position key by the same amount (exact unless scale or rotation are keyed). "Show keyframes for" lists the sections (Transform, Opacity; Volume's lane is Batch 37), not single properties. Clicking a diamond selects it and, without a drag, moves the playhead to it (the panel then shows its values; spec §6.4 "selecting a diamond shows its value"); a press anywhere else on the timeline or the canvas drops the selected keys. Splits keep both halves exact: a key with the value at a new edge inside linear and hold segments (and past the last key), the key beyond the edge (outside the piece) inside eased segments. Speed changes and rate stretches scale the key frames and merge keys landing on one frame (the later one wins). The animated punch zoom keys a piece that already has Transform keys with the cut-in zoom on its scale keys instead (its own motion stays). The reserved app setting `punchZoomAnimated` (false) is now `punchZoomAnimate` (true by default): the old stored value is dropped. Details under the batch. (Batch 35)
- Fades and transitions (Batch 36): a transition is stored as `{ id, kind, before, after }` (frames before and after the cut) on both clips (§5.2's two halves); the Transition section's duration and alignment are derived from it (a one-sided end drag gives a custom split). `reconcileTransitions` keeps every transition valid after any command, in the command's own undo step (DocumentStore), and on the trim preview: halves without a matching abutting partner go with the partner's; pairs copied together get a new id; a side stays inside its clip; a side that fitted its handle is shortened to what an edit leaves of the handle, and the transition goes when that handle is used up (§6.10); a side already repeating edge frames keeps its length. A split through a transition's frames removes it. Solids gain an optional `fades` (§6.15 lists them; §5.2 has no field). Audio fades and crossfades are equal power, fitted into the audio that exists (sound has no repeated frames: a crossfade without handles fades out, then in). Audio transitions are crossfades whatever the picture's kind. Dips draw the color in the clip's own quad. Media bounds count within 2 us of rounding (`BOUND_SLACK_US`) and edits clamp to them (trims stopped a frame before the media start after earlier trims).
- Audio editing (Batch 37): Volume keys live on audio clips only (a video's sound plays through its linked audio clip, spec §14; `keyable` changed). The keyed gain rides on each voice's fade node with the fades and crossfades (one automation, written per 50 ms step one second ahead with `setValueCurveAtTime`); a clip without keys keeps its gain on the clip GainNode (ramped on change); an edit of a playing clip's volume keys restarts its voice. The rubber band's scale is a cube-root amplitude curve (-60..+12 dB, 0 dB at 60%); a drag of the line sets the gain of a clip without keys and moves the two keys around the pointer (in value) of a keyed one, a key drags in time (between its neighbours) and value, Shift keeping its frame. Normalize uses the peaks and refines the loudest buckets from the decoded samples when they are in memory; a keyed clip has all its volume keys shifted. Auto-duck lowers the music by 12 dB relative to its own gain curve (a second run ducks again), joins voices closer than two ramps, and counts audio clips on unmuted audio tracks above the music's track. Detach audio unlinks a video from its audio clip (already on its own track), and makes an audio clip only for a video with sound and none. Audio scrub grains play at the clip's speed through the playback graph, 30 ms ahead of the render clock. Details under the batch. (Batch 37)
- Remove silence (Batch 38): detection reads the 8-bit peaks (spec §14 "from the peaks"), which round levels up to n/127, so a threshold acts as the largest n/127 at or below it (-40 dB finds windows at or below -42.1 dBFS) and nothing quieter than about -42 dBFS is told apart from digital silence; the threshold goes from -60 to -10 dB. A 20 ms window is loud when any peaks bucket it overlaps is. The minimum silence and the padding are playback time (the clip's speed applied); a silence at a clip's start or end goes up to the clip's edge (no padding there); cut frames are rounded inward. Linked partners always follow the audio (Linked selection on or off), a link group with a member on a locked track is left out, and a group's cuts stay inside the frames every member covers (a J or L cut's lead-in is kept) so all its tracks ripple alike. Apply = the cut (pieces through `sliceClip`) and the Ripple delete close (`closeGaps`) in one transaction. The parameters are remembered app settings; Esc closes the row. (Batch 38)
- Clipboard (Batch 39): the clipboard is the tab's last copy (clips or keyframes) mirrored on the system clipboard as JSON text (`shorts-editor/clipboard` v1). Mod+V / Mod+Shift+V decline their key so the browser's own paste event brings the system text without a permission prompt (a payload there wins; other text pastes the tab's own copy); menu rows paste the tab's copy, or read the system clipboard when the tab has none. Paste lands each kind's lowest copied lane on the lowest targeted, unlocked track of that kind keeping the offsets (no targeted track of a kind: the clips keep their lanes), overwrites (Paste insert ripples every unlocked track), moves the playhead to the end of the pasted clips and selects them; pasted cues move to the nearest free spot (or the paste is refused). In another project, media are matched by name, else file name, of the same kind and long enough for the pasted ranges, else the copied record is added as an offline item (Batch 41 relinks); a paste across frame rates is refused until Batch 42's conversion. Duplicate in the timeline copies the selection (linked partners, groups) after it where every copy fits; in the preview the selected layers at the same frames on the track above (a new one when it is taken), +20 px, unlinked. Paste attributes takes each group from the first copied clip that has it (the primary first); Keyframes on brings the section's keys (cut to the target), off the values at the copied clip's first frame, static. Details under the batch.

- Commands (Batch 40): the handlers live in `CommandRegistry` (core/commands, was `ActionRegistry`: `register(id, run, { enabled })`, `run(id, context, arg)`), the labels, categories, icons, search words and scopes for unbound commands in one data file, `app/commandCatalog.ts` (276 entries: 275 registered in a dev build + `app.export`, planned). Buttons and menus resolve through both: `IconButton` / `Button` take `commandId` (a click runs it, the label and icon default to the catalog's, the tooltip reads its live key) or `control` (a TypeScript union: one of the two is required). A `control` is a field's or a dialog's own button (value toggles and pickers of the properties sections, Cancel / OK, the shortcut editor's chips, toast and start screen rows), not a user-facing action; menu openers (`aria-haspopup`) and form roles (tab, option, checkbox, radio, switch) are neither. The dev audit (`app/commandAudit.ts`) checks the registry against the catalog, the keymap and planned.ts on startup and every button and menu row as it appears. A row that acts on something other than the selection gets it as the command's argument (the preset card rows, the favorite chips: the preset id; the ruler's Add marker: the frame).
- Shortcut conflicts (Batch 40, "conflict detection within scope"): two commands on one chord conflict when both see the key press: the same scope, or a global key and a panel's binding (the panel's hides the global one there); dialogs and text editing never see global keys. Pairs the keymap file ships (the preview's arrows nudging, else stepping frames) are by design and not reported. A conflict is flagged on both rows, not refused (the user removes one key with its x); while it stands, the most recently set binding wins its chord in a scope. Recording a key: the next key press (capture phase, before the dispatcher and the dialog's Esc); Esc cancels, so Escape itself is not recordable (`app.cancel` keeps it).
- Keymap file (Batch 40, "export/import keymap JSON"): `shorts-editor/keymap` v1, `bindings`: every bindable command's keys (`[]` for one unbound). Import gives the file's commands its keys and every other command its defaults (an export imported again reproduces the keymap); unknown commands and keys the dispatcher cannot match are skipped and counted. The user's keys are stored as overrides of the keymap file in the app settings (`keymap`).
- Mod+S (Batch 03 follow-up, decided in Batch 40): `project.save` is an `everywhere` binding: it runs while a text input or a dialog owns the keyboard too, so Chrome's "Save page" dialog never opens over the editor (saving is always safe).
- Keys not in §18 (Batch 40): `toggle.audioScrub` on Alt+S (the Batch 37 follow-up; Premiere's Shift+S is Linked selection here); `app.shortcuts` (the cheat sheet) on Shift+/ and "?" (the batch's Shift+/ by key position, "?" by the character on other layouts).
- Command palette (Batch 40): lists the catalog's registered commands but the context-only ones (the preset card rows, the ruler's Add marker here, the text editor's own keys, Esc and the palette's own key); a command whose `enabled` predicate fails, or that needs a project on the start screen, is dimmed and not run. It runs as its key would in the panel that had the keyboard before the palette opened (a held key gets its key-up right after, so a step steps once), and goes first in the recent list (12, app settings).
- Menus take the keyboard (Batch 40): an open context menu or dropdown has the focus (the dialog scope, so Space, Enter and the arrows never reach the panel's shortcuts) and gives it back on close. The Zoom dropdown lists Fit and 25-400% only: a free zoom shows on the button, no longer as a row (a row is a command, and a free zoom has none).
- Clip menu (Batch 40, §6.16 complete): Reveal in media panel (`clip.revealMedia`: the Media tab, the media selected and scrolled into view; the old `TODO(batch 41)`, whose batch does not list it) for clips that play a media item; Match project size (Fit / Fill: `transform.fit` / `transform.fill`, the quick row's) for layers with a content size; the label swatches are `clip.label.<color>` (a color every selected clip already has comes off again) and `clip.label.none`. Reverse stays out (not built, Batch 27).
- Menus with commands (Batch 40): the media menu's Rename and Remove are `edit.rename` / `edit.delete` run in the media scope (one id per action, §3.6); the preset card's rows are `preset.*` commands with the card's id; the new cue row menu (the Captions tab, right-click outside the text) has Edit text (`caption.editText`), Cut, Copy, Paste at playhead, Split at playhead, Merge with previous cue, Delete, Add cue at playhead and Caption style; `preset.save` is one command for both Save as preset fields (the Presets header's when the Presets tab has the keyboard, else the quick row's); the timeline toolbar's buttons take their names and icons from the catalog and are enabled when their command is registered.
- Schema 2 (Batch 41): `Project.bins` (`{ id, name }[]`, spec §12 "flat folders"; §5.2 names only `MediaItem.binId`) and an optional `MediaItem.size` (the source's bytes at import; spec §12 "matched by name/size when relinking folders" needs it). Migration 1 -> 2 adds `bins: []`; items imported before have no size. (Batch 41)
- "Remove from project" on used media (Batch 41, spec §6.19 "Remove, keep offline clips"): the record goes and the clips stay as offline clips without a record (the validator no longer requires a media clip's media to exist, the Batch 02 follow-up's second option); they draw a slate saying "Media removed" and cannot be relinked (Undo brings the media back), and keep their transitions (nothing bounds an offline clip's tail: `handleOf`). "Remove and delete clips" removes the media's clips on locked tracks too (the user chose to remove the media); a partner left alone in a link group or a group loses it, and the deleted clips leave the timeline selection. The copied-file checkbox deletes the files from media/ after the command (not undoable: an undo brings the media back offline); a file another media item uses is kept. (Batch 41)
- Media tab layout (Batch 41): spec §12 lists the search field and the filter chips among the header actions; they sit in a tool row under the header (the Presets tab's layout: the 32px header holds the tabs and six icon buttons). New bin is in the header. The filter chips combine as any checked kind AND Unused, on top of the shown bin; the search matches every word in the name or the file's name (a copy's file name, not the project's media/ folder; a linked file's folders and name), case- and accent-insensitive, and is not kept in session.json (the bin, the chips, the view and the column widths are). Hidden cards stay mounted. The selection keeps only what the tab shows: a bin, a chip, the search or an edit (a move to another bin, a use while Unused is on) that hides selected media drops them, and hidden new imports are not selected, so Delete, Move to bin and drags never act on hidden media; Reveal in media panel clears the search and chips, and shows the media's bin (or All), when they hide it. Mod+A in the Media tab selects what it shows (`selection.selectAll` gains the media scope). (Batch 41)
- Reference import mode (Batch 41, spec §9.1): chosen in Settings > Media (a Media tab before Batch 42's General tab) and the palette (`media.importMode.copy|reference`). Files with a handle (the picker, dropped files and folders) are linked; pasted images are always copied (no handle). The handle is stored in IndexedDB under `media-handle:<media id>` (the global kv store, so a copy of the project in the same browser finds it too); `pathHint` is the path inside a dropped folder, else the file name (the API gives no full path). On open the read permission is requested inside the opening click when the browser still counts it as a user gesture; else the Media tab's notice offers Allow access. (Batch 41)
- Missing and offline media (Batch 41): four reasons, `missing` (no file, a moved linked file, an empty handle key), `permission`, `failed` (the preview could not decode it: undecodable media get the slate too, spec "offline and undecodable media"), `removed` (no record). Checked on open and for every new media; any failed file read marks it; a media back online is reloaded by every service. Relink keeps the item's mode: a copied item gets a new copy in media/ (while no import runs: unique names), a linked item a new handle key (so Undo points at the old one), a pasted offline record follows the import mode; the file must be of the item's kind, hold its clips' source ranges and have sound when audio clips use it (checked again after the copy). A file that differs (size, duration or picture size) takes the new probe fields and drops the media's caches; the same file keeps them. Undo and redo of a relink check the files again (`MediaSources.attach` follows the document; removed media lose their status at once), and a file of other content than before makes the image poster, the sheets, the peaks and the proxy again (`filesChanged`: a ready or failed proxy becomes pending). Relink folder matches the selected offline items (all when none is selected) by the file name of the item's path, then its panel name, then by size when the item has one; without a size a single name match is taken and probed; the walk stops at 20,000 files (the toast says so), and the toast counts files not found apart from files found but refused. (Batch 41)
- Reveal in folder (Batch 41, spec §12 "FSA cannot reveal; shows the relative path and copies it"): a toast with the path (in the project folder, a linked file's hint, or where an offline record last was) and the path copied to the clipboard. (Batch 41)
- Frame rate conversion (Batch 42, spec §15): every frame value is multiplied by new fps / old fps (an exact fraction of integers) and rounded to the nearest frame, halves away from zero (`core/document/fpsConvert.ts`). Clip edges convert as timeline positions track by track (clips that abutted still abut); a clip whose edges round onto one frame keeps 1 frame and pushes the next clips of its track (counted as moved). Keyframes and a cue's words convert as positions (keys landing on one frame merge, the later winning, as a rate stretch does; a word keeps at least 1 frame); fades, transition sides (a transition keeps at least 1 frame) and text animation durations (at least 1) and staggers are lengths; markers are positions. Media clips keep their source in/out (the same picture over the same time) while it still matches the new duration within one source frame (§5.1), else `out` follows the duration, clamped to the media. A lossless conversion (30 to 60 fps, or none needed) is made at once with a success toast; one that rounds asks first, naming how many timings round, keys merge or clips move. One undo step; the session's playhead, in/out, scroll and zoom (the same pixels per second) follow every frame rate change, Undo included, and gap, keyframe and silence-preview selections are cleared. (Batch 42)
- Clipboard across frame rates (Batch 42, the Batch 39 follow-up): pasted clips copied at another frame rate are converted the same way (`payloadAtFrameRate`, each lane a run from the block's first frame), and so are Paste attributes' fades, keys and animations; the "Can't paste across frame rates" refusal is gone. (Batch 42)
- Resolution change (Batch 42): the Scale layout / Keep dialog shows only when the timeline has layers (video, image, solid, text); Keep leaves every layer at its size in pixels and its offset from the center (`setResolution` without `scaleLayout`). Cancel or Esc changes nothing. (Batch 42)
- Default durations and the default transition (Batch 42, spec §11, §6.15) are global app settings like the proxies and the autosave delay (§5.2 `Project` stays verbatim): still image 5 s, title 3 s, solid 5 s, freeze frame 2 s (0.1-60 s, stored in ms), the transition 15 frames (1-120, §6.15 "15 frames") and its kind (Mod+Shift+D, cross dissolve). The edits read them from `timeline/edit/editDefaults.ts`, which the app updates from the settings (one value for the many drop, insert, title, solid, freeze and transition paths, rather than a parameter threaded through each); tests run with the built-in values. (Batch 42)
- History restore (Batch 42, spec §15): the backup becomes the document through `DocumentStore.load` (undo history cleared, as for a crash recovery: the confirmation says so) after what is unsaved is saved; the restored document is saved at once, so the pre-restore project.json is the newest backup and autosave goes on. Refused in a read-only project (the list still shows). The list is newest first by the backup's name stamp and shows each version's own save time (`meta.modifiedAt`) and project name. (Batch 42)
- Templates (Batch 42, spec §15): the frame size, frame rate and background, the tracks (kind, name, height, lock / mute / solo / hide / target) with the caption track's style, and the project's own text presets (its `presets/text/`), in IndexedDB `templates.v1` (at most 50; a template of the same name is replaced). New from template: the start screen's rows (`project.newFromTemplate` with the template id), then the folder and the New project dialog with the template chosen (its Template select; the template's size and frame rate fill the form and can be changed). Save as template works in a read-only project (nothing is written to the folder). (Batch 42)
- Recent thumbnails (Batch 42, spec §15 "captured at the playhead on close"): captured when another project opens (at most 1.5 s, else the old one stays) and when the tab hides (a closing tab may not finish; only when the document or the playhead changed since the last capture), as Export frame renders, scaled to 192 px tall webp, kept in the recent entry (IndexedDB). The recent list is a grid of project cards; the entry also keeps "size · fps". (Batch 42)
- Read-only behaviors (Batch 42): edits stay possible and are kept in memory only (Batch 03); everything that writes to the folder is refused with one toast "This project is read-only · Allow editing to …" (imports, media removal, bins, proxies, relinks, Clear cache, History restore); closing the tab with read-only edits (or after a failed save) asks first (`beforeunload`); opening another project (new, open, recent, template, drop) from a read-only project with unsaved edits asks "Discard unsaved changes?" (Cancel, Allow editing, Discard and continue). (Batch 42)
- Clear cache (Batch 42, spec §9.7, §11): asks first (making proxies of long videos again takes minutes), in the Project section and Settings > General > Storage (`project.clearCache`). The media and preview services are detached, every file under cache/ is deleted, the §9.7 folders made again and the services attached again (the document and its undo history stay): thumbnail sheets, posters, peaks, sample indexes and proxies are made again in the background. Linked media keep their handles (IndexedDB). The re-attach resets the Media tab's selection and search (the panel's initial state). (Batch 42)
- Settings (Batch 42): General is the first tab, Shortcuts beside it (`app.settings` takes the tab: the cheat sheet's Edit shortcuts opens Shortcuts); Batch 41's Media tab is General's Media group. The tabs take the focus when clicked (the field focused in the other tab unmounts). (Batch 42)
- New project keys (Batch 42, the Batch 01 follow-up): `project.new` is Mod+Alt+N first (Chrome keeps Ctrl+N for a new window in a normal tab and pages cannot take it) and Mod+N second (works in the installed app's window); tooltips and the palette show Ctrl+Alt+N. (Batch 42)
- Export pipeline (Batch 43, spec §16, §3.5):
  - The mixdown is scheduled on the main thread. `OfflineAudioContext` exists on windows only, so `renderMixdown` (the playback scheduler, as for transcription) renders the whole range at 48 kHz stereo before the first frame (it renders on the audio thread). Its planes are transferred to the worker, about 23 MB per minute.
  - The MP4 keeps its moov at the front by reserving room for it from the chunk counts (mp4-muxer's `fastStart: { expectedVideoChunks, expectedAudioChunks }`), instead of `in-memory` below 2 GB and `fragmented` above. The mdat streams to disk as it is encoded at any length, the RAM stays flat, and large files are never fragmented MP4. The moov first, as Instagram wants, holds for every size.
  - The file is written where the proxy's is: the worker's bytes go to the main thread and are written at their positions through `FsWritable` (a `FileSystemWritableFileStream`) into `cache/export-temp/<id>.mp4` (spec §9.7). The finished file moves to `exports/` (`FsDir.moveTo`: `move()` where the browser has it, else a copy and a removal). A cancel or a failure deletes the temp file, so `exports/` never holds a partial file.
  - The export worker decodes with its own decode sessions, reached in-thread (`media/workers/loopback.ts`, the decode handlers shared with `decode.worker`) rather than through a nested worker.
  - SVG images are rasterized on the main thread at 4096 px (workers cannot draw SVG) and resized in the worker to the size each frame asks for.
  - A preset's size caps the long edge: the project keeps its aspect and is never scaled up. Its frame rate caps the rate: the project's rate, divided by the smallest whole number that brings it under (60 to 30, 59.94 to 29.97, 50 to 25), so no exported frame repeats.
  - Every export has an audio track: silence when nothing is heard; AAC-LC, else Opus when this browser has no AAC encoder. The audio runs up to one AAC packet (1023 samples, 21 ms) past the video: the encoder pads its last frame, and no edit list trims it.
  - The video track's timescale is a whole number of ticks per frame of at least 90 kHz (90000 for 30 and 29.97 fps), so microsecond timestamps land on exact ticks.
  - One export at a time; the queue is Batch 44's. A fresh worker runs each export and is stopped after it, freeing its device and decoders. Switching projects cancels a running export.
  - While an export runs, proxy jobs pause (thumbnails and peaks go on), playback plays proxies (`qualityOverride`: the Proxy mode while playing), and Clear cache is refused. (Batch 43)
- Export UX (Batch 44, spec §16, §17, §2.2):
  - Presets: Reels, TikTok and Shorts are fixed. "Editable and saveable" is read as follows: changing a setting turns a built-in preset into Custom, seeded with that preset's output for this project (`customFrom`). Custom can be saved as one's own preset (global app settings, at most 30, 40-character names). One's own presets change in place and can be deleted (Custom then takes their settings). Custom before any change is Reels without the size cap.
  - Shorts' bitrate is YouTube's recommended upload rate for the output (8 / 12 Mbps at 1080p up to / above 30 fps, 16 / 24 at 1440p, 45 / 68 at 2160p): the spec names none. Its size is 2160x3840 when the project's long edge is at least 3840, else 1080x1920, and its rate cap is 60 fps.
  - Custom: the resolution is 100/75/50% of the project's size (no cap). The frame rate is the project's rate or one of its whole divisions down to about 10 fps (`fpsChoices`), so no frame repeats and nothing is resampled. Bitrate VBR (target + max) or CBR. WebCodecs has no peak bitrate, so the codec level is chosen to hold the max. Keyframes every 0.5-2 s (spec §16 binds at most 2 s). Audio at 128/192/256/320 kbps (§14). The hardware preference goes to `hardwareAcceleration`.
  - Support detection: `VideoEncoder.isConfigSupported` is asked on the main thread per codec and format (a capability query, no encoding) and cached. A codec it refuses is marked "(not supported here)" in the Codec list, and the summary says H.264 is used (the engine falls back, as in Batch 43). Here HEVC is refused with "Prefer software".
  - The estimated size is (video + audio bitrate) x the range's duration + 1% for the container. For simple content it is a ceiling: the hardware encoders do not pad, even in CBR (a 3 Mbps CBR HEVC export of flat test stripes averaged 225 kbps against a 3.2 MB estimate).
  - Queue: a job takes its document snapshot when it is queued (what the user saw at Export), and gathers its inputs (files, SVG rasters, fonts, mixdown) when it starts. A queued job can be paused (it starts paused) or removed. Each job runs in a fresh worker. The 70/30 texture split holds from the first video job until the queue is empty. Closing the project cancels every job.
  - Choose file…: the save picker opens when the job is queued (it needs the click's user activation), one picker per export, extra and Export again. The bytes are written straight into the picked file. A cancel deletes a file the picker created and leaves a file that existed as it was (its write is aborted, never committed). A read-only project can export to a picked file; exports/ is refused there.
  - Open folder: browsers cannot open a file manager, so the system's open dialog starts in exports/ (or in the picked file's folder), and a file chosen there opens in a new tab. For a project in the browser's own storage (no real folder), a toast names the folder instead.
  - Progress: the Queue section's cards. While the Export tab is not shown, the running job keeps Batch 43's pinned progress toast (Pause/Resume, Cancel, "+n queued"), so progress never disappears.
  - The log is session state of the project (session.json, harmless to lose): the last 20 jobs, done, cancelled or failed. Each entry keeps its request, so Export again repeats the settings, range, template and destination on the current document. The range choice is session state too. "In to out" is dimmed without marks (never hidden) and reads `markedRange` (open ends run to 0 / the content end).
  - Extras: Export frame writes `<project>-frame-<playhead>.png` to the export destination: exports/, or the picker as in Batch 05. The preview header's button runs the same command. Export audio is a queue job in export.worker: WAV (16-bit PCM 48 kHz stereo, no dither) or M4A (AAC-LC at the preset's audio bitrate, else Opus; the moov at the front), for the range. Export captions writes SRT/VTT of the range, with the cues cut to it and timed from its start so they match a video of the same range, named by the template. Copy frame puts the Export frame PNG on the clipboard.
  - Esc closes the Export tab from any scope as the last step of `app.cancel` (after gestures, inline text editing, crop mode, Remove silence and fullscreen). Inside Save as preset's name field, Esc closes the field only. (Batch 44)
- Modal focus (Batch 42, found while checking Settings): focus that would fall to the page (a field blurring itself on Enter, a select chosen with the pointer) goes back to the dialog panel, so Escape closes it and no panel shortcut runs behind it. The project dialogs render after the settings and the cheat sheet (a dialog opened from Settings, Clear cache, shows above them). (Batch 42)
- Performance pass (Batch 45, spec §3.5, §4, §9.6):
  - Closing a project stops its decode, analysis and proxy workers (§3.5 describes long-lived workers): their decoders, sample indexes, parsed audio tracks and heaps go with the project (P13), and the next project starts new ones on its first request. The renderer also destroys its spare video-frame and pooled blur textures then (`releaseCaches`), and `DecodedAudio.reset` closes the worker's audio tracks.
  - While a video's proxy is being made (`proxy.status` pending), its eager thumbnail levels wait (§9.6 makes sheets from the proxy "when present"): they would be made again from the proxy anyway, and decoding the 4K source beside the proxy job starved it of the shared hardware decoder (a 20-minute 4K60 proxy ran at 0.075-0.10x real time). Sheets that are shown (media cards' first frames, the timeline's visible sheets, a hover scrub) still come from the source at once.
  - No split of the main chunk (Vite's 500 kB warning stays): P12 is met about 10x over (the start screen interactive 53 ms after navigation on a warm cache, about 125 ms cold, an empty project about 100 ms after Create), and the heavy modules §4 names are already separate chunks (export.worker, the transcription worker and its runtime, local font listing). Splitting Settings, the palette or the dialogs would add a load on their first opening for a few ms of startup.
  - React commits are counted by a `<Profiler>` around the app in dev builds only (production React does not call it); P1 is verified in dev builds, where React is slower.
  - Memory baseline (acceptance 4): textures, open frames, decoders, decoded audio and worker heaps return exactly to the empty-project values. The page's JS heap ends 6.4% above a cold page after one heavy project and plateaus at +10.4-11.4% after 3-5 (the heap snapshot puts +2.6 MB of the +3.0 MB in V8 compiled code and feedback of code paths that ran, app objects +26 KB), +2.6-4.8% against the first closed state. The cold page is not the baseline the compiled code can return to.

- Visual polish (Batch 46):
  - Zoom-out limit (§6.2 "fit-to-content down to 0.01 px/frame"): a short or empty timeline zooms out until a minute shows (the Batch 07 follow-up: an empty project stopped at 2 s, with no room to see where a clip would land at 10 s). Fit itself and Zoom to selection still stop at Fit; a timeline longer than a minute keeps Fit as the limit.
  - The read-only banner (§15) is a notice in the app bar instead of a strip above the workspace: granting the permission no longer moves the four panels (acceptance 3), and the app bar stays the only element outside them (§2.1).
  - Space and Enter on a control the keyboard focused activate it (a button clicks, a switch toggles), and the arrows, Home, End and Page keys stay with such a slider or inside a radio group, tab list or list box (`KeyDispatcher.isNativeKeyTarget`). §18's Space = Play/Pause and the arrow frame steps apply everywhere else, including a control a pointer press focused: Chrome focuses a clicked button, and the switches, text buttons and some raw buttons do not prevent it (the icon buttons, menus, chips and cards do). A key that a clicked control's widget handles itself (a color square's arrows) stays with it. The dispatcher records where the focus came from: a Tab press makes the next focus a keyboard one, a pointer press a pointer one, and a focus a script moves (a closed field handing it back to its button) takes the kind of the last of the two. It does not read `:focus-visible`, because Chrome turns that on for a clicked button at the first key press, before the key's listeners run (measured in Chrome 155). (Corrected by the Batch 46 fix-attempt: the first version assumed a click never leaves a button focused, so Space toggled a clicked switch again.)
  - Disabled number, text and select fields are `aria-disabled` and read-only instead of natively `disabled`, as buttons have been since Batch 01: Tab reaches every control in the properties panel (acceptance 2), and the field shows why it is off.
  - Auto-scroll (§6.6 "speed proportional to the overshoot"): the speed eases in through the edge band (depth squared), grows linearly past the edge up to three times the speed at the edge, and holding at an edge ramps it up to twice that over a second (the batch's acceleration curve).
  - Snap lines (the batch: "none or 80 ms fade"): none. A line shows on the frame a snap engages and goes with it; a fade-out would show a snap that no longer holds.
  - The Clip section's Enabled switch runs `clip.toggleEnabled`, so its live shortcut shows: with mixed values it disables all the clips (the old switch enabled them).
  - Canvas backing stores (§2.1 "re-allocate backing stores ... throttled to one reallocation per animation frame") keep headroom (`core/scheduler/canvasCapacity.ts`): a capacity rounded up to 128 CSS px plus one step, shrunk only when three steps are spare. The canvas element is as large as its capacity, drawn from its top-left; its host clips the rest. A left-splitter drag reallocates in 4 frames instead of 86.
  - The splitter ratios are registered non-inherited custom properties (`@property`, App.module.css) written on the grids that use them and on their splitters, instead of on the workspace: a ratio written on the workspace restyled every element of the app on each drag frame.
- HDR video (Batch 47): the batch names "copyExternalImageToTexture color space handling", but in Chrome 155 copyExternalImageToTexture and importExternalTexture convert an HLG frame to sRGB without tone mapping (measured on an iPhone HLG clip, BT.2020 / HLG / Dolby Vision 8.4: mean saturation 0.12-0.22 and luma 0.60-0.62 against 0.26-0.42 and 0.32-0.34 through a 2D canvas; visibly washed out). So a frame tagged HLG, PQ or BT.2020 (`render/gpu/hdr.ts`) is drawn into a color-managed 2D canvas at its upload size and that canvas is uploaded: the browser tone maps it to SDR as a <video> element shows it. Proxies, thumbnails and posters were drawn through 2D canvases already, and the export draws through its worker's canvas, so every path shows the same picture. (Batch 47)
- Corrupt imports (Batch 47, acceptance "imports as failed with a clear badge"): a file of an accepted type that cannot be read (a damaged MP4, no track, a failed copy or link) becomes a failed import: a row in the Media tab with a red "Failed" badge, the file name and the reason until it is dismissed (`media.dismissFailedImport`). It is session state of the project, not a media record: §5.2's `MediaItem` stays verbatim, nothing can use the file and it is not copied into media/. The refusal toast stays. A damaged MP4's reason is "Not a readable MP4/MOV file: it is damaged or is not a video" (the parser's message goes to the console only). (Batch 47)
- Worker crashes (Batch 47): any uncaught error in a worker still counts as a crash (its requests reject with `WorkerCrashError`, the next request starts a new worker). The decode worker also has a watchdog: while its requests wait and it has been silent for 400 ms it is pinged, and with no answer 800 ms later it is treated as crashed (a worker closed from DevTools or killed by the browser fires no event). After a crash frame requests, prefetch windows, opens and audio segments ask the new worker once (no media is marked failed for it), the preview asks again 500 ms later after a second crash, a proxy job runs once more and a thumbnail sheet is asked for once more. A decode worker paused in a debugger is restarted too: `__editor.workers.watchdogEnabled = false` in dev builds. (Batch 47)
- Error boundaries (Batch 47): each workspace panel has a React error boundary; a canvas view that fails 3 renders in a row (`FrameScheduler.onViewFailure`, one bad frame is only logged) puts its panel in the same error state; `panel.reload` (the fallback's button, the palette) remounts the panel (or every failed one). An error outside the panels, or a startup that throws, shows the fatal screen with Reload (saves first). (Batch 47)
- Export robustness (Batch 47): the export's GPU device is not replaced when lost (`GpuDevice` option `recover: false`): the job fails with "The GPU was reset during the export (device lost). Export again." whatever step meets the loss first, as replacing it mid-export would skip the old device's textures without a word. A video whose decoder refuses it partway through an export becomes offline there and the frame is drawn again with its slate, as the preview shows it (before: the export failed). (Batch 47)
- Long non-MP4 audio (Batch 47, the Batch 10 follow-up): MP3, AAC, WAV and Ogg files are still decoded whole; one longer than 45 minutes (about 1 GB of stereo float; its duration read from the file's metadata by an <audio> element before any decode) is refused at import as a failed import with the reason, rather than risking the tab's memory. Segmented decoding moved to Batch 50. (Batch 47)
- Dev assertion (Batch 47, "open VideoFrames are zero after idle"): dev builds look every second; after 3 s with no frame requests and nothing playing, scrubbing, trimming or exporting, any VideoFrame still open (the main thread's, the decode worker's rings, which a session gives back after 1 s without requests) is a console error. The 100-cycle check is a dev benchmark (`dev.benchProjectCycles`, `__editor.perf.bench.cycles(n)`), run by a CDP script. (Batch 47)

- WebGL2 renderer (Batch 48):
  - §1.4 is amended as the batch asks: the GPU requirement is WebGPU or WebGL2. WebGL2 counts only when it runs on the GPU (`failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat`): software rendering is still "no degraded mode". The backend is chosen once at startup: a WebGPU adapter first, else WebGL2.
  - The URL flag (`?renderer=webgl2`: WebGL2 first; `?renderer=webgpu`: WebGPU only) works in every build: it is harmless, and it lets a user whose WebGPU driver misbehaves use WebGL2.
  - WebGL2's context lives on its own OffscreenCanvas and presents the preview through `bitmaprenderer` (`transferToImageBitmap`): textures cannot be shared across contexts, and the preview canvas is remounted with its panel. The export worker's context lives on its frame canvas, because Chrome 155 makes no VideoFrame from a `bitmaprenderer` canvas or from a WebGL canvas's ImageBitmap.
  - WebGL2 textures are capped at 8192 px (WebGPU's default limit), so both backends upload the same sizes. Video-frame textures take each frame with `texImage2D` (mutable storage), because `texSubImage2D` into immutable storage held the decoder's buffers longer.
  - 4K at Full quality without a proxy drops 0-18 of ~157 frames on WebGL2 against 1-2 on WebGPU: WebGL has no external textures, so the whole frame is copied before it is scaled. Auto quality (proxies) plays the same on both. (measured, accepted)
  - The preview renders nothing while its renderer is not ready (a lost device), so renders failing during a restore cannot trip the panel error state. (Batch 48)

- WebM sources (Batch 49):
  - Own EBML demuxer (`media/demux/ebml.ts`, `webm.ts`, `webmCodecs.ts`; no dependency). The container is told by the file's first bytes, so a WebM named `.mp4` also opens. `.mkv` stays refused by name (§9.1 lists `.webm`).
  - The sample index comes from a scan of every Cluster, at the probe and at the first open, then from cache/index/ (same format), not from Cues (key frames only, absent from live recordings). 10 minutes, 183 MB: 0.44-0.47 s per scan.
  - Audio, against the batch's "decodeAudioData continues to handle audio": Opus decodes in decode.worker from the demuxed packets, like MP4 audio since Batch 10. decodeAudioData holds a whole recording as PCM, and its output starts at the first audio block, so the audio of a Chrome screen recording would play 33-36 ms early. Vorbis, laced audio and Opus without a WebCodecs decoder keep decodeAudioData, padded or cut by the lead the worker reports.
  - VP8 and H.264 in WebM are accepted besides VP9 and AV1 (Chrome's MediaRecorder writes them). Rotation is 0, VP9 alpha decodes opaque, and a recording whose size changes midway is laid out at its first size.
  - Frame rates from jittery tick times (WebM's milliseconds: 30 fps as 33 / 34 ms) snap within half a tick, for every container; fine MP4 timescales are unaffected.

- Release (Batch 50):
  - The last `TODO(batch 53)` comment (the per-cue caption style hook in `Compositor.writeCaption`, Batch 32) is gone although Batch 53 is still planned: acceptance 2 asks for none in `src/` at v1. The hook and its context are in `docs/BACKLOG.md` (Batch 53), and the code keeps a plain comment pointing there.
  - In-app help is a Settings > About tab, not a new app bar button (the §17 inventory stays as listed): the version, the renderer in use, Keyboard shortcuts and Command palette buttons, and View licenses. `app.about` ("About Shorts Editor") opens it from the palette.
  - The build writes `dist/licenses.txt` (the licenses of every package in the main and worker bundles, and the OFL texts of the bundled fonts) with a small build plugin (`scripts/licenses.ts`), because Vite's own `build.license` lists the main bundle only and most packages are in workers. No new dependency.
  - Vite's chunk-size warning is a budget, `build.chunkSizeWarningLimit` 1600 kB (main chunk 1300 kB), so the release build prints no warning; the chunk is not split (Batch 45; P12 on this build: start screen interactive at a median 48 ms warm).
  - Fades fit the clip as a pair after trims, speed changes and frame rate conversions (`fitFades`, `core/document/fades.ts`): when the two together are longer than the clip, both shrink in proportion to fill it. Before, each was clamped on its own and they could overlap (the fade handles already kept the pair). The validator still checks each fade alone, so documents saved earlier open unchanged.
  - The frame rate conversion report counts a media clip whose source range is re-fitted (off the new rate's grid: clips pasted from projects at other rates) as `rounded`, so that conversion is no longer called lossless. A freeze frame's `out` (one frame after its held time) is not counted: the picture shows `in` only.
  - WebM files whose sound is decoded whole (Vorbis, laced blocks) are refused past 45 minutes at the probe, with the reason, like MP3/AAC/WAV/Ogg since Batch 47.
  - Hosting: no COOP/COEP (the Batch 33/45 hosting decision). Nothing needs cross-origin isolation, and COEP `require-corp` would require CORP headers on the Whisper model downloads (README, Production build and hosting).
- Font library (Batch 51, spec §20.1):
  - Size: 330 families (spec "at least 200, target about 300"), 32.2 MB with licenses and catalog (cap 40 MB). 377 were curated and fit (34.6 MB); 47 lookalikes were dropped to stay near the target.
  - The eight Batch 28 fonts moved from `src/render/text/fonts/` (Vite-hashed assets) into the library (`public/fonts/library/<slug>/`, byte-identical files, under the app's base URL); they are still added to the font set at start (`CORE_FONTS`), so new text and old projects draw before the catalog is read.
  - Font records are `fonts/fonts.json` entries (manifest version 2: `source` library / user / system, a variable file's `weightRange`, a subset's `unicodeRange`, `origin`), with a migration from version 1 (system faces). `project.json` is unchanged, so its schema version stays.
  - The catalog loads on the first font browser open (and Settings > About), and also in idle time when the open document names a family no other source knows (a project whose library fonts have no copy in `fonts/`, e.g. read-only). Never at app start.
  - Font browser rows decode their files in idle time and add them to the document's font set in batches, at most every 100 ms: each face added restyles the whole page (6-14 ms measured with the editor open), which held a steady scroll at 30 fps. Faces that text needs are added at once. A file fetched for a row that scrolled away is dropped without being decoded.
  - A pick without a weight chip sets the family and the family's weight nearest to the text's (so the Weight field shows what draws); with a weight chip, the chip's weight (spec: "sets the family and that weight").
  - My fonts: `.ttc` collections are refused (spec lists TTF, OTF, WOFF, WOFF2). WOFF2 names come from the file name, as the spec says. A family renamed in My fonts keeps its old name in the texts that use it (their projects keep drawing it from their copies). A My fonts family named like a library family counts as the library's.
  - `licenses.txt` lists each library family with its designer and copyright line and points to its full text (`fonts/library/LICENSES/<slug>.txt`, shipped in `dist/`), then gives each license's full text once (226 kB instead of about 1.5 MB). Packages inlined in another package's prebuilt file are named in `INLINED` (transformers.js: @huggingface/tokenizers, @huggingface/jinja; the ONNX Runtime bundle holds only its own code and onnxruntime-common).
  - The text measurer's font metrics cache is dropped with the layouts (`TextMeasurer.reset`): metrics measured while a font was still loading were the fallback's for the rest of the session (a Batch 28 bug that on-demand library fonts made common: Pacifico drew 8 px higher in the preview than in the export).

- [from Batch 06 -> Batch 09] Uploads cost decoder throughput: `copyExternalImageToTexture` from a hardware frame took 1080p H.264 from 2.9 ms/frame (frames closed) to 7.3 (one reused texture) and 8.5-11.5 (a new texture per frame), and 4K HEVC from 11 to 21-29 ms/frame (headless Chrome 155, RDNA2). Use `frameService.prefetch` windows rather than one request per frame (a request round trip costs 15-30 ms per frame). Hardware decoders stall when the app holds many of their frames (20 held frames hung one); the session's stall fallback frees its ring, but keep windows small. (done in Batch 09: spare frame textures are recycled, frames are scaled to the project size on upload, playback uses 2-frame prefetch chunks, windows take their frames out of the ring and idle sessions free their ring after 1 s)

## Dependencies
Why each dependency exists (Batch rule 8).
- `react`, `react-dom` 18.3.1: UI chrome (spec §3.1). (Batch 01)
- `lucide-react`: icon set named by the design system. (Batch 01)
- `vite`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`, `typescript`: dev/build (spec §3.1). (Batch 01)
- `vitest`, `jsdom`: unit tests; jsdom for the DOM-dependent core tests (keyboard dispatcher, focus scopes, theme bridge). (Batch 01)
- `eslint`, `typescript-eslint`, `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`: `npm run lint`, including the color-literal rule of §3.7. (Batch 01)
- `@types/react`, `@types/react-dom`, `@types/node`: typings. (Batch 01)
- `immer` 11: `produceWithPatches`/`applyPatches` for commands and undo (spec §3.3 names it). (Batch 02)
- `idb-keyval` 6: IndexedDB for recent-project directory handles and global settings (spec §3.1 names it). (Batch 03)
- `mp4box` 2.4.1: MP4/MOV demux (spec §3.1 names mp4box.js). Imported only by `decode.worker` (190.6 kB worker chunk; the main bundle does not contain it). (Batch 04) Since Batch 17 also by `analysis.worker`, which opens its own video sessions for the thumbnail sheets (205.83 kB chunk, was 3.88 kB).
- `@webgpu/types` 0.1.74 (dev): TypeScript declarations of the WebGPU API (`GPUDevice`, `GPUTexture`...), which `lib.dom` does not ship. Types only, nothing bundled. (Batch 05)
- `mp4-muxer` 5.2.2: the proxy's MP4 (spec §3.1 names mp4-muxer) and, since Batch 43, the export's (moov reserved at the front, streamed; only in export.worker's chunk). Streams its bytes (`StreamTarget`, chunked, no fast start) from `proxy.worker` only (226.31 kB worker chunk with mp4box; the main bundle does not contain it). Upstream marks it superseded by Mediabunny; it is kept because the spec names it. (Batch 24)
- Bundled content fonts (Batch 28): not an npm dependency. 34 woff2 files (Inter, Montserrat, Nunito, Oswald, Unbounded, Playfair Display, Caveat, JetBrains Mono; latin and latin-ext, `wght` variable, 1.4 MB) copied with their SIL OFL licenses from the Fontsource 5.3.0 packages (`npm pack`) into `src/render/text/fonts/`; spec §3.1 asks for "a curated bundled set (variable fonts, open licenses)". Built as hashed assets, loaded only when a text uses them. Since Batch 51 they are part of the font library (below).
- Font library (Batch 51): not an npm dependency. 330 Google Fonts families (1406 woff2 files, latin and latin-ext; 116 variable, 214 static) with their license texts in `public/fonts/library/`, downloaded from Fontsource by `scripts/fonts/fetch-library.mjs` (Node 22 `fetch`, no package) from `scripts/fonts/families.json`; SIL OFL 1.1 (316), Apache 2.0 (13), Ubuntu Font Licence (1). 32.2 MB, committed so builds need no network.
- `@huggingface/transformers` 4.3.1: local Whisper transcription (spec §10.6 names it), with `onnxruntime-web` (its WebGPU / WASM runtime). (1) Batch numbers are read in base 10, because PROGRESS.md stores "01", which bash would treat as octal (so "08" and "09" would fail). (2) Completion is compared as a number, because "02" != "2" as strings, which would stop the run after the first batch. (3) A run that only applied review fixes is detected by a `batch-NN: fixes` HEAD commit, not by grepping the whole file for `fix-attempt: done`, because that grep matches any earlier batch and would skip the retry and could loop forever.

  1. `src/ui/TextField.tsx:31-43` (commit mode): Enter calls `commit()` and then `blur()`. The `onBlur` handler (line 59) belongs to the same render and still sees the typed `draft`, so it commits a second time. Escape calls `setDraft(null)` and then `blur()`, so the same stale `onBlur` commits the typed text instead of reverting it. That breaks the component's own contract (lines 5-6) and spec §11 ("Esc reverts"). A jsdom probe confirmed it: type "typed", Enter -> `onCommit` called twice; Escape -> `onCommit("typed")` once. Effects in this batch: in the Project section, Escape in Name (`src/panels/properties/ProjectSection.tsx:70`) or Background (`:89`) renames the project or changes the color instead of reverting. Enter in Background dispatches `setBackground` twice, and each call assigns a new object (`src/core/commands/projectCommands.ts:77`), so one edit leaves two undo steps. Fix: use a ref to commit at most once and to cancel on Escape, as `ProjectName` already does (`src/app/AppBar.tsx:64,74-79,91-95`). Add a regression test (jsdom + `createElement` in a `.test.ts`).

Enter calls `onChange` twice. Fix it the same way as item 1.

Mod+O on the folder that is already open, before the pending autosave has run (likely with the 10 s autosave delay), loads the stale project.json into the editor. The flush writes the newer document, but the editor still shows the stale one, and the next edit's autosave overwrites the newer file (it survives only in history/). Fix: flush the current session (`await current?.flush()`) before `openProjectFolder` in `openDir`.

### Batch 04: Media import, probe, media panel basics, worker infrastructure
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-14
- notes:
  - Workers (§3.5): `media/workers/protocol.ts` (methods `probe`, `poster`, `decodeImage`; request ids; priorities user/playback/prefetch/background; a `cancel` message; errors as name + message; transferables collected from results), `WorkerHost` (worker side: priority queue then arrival order, concurrency 2, an AbortController per request; a cancelled request always answers AbortError and its late result is closed), `WorkerPool` (main side: one worker per kind, created on the first request; abort -> cancel message + immediate AbortError; a crashed worker rejects its requests and is recreated next time), `decode.worker.ts`. Vite builds workers as ES modules.
  - Bytes (§9.2): `ByteSource` (Blob range reads through `slice().arrayBuffer()`, 4 MB chunks, in-flight reads shared, fresh copies returned) over a `ChunkCache` byte-LRU of 64 MB shared by every source of the worker.
  - Probe (§9.1): `mp4Probe.ts` feeds mp4box with 1 MB ranged reads and jumps where mp4box asks, so moov-at-end files never read their mdat. It gives codec strings, the avcC/hvcC/av1C/vpcC description, coded size, rotation from the tkhd matrix (`rotation.ts`), durations from the sample tables through the new `time.ts` `ticksToUs`, fps from the first 120 cts deltas (`fps.ts`: the mode, averaged over its cluster, snapped to the nearest standard rate within 0.03%, else timescale/mode), and the audio codec/channels/rate. `imageProbe.ts` (worker): ImageDecoder for GIF/WebP animations, else createImageBitmap. Main thread: `audioProbe.ts` (`decodeAudioData` on an OfflineAudioContext, for mp3/aac/wav/ogg) and `svgProbe.ts` (size from width/height or the viewBox; poster through a sized canvas). `testMp4.ts` is a test-only MP4 writer (there is no ffmpeg on this machine), used by the unit tests and to wrap real WebCodecs output in the browser checks.
  - Posters: `decode/poster.ts` (worker) decodes the first sync sample with a one-shot VideoDecoder, draws it upright into an OffscreenCanvas (320 px long side) and returns a transferred ImageBitmap plus a WebP blob. `media/PosterStore.ts` follows the document: new media (import, open, undo) get a poster from `cache/thumbs/<id>.poster.webp` (decoded in the worker), or one regenerated and written back (not when read-only); removed media have their bitmap closed; cards observe one id, and (since the review fixes) `PosterPainter` draws them in the FrameScheduler loop.
  - Import: `media/mediaKinds.ts` (the 14 §9.1 extensions, a MIME fallback for pasted images; WebM refused), `project/mediaFiles.ts` (safe, case-insensitive unique names; `copyIntoMedia` streamed with progress and cleaned up on failure; project-relative `resolveFile`/`writeFileAt`/`removeFileAt`), `FsDir.getFile`/`FsDir.writeFile` (`blob.stream()` piped into the writable through a byte counter), `media/MediaImporter.ts` (classify -> refuse -> probe 3 at a time -> copy one at a time -> one `media.add`; imports are serialized; an aborted import removes its copies and adds nothing). Document: `core/commands/mediaCommands.ts` (`media.add`, `media.remove`, `media.rename`, `mediaUseCounts`); `validate.ts` checks MediaItems (integer us and sizes, quarter-turn rotation, positive rational fps, relPath inside the project).

- review: rejected
  1. `src/panels/media/PosterCanvas.tsx:14-25`: each card draws its poster into its visible `<canvas>` directly from the `PosterStore.observe` callback (`drawImage` at line 24), outside the `FrameScheduler`. Spec §3.4 (BINDING) allows nothing to render outside the scheduler loop except React chrome, and `src/core/scheduler/FrameScheduler.ts:1-2` says "Nothing else draws canvases". The Batch 04 notes describe the direct draw ("cards observe one id and draw into their own canvas") but log no deviation. This also matters for later batches: Batch 17 moves cards to sprite sheets and Batch 20 adds hover scrub, which redraws these canvases on every pointer move, and both would build on this pattern. Fix: the observer only marks the card dirty, and a `RenderView` registered with `scheduler` (a new `InvalidationFlag`, e.g. `mediaThumbs`) draws the dirty cards, so a burst of poster arrivals is drawn at most once per frame. Or, if direct drawing is intended, write the deviation and its reason here.
  2. `src/media/workers/WorkerPool.ts:83-85`: when a `result` arrives for an id that is no longer pending (aborted and already rejected by `onAbort`), it is dropped without closing its transferables. The worker closes late results only when the `cancel` message arrives before the handler finishes (`src/media/workers/WorkerHost.ts:166-168`). If the worker has already posted the result, the transferred `ImageBitmap` reaches the main thread and is never closed, which breaks P13 ("Memory of closed resources is explicit"). This can happen today when a project closes while posters are loading (`PosterStore.dispose` -> `controller.abort()`, `src/media/PosterStore.ts:90`). From Batch 06 on, the same path leaks `VideoFrame`s when scrubs cancel frame requests, and unclosed frames stall the decoder. Fix: in `receive`, when there is no pending entry and `message.type === "result"`, call `close()` on every item of `transferablesOf(message.value)` that has one. Add a `WorkerPool.test.ts` case that aborts after the host has posted the result and asserts the value's `close` was called.
  3. `src/media/mediaKinds.ts:46`: `BY_EXTENSION[ext]` is a lookup on a plain object literal, so extensions that name `Object.prototype` members are accepted: `classifyFile("clip.constructor", "")` returns the `Object` function and `classifyFile("clip.__proto__", "")` returns `Object.prototype` instead of null (confirmed with a temporary Vitest probe). Such a file is not refused. `createProbeFile`'s switch (`src/media/MediaImporter.ts:25`) matches no case and returns `undefined`. The importer then copies the file, `mediaItemFrom(undefined, ...)` (line 179) throws a TypeError, and the whole import is rolled back. The user sees "Import failed / Cannot read properties of undefined" instead of a toast that names the file, and the valid files picked or dropped with it are not imported (Acceptance 3). Fix: `Object.hasOwn(BY_EXTENSION, ext)` (or a `Map`), plus a `mediaKinds.test.ts` case for `.constructor` and `.__proto__`.

### Batch 05: WebGPU renderer foundation
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-14
- notes:
  - Built across two runs: the first run left `render/gpu` and `mat3`/`drawList` uncommitted (they typechecked and their tests passed); the second run checked them and built the rest.
  - `render/gpu`:
    - `GpuDevice`: one GPUDevice for the app. On loss (including `device.destroy()`) it asks for a new adapter and device at once, then retries after 50/200/500/1000/2000 ms. It reports `generation`, `restores` and `lastRecoveryMs`.
    - `Renderer` interface (`draw(list, target, viewport?)`, `createTexture`, `uploadVideoFrame` (closes the frame), `uploadImageBitmap`, `resize`, canvas/offscreen targets, `readBitmap`, `subscribe` "lost"/"ready").
    - `WebGpuRenderer`: three WGSL pipelines (textured quad with per-layer matrix, opacity, crop UV rect and flips; two-texture dissolve for Batch 36; solid color) with premultiplied alpha blending. One uniform buffer at 256-byte dynamic offsets, a bind group per texture made at upload (none per frame), mip chains rendered level by level (`mipmaps.ts`), a scissor to the frame, the border drawn outside it, and readback with padded rows and un-premultiply (`readback.ts`). Uploads use `copyExternalImageToTexture`. Matrices are 3x3 affine in project px (`render/mat3.ts`); a view uniform maps them to clip space.
  - `media/cache/TexturePool.ts`: a byte-budget LRU keyed `(mediaId, lod, timeUs)`, with `imageKey(mediaId)` for static mipmapped images. Counted pins, `setBudget`, `delete`/`deleteMedia`/`clear`, stats and a change listener. Every texture leaving the pool is destroyed (P13). The default budget is 768 MB (P6). The pool is emptied on device loss.
  - `render/preview/`:
    - `viewport.ts`: Fit letterbox with the margin, edges on whole device px; numeric zoom centered; contain fit; device size.
    - `PreviewView`: the WebGPU canvas at devicePixelRatio. It follows the layout store (preview panel size), session zoom, document `settings`, Theme and DPR (matchMedia), and the renderer's "ready". It renders only on the scheduler's `preview` flag and resizes the backing store inside `render`. `renderFrame()` draws to an offscreen target at project size and reads it back.
    - `PreviewStatsOverlay`: the dev text, written in the scheduler loop.
