### Batch 06: Video decode engine and frame delivery
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-14
- notes:
  - Protocol (§3.5): `media/workers/protocol.ts` gains a `progress` message (one request can post several frames before its result), the frame priorities `scrub > playback > idle`, and the methods `openVideo`, `requestFrame`, `prefetch`, `closeVideo` and `decodeStats`. `WorkerHost` handlers get an `emit`; a progress value posted after a cancel is closed in the worker. Frame methods are "immediate": they start at once instead of waiting for the two queued slots, because each session orders its own jobs. `WorkerPool.request` takes `onProgress`, and progress that nobody takes is closed.
  - Sample index (§9.2, §9.1): `media/demux/sampleIndex.ts` holds the track in typed arrays: offsets, sizes, dts, cts, durations and sync flags in decode order. Its lookups are display order (by cts), `frameAt`/`positionAt` (binary search), `keyFor` and `feedUntil`. `keyFor` gives the sync sample to start from, one GOP earlier for a leading picture of an open GOP. `feedUntil` is the last decode index the decoder needs to show a frame (B-frames). `sampleIndexFile.ts` stores it in `cache/index/<mediaId>.bin`: magic, version, the source's size and lastModified, codec, description, size and rotation, then the 8-byte-aligned arrays. A mismatched or damaged file reads as null, and the index is rebuilt.
  - `media/decode/VideoDecodeSession.ts` (worker), one per video and lod:
    - Jobs run one at a time, by priority; a prefetch yields to a frame request.
    - A seek feeds the keyframe straight into the configured decoder (see Global deviations). Chunks go in dts order, outputs are matched by cts timestamp, and frames before the target are not delivered.
    - Sequential requests continue without a seek. A frame request feeds only up to `feedUntil` of its target; a prefetch feeds ahead through its range.
    - Backpressure: at most 8 chunks in flight and `decodeQueueSize` below 4.
    - An 8-frame ring serves backward steps, and callers get clones. The end of the track flushes.
    - A decoder that holds frames longer than the content needs (no output for 100 ms while idle) gets one more chunk each time, remembered for the session, and its ring is freed.
    - Leading pictures decoded without their previous GOP are dropped.
    - A decoder that fails before the session ever produced a frame marks the video undecodable (`UnsupportedCodecError`).
    - Scrubs: the keyframe first when the target is 4 or more frames past it, then the newest decoded frame at most every 33 ms across scrubs, once a scrub has waited 16 ms. A fast drag supersedes every request before it completes, so these are what move on screen.
    - `createVideoDecoder` wraps WebCodecs behind `DecoderLike`; `testDecoder.ts` is the test fake.
  - `media/decode/DecodeSessions.ts` (worker registry):
    - `open` loads the cached index or builds it (handing the bytes back for caching) and checks `VideoDecoder.isConfigSupported`. It answers frame times (display order, us), codec, coded size, rotation, `decodable` and `indexFromCache`.
    - `requestFrame` / `prefetch` map times to frames; `close`; stats.
    - A decoder closes after 10 s without requests, and at most 6 are live (LRU among idle ones). The index stays, so a later request only creates a decoder.
    - Wired into `decode.worker.ts`.
  - `media/decode/FrameService.ts` (main thread), `getFrame(mediaId, timeUs, { lod, priority, signal, onApproximate })`:
    - The time snaps to the frame shown at it, and a pool hit answers without the worker. Otherwise the worker's frame is uploaded and closed at once (P5, P13) and put in the `TexturePool` under `(mediaId, lod, frameTimeUs)`. A cached texture is never replaced, because it may be on screen.
    - Stand-ins: the nearest cached frame (new `TexturePool.nearest`) is shown synchronously, inside the call, then any closer frame from the worker.
    - A scrub supersedes the previous scrub of the same media and cancels its prefetches.
    - At most 4 requests per media at the worker; the rest wait, most urgent first.
    - A worker that lost its sessions is reopened once.
    - `prefetch`, `release(mediaId)`, and `attach(source)` per project (file, read and write of `cache/index/`; read-only projects skip the write).
    - Stats: approximate and exact latency (last, p95 of 64), requests, pool hits, superseded, failed, frames received, open frames.
  - `WebGpuRenderer`: a failed external copy destroys its new texture (Batch 05 follow-up). `uploadVideoFrame` also submits the queue at once, so the decoder gets its picture buffer back sooner (measured 25-35% faster decoding while uploading).
  - Preview:
    - `VideoHarness` (temporary) follows the Media panel selection and opens the video. A native range over the frame positions asks `getFrame` with scrub priority on each input and draws stand-ins, then the exact frame, upright through `rotatedContainTransform` (§9.3: rotation in the layer transform). It pins the shown frame and redraws after a device loss.
    - The bar, readout and status are DOM written by the harness, so React mounts `ScrubBar` once.
    - Unsupported codecs show "Can't decode HEVC (hvc1…) in this browser" and disable the bar.
    - `ImageHarness` and `VideoHarness` share `pickPreviewMedia`, and each clears only its own layers (`PreviewView.clearLayers`).
    - The dev stats overlay adds two lines of decode stats (worker counters polled every 500 ms while shown) and the open VideoFrames on each side.
    - `app/previewController.ts` owns `frameService` and `videoHarness`; media leaving the project release their sessions and textures.
  - Also: `codecLabel` moved to `media/mediaKinds.ts`; `sampleIndexPath`/`INDEX_DIR` in `project/mediaFiles.ts`; the `media/demux/index.ts` placeholder removed; the `TODO(batch 06)` comments retired.
  - Measured:
    - 447 unit tests in 59 files (+55 tests, +4 files), plus the perf project.
    - Build: 323.10 kB JS (106.36 kB gzip, +12.9 / +4.0 kB), 34.64 kB CSS, decode.worker 204.53 kB (+14.0 kB).
  - Headless Chrome 155 (CDP, AMD RDNA2, dev server, OPFS project), test media and results:
    - Media were made in the page with WebCodecs and wrapped by `testMp4.ts`, each frame showing its index as 12 black/white stripes, read back through `renderFrame()`:
      - `uhd60.mp4`: HEVC 3840×2160 at 60 fps timestamps, 360 frames, a keyframe every 60, 63.4 MB ≈ 84 Mbps.
      - `fhd60.mp4`: H.264 1920×1080 60 fps, 360 frames, 1 s GOPs, 24.2 MB.
      - `portrait.mov`: HEVC 1920×1080 30 fps with the rotation-90 matrix.
    - Acceptance 1, 40 random jumps per video. Wrong frames: 0/80. A frame was drawn in the first animation frame in 38/40 per video; the misses are the first scrub of a just-opened video, which waits for its keyframe.

      | Exact latency | 1080p H.264 | 4K HEVC |

      | Median | 38 ms | 181 ms |

- deviations:
  - The sample index from the moov tables, and seeks with no flush or reset: see Global deviations.
  - Acceptance 1 is met only near a keyframe. Exact frames within 80 ms (1080p) / 120 ms (4K) hold for forward drags, ring and pool hits, and targets up to ~25 (1080p) / ~10 (4K) frames past a keyframe; the medians are 38 ms and 181 ms. Deeper in a 1 s GOP the time is the hardware decode rate times the distance (about 10 ms per 4K frame here). Stand-ins (the nearest cached frame within the same call, the keyframe, then the newest decoded frame) keep the picture moving meanwhile. Proxies (Batch 24, P8's "50 ms on proxy") are the spec's answer; follow-up added.
  - Progressive delivery goes beyond "keyframe first, then exact": the nearest cached frame is shown at once (P8 wording), and a scrub waiting longer than 16 ms also gets the newest decoded frame, every 33 ms at most.
  - Class cancellation is done in `FrameService` (superseded scrub, prefetches of the scrubbed media) with the per-request cancel messages, not with a group cancel in `WorkerHost`/`WorkerPool`.
  - Frame methods skip the worker's two-slot queue ("immediate"); each session orders its jobs by priority.
  - At most 6 live decoders (the spec gives no number), and the decoder idle close is 10 s (P13).
  - A decoder that fails before any frame came out marks the video undecodable, because `isConfigSupported` alone missed real refusals. The error badge is in the preview's dev bar, not on media cards.
  - A frame request feeds only what its target needs; the spec's "at most 8 in flight" and `decodeQueueSize` limits apply on top.
  - `uploadVideoFrame` submits an empty command list after the copy (see notes).
  - `lod: "proxy"` is accepted end to end, but there are no proxy files yet (the frame source returns null).
  - The dev scrub bar shows in production builds too, like the Batch 05 image harness: it is the only way to see video before Batch 08.

- review: rejected
  1. `src/media/decode/VideoDecodeSession.ts:143` and `:350-356`: false stalls, and their effect never wears off.
     - The stall check is `now - lastProgressAt >= STALL_MS`. Only `output` sets `lastProgressAt` (line 452). It starts at 0, and `seek()` and `feed()` never reset it when the decoder gets new work.
     - Scrub jobs always wait in 16 ms slices (`APPROXIMATE_WAIT_MS`, line 350), because `DecodeSessions.requestFrame` always passes an approximate callback.
     - So a scrub that comes more than 100 ms after the session's last output counts a stall as soon as the decoder spends 16 ms on a frame with an empty queue. That covers the first scrub of a video and any scrub after a pause in a drag. A 4K HEVC keyframe, or the first frame of a new decoder, takes that long.
     - Each false stall frees the backward-step ring (line 355) and adds 1 to `extraInFlight` for the rest of the session (line 354). From then on, `canFeed` (lines 402-403) lets every frame request feed one more chunk past its target and keep one more chunk in flight.
     - Seeks reuse the running decoder without a flush (Global deviations), so the next seek first waits for every extra chunk: about 10 ms per frame at 4K. Exact-frame latency (Acceptance 1) gets worse the longer the editor is used, and the measurements in the notes come from short sessions.
     - Confirmed with a temporary Vitest probe. The probe decoder took chunks at once and gave its first output 17 ms later, with the clock at 5 s. It showed `stalls: 1` after the first scrub and `stalls: 2` after a second scrub 2 s later. A later playback request to frame 200 then fed 2 chunks past its target.
     - Fix: count a stall only after STALL_MS without output since the decoder last got work. Set `lastProgressAt = now()` in `seek()` and after each `decoder.decode()` in `feed()`, or measure from the start of the wait. Add that probe as a test, asserting `stalls: 0` and no chunk fed past the target.
  2. `src/media/decode/VideoDecodeSession.ts:361-363`: `canContinue` can return the wrong frame, marked exact.
     - It checks that the target's start key was fed (`key <= nextFeed`) and that the target is still pending. It does not check that the current run started at or before that key.
     - A leading picture of an open GOP (RASL after a CRA, the `keyFor` case at `src/media/demux/sampleIndex.ts:131-135`) is in flight in a run that started at its own CRA. `canContinue` continues that run instead of seeking from the earlier GOP. `output` then drops the picture as a leading picture (lines 458-464). The loop returns `nearest()` (line 340), which is the CRA or the frame after it, and `src/media/decode/DecodeSessions.ts:113` marks it `approximate: false`.
     - How it happens: in a backward drag across a CRA, one move seeks to the CRA's GOP, and the next move lands on a RASL frame while it is still decoding.
     - Confirmed with a temporary probe on the open-GOP index of `VideoDecodeSession.test.ts`, extended to 12 samples so the track does not end (I0 P2 B1 | CRA4 RASL3 P5 P6...). A scrub to position 5 was aborted, then a scrub to position 3 asked for 100000 us. It got the frame at 133333 us (the CRA), with 1 seek in total.
     - This breaks the batch goal ("frame-accurate") and the contract of `FrameResult.timeUs`, "at or before the requested time" (`src/media/decode/FrameService.ts:37`). The dev bar shows the wrong frame as "exact". x265 encodes open GOPs by default.
     - Fix: in `canContinue`, also require `timeUs >= this.runStartUs` (a leading picture of the current run cannot be reached by continuing), so the request seeks from `keyFor`'s earlier GOP. Add the probe as a test. Also mark a delivered frame whose timestamp is not the target as approximate in `DecodeSessions.requestFrame`; the `nearest()` fallback for frames the decoder drops reaches the same path.

The worker's close then finds nothing, and the open registers its session afterwards (`src/media/decode/DecodeSessions.ts:99-100`). - fix-attempt: done (2026-10-14)
  1. False stalls (`VideoDecodeSession.ts`): `seek()` and every `decoder.decode()` in `feed()` now set `lastProgressAt` too, so a stall counts only after STALL_MS without output since the decoder last got a chunk or gave a frame, with its queue empty. Test "counts no stall while the decoder works on chunks it was just given": a fake decoder that takes chunks at once and outputs each frame 17 ms later (new `latencyMs` option in `testDecoder.ts`), clock at 5 s, scrubs to frames 10 and 50 two seconds apart, then playback to 200. Result: `stalls: 0`, `seeks: 3`, and the last chunk fed is each request's target. On the old code it fails after the first scrub (a chunk fed past frame 10).
  2. Open-GOP leading pictures:
     - `canContinue` also requires `timeUs >= runStartUs`, so a leading picture of the run's own sync sample seeks from `keyFor`'s earlier GOP.
     - That seek leaves the old run's copy of the picture in the decoder, decoded without its references. It comes out first and would land in the ring under the right timestamp, so the fix in `canContinue` alone still returned a broken frame as exact. `seek()` now records the leading pictures still pending in the superseded run (`staleLeading`, timestamp -> copies), and `output` drops their first copy. Flushes, decoder errors and closes clear the record. A decoder that skips such a picture instead costs one later copy of it: that request gets the nearest frame, marked approximate, and the next one seeks again.
     - `DecodeSessions.requestFrame` marks a result whose timestamp is not the target's as `approximate: true` (the `nearest()` fallback). `FrameService` passes it on and records no exact-latency sample for it. The `FrameResult.timeUs` and `DeliveredFrame.approximate` docs say so, and the dev bar shows "nearest N ms" in the approx style instead of "exact".
     - The fake decoder now models open GOPs: with `references` + `decodeOrder`, a leading picture comes out `corrupt` when its reference was not fed in the same unbroken run, and a key chunk first outputs the frames held before it. Test "seeks from the GOP before for a leading picture in flight, and drops the copy decoded without it" is the reviewer's probe (I0 P2 B1 | CRA4 RASL3 P5..P11, a scrub to 5 superseded while CRA4/RASL3/P5 are in the decoder, then a scrub to 3). Result: the frame at 100000 us, not corrupt, 2 seeks. Old code: 133333 us (the CRA) with 1 seek. With only the `canContinue` change: the corrupt copy.
     - Also tested: `DecodeSessions.test.ts` "marks the nearest frame approximate when the decoder cannot produce the one asked for", `FrameService.test.ts` "passes on a frame the decoder could only approximate, with no exact-latency sample".
  3. The observation (an open racing a close), fixed on both sides:
     - Worker: `DecodeSessions.close` marks the opens under way for that media, and they end with an AbortError instead of registering. Replacing an entry inside `open` uses a private `remove`, so it marks no other open. Test "drops a video closed while it opens, and keeps the others".
     - Main thread: the race had a second window. `FrameService.open` reads the file and the cached index before it posts `openVideo`, so a `release` at that point posted `closeVideo` first and the open after it. Each open now has an AbortController that `release` aborts: an open still reading never posts, and one at the worker is cancelled (the signal goes with the request). Test "cancels the open of a media released while it opens".

### Batch 07: Timeline canvas foundation
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-14
- notes:
  - `src/timeline/view/` (framework-free):
    - `geometry.ts`: `TimelineGeometry`. Header column, ruler, track area, rows anchored at the video/audio divider (video and caption tracks stack up from it, audio down; the caption track is always S), the "+ track" rows, `frameToX`/`xToFrame` (§6.2), the visible frame range, a binary-search `rowAt`, and the `scrollY` range.
    - `zoom.ts`: Fit (content + 2 s, at least 1 s), limits (Fit down to 0.01 px/frame, up to 400), `zoomAt` keeping a frame under an x, key zoom anchored at the visible playhead else the center (x1.25 / x0.8), scroll clamps (never before 0, at most 25% of the view past the content end), the logarithmic slider mapping, wheel delta normalization (one notch = one key step, pinch deltas smooth).
    - `ruler.ts`: levels 1/5/10 frames, 1/2/5/10/30 s, 1/5 min (plus 10/30 min and 1 h for long timelines at 0.01 px/frame). Second ticks sit on wall-clock seconds and frame ticks restart each second (29.97 matches the timecodes). Second labels are placed first; frame numbers fill the gaps only where they fit, and whole timecodes appear once the ticks are far enough apart. A label that would touch the previous one is skipped, so labels never overlap. Minor ticks subdivide at >= 8 px.
    - `clipLayout.ts`: device-pixel spans, a 1 px separator when a clip abuts the next, sub-pixel clips 1 device px wide, LOD (< 6 px body color only, < 24 px no icon or name, spec §6.4).

    - `textCache.ts`: label widths measured once per font and string, plus ellipsized names per width, capped at 4096 entries. `glyphs.ts`: lucide path data (Film, AudioLines, Image, Type, Square, Captions, Plus) stroked as `Path2D`.

### Batch 08: Compositor and preview at the playhead
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-14
- notes:
  - `src/render/compositor/Compositor.ts`:
    - `evaluate(doc, frame)` walks the visible video tracks from the bottom up. On each it takes the clip at the frame with a binary search (`clipInIndex`/`lastClipStartingBy`, now exported from `timeline/model/queries.ts`) and skips disabled clips.
    - Video and image clips become `media` layers with: mediaId, still flag, media time (§5.1 `in + framesToSourceUs(frame - start, speed)`, kept inside [in, out)), opacity × fades, the crop as a texture UV rect, and one matrix.
    - The matrix composes, first to last: the crop rectangle in texture space, rotation metadata (the texture stays as coded, §9.3), flips (the content mirrors in place), the display size, then the clip transform (anchor in content fractions, scale/scaleY, rotation in clockwise degrees with exact quarter turns, position from the frame center).
    - Crop fractions cut the shown (upright, flipped) sides. Fades are 0 on the first frame of a fade-in and on the last frame of a fade-out.
    - Rect solids with a flat RGBA fill become `solid` layers. Text, captions, other shapes, keyframes and transitions are `TODO(batch 28/32/34/35/36)`.
    - `neighbors(doc, frame)` lists the edge frames of the clips just before and after the playhead on each track, within 2 s.
    - Layer structs, arrays and scratch matrices are reused between frames, with no closures.
  - `drawList.ts` gains `MediaLayer`, `CompositeLayer` and `Composite`.
  - `DrawListSnapshot` flattens the last drawn list into reused buffers: numbers, plus texture identities and their `valid` flag. A render whose list and viewport are unchanged skips the GPU draw (§9.4).
  - `src/render/preview/LayerTextures.ts` (media layers → pool textures) keeps one slot per track:
    - It snaps to the nearest frame time (`nearestPosition`, new in `sampleIndex.ts`) and draws a pool hit at once.
    - Otherwise it requests the frame through `frameService.getFrame`, with `scrub` priority while the ruler is dragged (`TimelineView.scrubbing`) and `idle` otherwise. Only the first layer of a media gets the scrub request in a pass. A superseded slot request is aborted.
    - It draws the FrameService stand-in (nearest cached frame, then a closer keyframe) in the same pass. With nothing of that media ready, it draws the slot's last layer as it was (texture, matrix, crop, opacity), so cuts never flash black.
    - A request that settles on another frame is drawn and asked again only after the layer wants another frame.
    - It pins what is drawn and calls `onChange` (invalidate `preview`) for late frames.
    - `warm()` prefetches neighbour edge frames that are not cached yet and leaves alone the media being drawn, so a scrub never cancels them.
    - Undecodable or missing media are left out with one warning.
  - `src/media/decode/ImageService.ts`: still images are decoded in decode.worker (SVG on the main thread), uploaded once with mipmaps under `imageKey` and their bitmaps closed. Loads are shared and cancelled when the project detaches.
  - `PreviewView`:
    - Subscribes to the playhead, document affects (`timeline`, `clips`, `tracks`, `media`, `settings`, `composite`), size, zoom, theme, DPR and the device.
    - Each render runs evaluate → resolve → warm → snapshot compare → draw or skip.
    - Stats: draws, skipped, ms and the per-pass layer counts (exact, stand-in, held, missing, pending, warming, failed), shown in the dev GPU stats overlay.
    - `setLayers`/`clearLayers` are gone. Export frame draws the last resolved list.
  - Removed: `ImageHarness.ts`, `VideoHarness.ts`, `pickPreviewMedia`, the dev `ScrubBar` and its CSS, `--danger-wash`, and the harness-only `containTransform`/`rotatedContainTransform` (their rotation cases moved into `Compositor.test.ts`).
  - Insert: `defaultTransform(media, frame)` in `insertMedia.ts` gives Fit through the display size (rotation metadata swaps width and height), anchored at the media center. A video's linked audio clip keeps scale 1.
  - `basicCommands.ts`: `clipPatchAffects`. Transform/opacity/crop-only patches carry the new `composite` flag (Global deviations), and undo carries the same flags.
  - `FrameScheduler` renders the dirty flags in a fixed order (`timelineContent`, `timelineOverlay`, `preview`, `previewOverlay`, ...). That fixes the Batch 05 stats-ordering follow-up.
  - `WebGpuRenderer.draw` allocates nothing on our side once warm (Batch 05 follow-up):

### Batch 09: Playback engine (video)
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-14
- notes:
  - `src/playback/PlaybackEngine.ts` (framework-free; React reads only `playing` through `subscribe`):
    - Clock (§8): `playhead = start + floor((clock - startClock) * speed * fps)` (`playedFrames` in `time.ts`), run from a `FrameScheduler` ticker. One session write per new frame. The timeline overlay, the preview and the timecode readouts follow it; the document never changes.
    - Preroll: starting from pause waits up to 0.5 s (`PREROLL_SECONDS`) until every clip under the playhead has its window decoded (15 frames, or 0.5 s at low frame rates). The clock start is taken half a display frame early, so frame boundaries fall between vsyncs and jitter neither repeats nor skips a frame.
    - Per frame, the preview evaluates the composite with `playback` priority (`PreviewView` `priority()`). `LayerTextures` then requests nothing and uses no stand-in, and a frame not decoded yet holds the track's previous layer.
    - Prefetch windows: every video clip under the playhead keeps up to 15 frames (at most 0.5 s) of its media decoded ahead, at `playback` priority. They come in 2-frame chunks, each asked for as soon as the previous one completes (see deviations). Received frames stay pinned until the playhead passes them.
    - Shuttle speeds deliver only the frames a 60 Hz screen can show (`stride`: the worker decodes the frames between but does not send them). 60 fps media in a 30 fps project deliver every other frame.
    - Backward (J): 15-frame windows ending at the playhead, asked for when half are used. The worker decodes each window forward from the keyframe before it (reverse GOP decoding): more decode work, never a main-thread wait.
    - Lookahead (P7): every 250 ms, the clips starting within 2 s get their first 4 frames at `idle` priority, so their decoder has already sought to the keyframe before the in point. This covers the play direction, plus the start of the timeline when loop wraps. Images about to appear are loaded. decode.worker closes decoders idle for 10 s (`DecodeSessions` IDLE_MS).
    - Dropped frames (1x only) are frames the clock skipped, plus frames whose first preview render lacked the exact frame of a layer (`PreviewView.firstShown`). A clip late on more than 2 frames in a row adds its media to `autoProxy` and logs a note (`TODO(batch 24)`: the proxy switch).
    - Transport:
      - play, pause and toggle;
      - the J/L ladder 1x/2x/4x/8x (`transport.ts` `shuttleSpeed`);
      - K held pauses, and J or L then steps one frame;
      - Shift+K plays around (2 s before to 2 s after the playhead, then back);
      - steps;
      - at the end of the content: stop on the last frame, or wrap when loop is on. Playing from the end restarts at 0.

      A playhead moved by someone else (Home, End, the timecode field) plays on from there. A ruler scrub pauses. The `IdleQueue` is paused while playing (Batch 01 follow-up).
  - `src/audio/AudioClock.ts`: the master clock.
    - The AudioContext (48 kHz, interactive) is created and resumed on the first pointer or key press, through capture listeners installed before the key dispatcher.
    - `now()` reads `getOutputTimestamp()`, carried forward with `performance.now()` between audio callbacks. Without output timestamps it uses `currentTime`, and before the context runs, `performance.now()`.
    - The reading is monotonic: it holds through small steps back and re-bases on large ones.
  - `src/app/playbackController.ts`: the transport actions (Space, J/K/L with hold phases, Shift+K, arrows with hold-to-repeat, Home/End, Mod+Shift+L loop), follow playhead, and the status strip binding. The stepping actions moved here from `timelineController.ts`.
  - Follow playhead (§6.2):
    - `zoom.ts` `pageToFrame` pages by one view width minus 10%, exactly when the playhead's x reaches the right edge of the track area. A frame far outside lands 10% inside the edge it comes in from, and backward pages work too.
    - `TimelineView.follow` pages while following. A horizontal wheel or scroll, or a wheel zoom, stops following until the next play; a vertical wheel does not.
    - `TimelineView.reveal` pages for keyboard jumps (arrows, Home/End, edit points, markers, the timecode field), playing or not (Batch 07 follow-up).
  - Preview chrome (§7.8, §13): the footer is now a bar (readouts left, transport centered, loop and Fit right) over a status strip.
    - Readouts: playhead timecode, duration and the fps badge, written by subscriptions (`bindPreviewReadouts`).
    - Transport: go to start, previous frame, play/pause, next frame, go to end. These are `IconButton`s running the actions; only the play/pause icon re-renders, on play and on pause.
    - Loop toggle (session `loop`).
    - Status strip: the quality chip ("Auto: full"), "Dropped N" for the last playback (reset on play), and "Pool used / budget MB" while the dev GPU stats are on. Its texts are written in the scheduler loop on engine and pool notifications.
  - Decode path:
    - `FrameService.prefetch` takes `priority` (`playback` before `idle`), `stride` and `onFrame`. `frameKeyInto` writes the pool key of a media time into a reused key. `sampleIndex.ts` adds `mediaTimePosition` (media time 0 = the first frame).
    - Frames are uploaded at most at the project's long edge (`uploadSize`). A larger frame is drawn once into a smaller texture from `importExternalTexture` (`SCALE_WGSL`, `fitWithin.ts`). Measured on 4K HEVC: 70 decoded frames/s scaled to 1080p, against 56 copied at 4K.
    - `WebGpuRenderer` keeps up to 4 spare video-frame textures from evicted frames, and uploads into one of the same size instead of creating and destroying textures (Batch 06 follow-up).
    - `VideoDecodeSession`: prefetch windows take their frames out of the ring instead of cloning them (a hardware decoder whose pictures stay referenced has to allocate new ones on the GPU thread). It also gains `stride` and `releaseRing`. `DecodeSessions` releases the ring of a session idle for 1 s (`RING_IDLE_MS`): during playback several decoders stay live for the cuts ahead.
    - Batch 06 re-review follow-up: frames of superseded runs are tracked apart from the current run (`stale`, one leading flag per copy). Before, an old run's output with a timestamp the new run had also fed pruned the new run's pending frames. The new run's leading picture then landed in the ring as valid, and `lastOutputUs` jumped ahead (the frame after the target came back). Test: "keeps the frames of a superseded run apart..."; on the old bookkeeping it returns frame 6 for 5.
  - Batch 08 review follow-ups:
    - `sinCos` writes a scratch struct.
    - `deviceSizeInto`/`frameTransformInto` write reused objects.
    - `LayerTextures` compares and copies keys instead of building `keyId` strings. Only `warm`, which does not run while playing, still builds them.
    - `FLAG_ORDER` is an `as const` array and `InvalidationFlag` is derived from it, so a new flag cannot be left out.
  - `PreviewView`: a new GPU device clears the `LayerTextures` slots. A frame request that failed while the device was being restored ("device not ready") was marked settled and never asked again, so the preview kept a dead layer. This was a race the Batch 08 run did not hit; the regression pass here did.
  - `FrameScheduler.addTicker`: tickers run at the start of each animation frame, before the views, so what they invalidate is drawn in the same frame. A registered ticker keeps the loop running.

- deviations:
  - P6 pinning: the engine pins the frames of its windows ahead of the playhead (up to 15 frames, 0.5 s) until the playhead passes them, and the preview pins what it draws. It does not pin everything within ±1 s. Reason: ±1 s at 60 fps is 120 frames x 8.3 MB (1080x1920) ≈ 1 GB, over the 768 MB budget. Frames just played stay in the LRU as its most recent entries.
  - Frames are uploaded at most at the project's long edge, for scrubbing too (`TODO(batch 21)`: detail-on-zoom above 100%). Reason: the preview never draws more at Fit or 100%, and 4K HEVC decodes at 70 frames/s scaled on upload against 56 when copied at 4K (see Global deviations).
  - Forward windows are 2-frame chunks requested back to back, topping the lead up to 15 frames, instead of one 15-frame window. Reason: decoding a whole window as fast as the hardware can starves Chrome's GPU process, which also composites the page. On 4K60 HEVC, 15-frame windows dropped 12-35% of frames, 2-frame chunks 1.3-4.5% (measured while building this batch).
  - Preroll: starting from pause waits for the clips' windows, up to 0.5 s (the spec names no preroll). Reason: interleaved A/B on 4K60 HEVC: a 3-frame preroll dropped 14-34 frames in the first 60 (1.2-2.9% overall); the full window dropped 7-9 (0.6-1.9%), and the clock started about 25 ms later (~85 ms after the press).
  - Prefetch windows take their frames out of the decoder's ring, and idle sessions give their ring back after 1 s. Reason: hardware decoders reallocate picture buffers while the app holds their pictures (measured 4K60 vsync misses).
  - Dropped frames count at 1x only (shuttle speeds skip frames by design). The count is clock skips plus first renders without the exact frame.
  - Arrows and K+J/K+L pause playback, then step. Home, End and the timecode field during playback play on from the new frame. The end of the content stops on the last frame unless loop is on.

The preview can stay on the wrong frame after a pause. `PlaybackEngine.pause` (`src/playback/PlaybackEngine.ts:238-250`) does not invalidate the preview. `PreviewView` reads its priority only at render time (`src/render/preview/PreviewView.ts:161`, from `src/app/previewController.ts:60`), and it re-renders only on playhead, zoom, document, theme, device and DPR changes (`:106-136`). While playing, `LayerTextures.resolve` holds the track's previous layer when the playhead's frame is not in the pool, and it requests nothing (`src/render/preview/LayerTextures.ts:219-222`). A pause on such a frame (K, Space or the button) leaves the playhead unchanged, so no render at `idle` priority ever runs. The exact frame is never requested, and the preview keeps showing the held layer, while the timecode shows the playhead's frame, until something else invalidates the preview.
     - At shuttle speeds this is the normal case, because windows deliver only every `stride`-th frame and the playhead usually stops between them. JKL is the tool for finding a frame to edit, and the batch goal is frame-accurate playback.
     - Reproduced in headless Chrome 155 (CDP, dev server, OPFS project `b09-a1`, 60 one-second cuts). The script plays at a speed, calls `playbackEngine.pause()` (the K path), waits 1.5 s, then compares the V1 slot's drawn key with `frameKeyInto` of the clip under the playhead. In both, `exact` was 0 of 1 layers and the preview made 0 renders after the pause. 4x (3 stops), -1x (3) and 1x (3) happened to stop on delivered frames.
     - Fix: invalidate `preview` when the engine goes from playing to paused, for example a `playbackEngine.subscribe` listener with a was-playing flag in `previewController.ts`, or a `PreviewView` dependency. The next render then resolves at `idle` priority, draws a stand-in and requests the exact frame.

### Batch 10: Audio decoding, mixing and sync
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-15
- notes:
  - Resumed: the first session wrote every Build item and was cut off at ~01:25 by the Windows Update reboot, before any acceptance check. This session reviewed that code, ran the checks in Chrome and fixed what they found (the stop click, below).
  - Decoded audio (`src/audio/decode/`):
    - `DecodedAudio`: `AudioBuffer`s per media and segment, kept on the main thread in `AudioBufferCache` (512 MB LRU; the entry just stored is never evicted). Released when a media leaves the project, cleared when it closes (P13).
    - MP4/MOV/M4A audio decodes in decode.worker with WebCodecs `AudioDecoder` (`openAudio`/`decodeAudio`/`closeAudio`; `media/decode/audioTrack.ts`, `AudioTracks.ts`). Only the audio samples are read, and any range decodes on its own (2 packets of preroll for the AAC overlap). Media over 10 minutes load in ~60 s segments on demand (`segments.ts`, boundaries on multiples of 1024 frames).
    - Edit lists: `mp4Probe.ts` now reads the edit lists, the esds AudioSpecificConfig and the audio sample table. The AAC priming is skipped, a leading empty edit delays the audio, and media time 0 is the video's first frame (the Batch 08 convention). The decoder's real output rate (HE-AAC doubles it) comes from decoding the first packets.
    - At most 2 channels: quad and 5.1 are mixed down with the Web Audio "speakers" rules, in the worker and for `decodeAudioData` output.
    - Other files (mp3, aac, wav, ogg), and MP4 audio without a WebCodecs decoder, use `decodeAudioData` (OfflineAudioContext, 48 kHz) on the whole file. The import probe's buffer goes straight into the cache (`DecodedAudio.put`), so the file is decoded once (Batch 04 follow-up).
    - Worker PCM is copied into the `AudioBuffer` in slices of 1M frames, yielding between them. The worker's arrays are then transferred on to analysis.worker, with no further copy.
  - Peaks (§9.6):
    - `media/cache/peaks.ts`: level 0 holds Int8 min/max per 256 frames per channel, halved level by level down to one bucket. `cache/peaks/<mediaId>.bin` carries a header stamped with the source's size and lastModified, so a replaced or damaged file reads as null and is rebuilt.
    - `media/workers/analysis.worker.ts` (new): `peaksLevel0` per segment and `peaksFile` (pyramid + file bytes). It never decodes.
    - `media/PeaksJobs.ts`: one job at a time, each started from an idle callback (none while playing). A job reuses a valid file; otherwise it decodes segment by segment through `DecodedAudio` (the buffers stay cached for playback), writes the file, and sets `analysis.peaks` to "ready".
    - "ready" goes through the new `DocumentStore.amend`, a command (`media.analysis`, `setMediaAnalysis`) with no undo step (Batch 04 follow-up). `AnalysisScheduler` hands every audio-bearing media to the jobs; the files of media already "ready" are checked once per session (the cache is disposable).
  - Graph (`src/audio/AudioMixer.ts`, §14):
    - Per voice: source -> envelope GainNode (start/stop ramps) -> clip GainNode (gain dB, mute; `TODO(batch 37)` fades, keyframes) -> track GainNode (mute/solo, `audibleTracks`) -> bus (the master GainNode, stereo) -> monitor GainNode (master volume and mute, monitoring only) -> destination.
    - The bus also feeds a splitter and one `AnalyserNode` per channel (2048 samples, no smoothing). The meters therefore read the mix before the monitor, which is what the export will contain.
    - Every gain change is a 10 ms linear ramp from an explicit start point (`ramp`/`rampTo`; see the click fix below).
  - Scheduler (`src/audio/scheduler/AudioScheduler.ts`, §8):
    - Driven from the engine tick (`sync(mapping)`), in 50 ms steps, starting voices at most 200 ms ahead.
    - The mapping is the engine's anchor, so audio and video read the same clock. Clock readings become context times through the new `AudioClock.contextTime`, `renderLead` and `epoch`.
    - One source per (clip, segment, loop pass); `playbackRate` = the clip speed (0.25x..4x).
    - A clip's start or a segment join starts exactly. Anything else (playback starting mid-clip, a seek, audio decoded late) starts with a 10 ms fade-in, its offset moved on by the delay.
    - Pause, seek, edits and a clock re-base stop voices with a 10 ms ramp. Speeds other than 1x are silent.
    - Edits while playing: mute/solo ramp the track gains, a clip gain or mute change ramps its voice, and a moved, trimmed or removed clip stops and is scheduled again.
    - Loop: the passes after the wrap are scheduled ahead. The engine now wraps at the exact time the end frame would have started (not at the tick that sees it), so those voices are kept.
  - Engine (`PlaybackEngine`):
    - The preroll also waits for the decoded audio under the playhead (up to the 0.5 s preroll).
    - At 1x, the clock starts, and re-anchors after a seek, `lead` = render lead + 20 ms ahead, so the first samples are heard on time.
    - The 250 ms scan loads the audio of clips starting within 2 s. A pause stops the scheduler.
  - Click fix (this session): a stop after a fade-in clicked. `cancelAndHoldAtTime` adds no hold point after a ramp that has ended (Web Audio spec; Chrome does the same). The 10 ms ramp-out therefore ran from the fade-in's end, seconds earlier, and the gain dropped to ~0 at once.
    - Found in the seek recording: Home pressed after a mid-clip seek jumped 0.30 in one sample.
    - `ramp` now sets an explicit start point at the exact current value (the last ramp of each param is kept in a WeakMap). The same bug had made mute/solo instant jumps.
    - `FakeParam` (`audio/testAudio.ts`) now models the Web Audio automation rules. "ramps a voice that faded in out from full level when it stops (no click)" fails on the old code (it renders 0.005 at the stop).
    - Also fixed: the `late` counter counted voices it then skipped.
  - Preview chrome (§7.8):
    - Mute (`audio.toggleMute`, Volume2/VolumeX, pressed when muted) and the master volume `Knob` (new `ui/Knob.tsx`), both before loop and Fit.
    - Knob: drag up/down, 150 px across -60..0 dB (Shift 5x finer); arrows, Page Up/Down, Home/End when focused; double-click resets to 0 dB. While dragged it writes the DOM directly and drives the monitor gain (no React commit), and the value is stored on release.
    - Both live in the app settings (`monitorVolumeDb`, `monitorMuted`).
    - Meter: `MeterView` + `PeakMeter` (pure, tested), a canvas strip along the panel's right edge in a new `PanelFrame` `aside` slot. It redraws through the `meters` flag every frame while audio plays and until the bars and holds settle, then stops.
    - Meter scale -60..+6 dBFS, green up to 0 dBFS and red above. The hold lasts 1.5 s, then falls at 24 dB/s. Each channel has a clip LED that latches on any sample above full scale; a click on the LED row resets it.
  - Track headers (§6.12, minimal): M and S toggles on audio track headers, right-aligned on the first line (`geometry.headerToggles`, hit type `headerToggle`, accent when on, hover wash on the overlay). Each click is one `track.update` command (`updateTrack`, affects `tracks` + `audio`) and one undo step.
  - Dev (`app/audioDev.ts`, dev builds only):
    - `__editor.audio.clapTest({ seconds: 330, interval: 1 })`: a WAV of 10 ms ticks on a new audio track plus a 1-frame white solid on each tick's frame, the first one 1 s in.
    - `.syncReport()`: video minus audio per clap, measured from the analyser on the bus and `getOutputTimestamp`. It is also logged and shown as a toast at each pause.
    - `.toneTest({ gainDb: 6, levelDb: -3 })`; `.scheduler`, `.decoded`, `.meter`, `.mixer`.
  - Measured:
    - 664 unit tests in 85 files (+66 tests, +8 files: AudioScheduler, PeakMeter, AudioBufferCache, DecodedAudio, segments, PeaksJobs, peaks, audioTrack), plus the perf project.
    - Build: 413.31 kB JS (136.09 kB gzip, +27.98 / +9.68 kB), 38.44 kB CSS (+1.74 kB), decode.worker 211.94 kB (+6.02 kB), analysis.worker 3.88 kB (new). The dev tooling is not in the build.
    - Setup: headless Chrome 155 (CDP, dev server, OPFS projects), 48 kHz context: base latency 10.7 ms, output latency 40-48 ms, render lead 46-55 ms. Monitoring was muted, so nothing played aloud. The meters, the clap analyser and the AudioWorklet recorders all tap the bus, before the monitor.
    - Acceptance 1 (`b10-clap`, 30 fps): 330 s, 329 claps 1 s apart, played from 0 once. Offset = video (render time of the flash frame) minus audio (tick onset found sample-exact by a worklet, mapped to its output time by `getOutputTimestamp`).
      - First 10 s: 10.4-14.1 ms. After 5 min (30 claps): 1.4-12.3 ms. All claps: 0.4-17.5 ms, mean 8.7 ms. One frame is 33.3 ms. The dev report agreed within 2 ms.
      - No drift beyond one vsync. One voice for the whole run, no clock re-base, 2 of 9899 frames dropped, 1 React commit (play), none during playback.
      - The offset is positive (video after audio): a frame is drawn at the first vsync after its time (0-16.7 ms). The display's presentation delay comes on top and cannot be measured headless (follow-up).
    - Acceptance 2 (`b10-seek`, a 440 Hz tone at 0.5, the bus recorded sample-exact): three seeks while playing, to 20 s (the timecode-field path), to 0 (a real Home key) and to 10.4 s.

      - The largest sample step around the seeks was 0.0288, the tone's own slope: no click. Before the fix, the Home seek jumped 0.30. WAVs: `%TEMP%/b10/seek-*.wav`.
    - Acceptance 3: two tracks (A1 440 Hz, A2 660 Hz), each track's output recorded. The header toggles were clicked with real pointer events while playing: mute A1, unmute, solo A2, unsolo, solo A1, unsolo.

    - Acceptance 5 (`b10-meter`):

      - 4K60 HEVC (`b09-a2`): 72% and 22% right after the 1080p passes (a hot GPU, as in Batch 09). After a 5 min rest, interleaved, the audio scheduler detached from the engine gave 0.83% and 1.58%, attached 1.17% and 1.08%. Every render had its exact frame: no regression.

- deviations:
  - MP4/MOV audio decodes with WebCodecs `AudioDecoder` in decode.worker, not with `decodeAudioData` on the main thread (§14). Reasons:
    - `decodeAudioData` needs the whole file in memory (a 4K phone video is gigabytes) and cannot decode a range, so "files over 10 min decode in 60 s segments on demand" is impossible with it.
    - It ignores the edit list: phone audio would play up to ~48 ms late (the AAC priming).
    - The worker reads only the audio samples. Other formats still use `decodeAudioData`.
  - Non-MP4 audio (mp3, aac, wav, ogg) over 10 minutes still decodes whole (`decodeAudioData` has no ranges), and files over 1 GB are refused for audio. Follow-up for Batch 45.
  - The scheduler starts one `AudioBufferSourceNode` per clip (per segment and loop pass) at most 200 ms ahead, in 50 ms steps, and lets it play to the clip's end. §8 describes buffer sources in 50 ms chunks. Reasons:
    - Back-to-back chunk sources must join sample-exactly, and every join risks a click (and 20 nodes/s).
    - A source per clip is click-free, and seeks, pauses and edits still stop it with the 10 ms ramp.
    - Nothing starts more than 200 ms ahead (the 400 ms limit of the implementation notes).
    - The per-chunk gain curves of §14 come with fades and keyframes (Batch 37).
  - At 1x the clock starts, and re-anchors after a seek, `lead` ahead: render lead + 20 ms, ~70 ms on this machine. Video and audio then start together and the first samples are not cut. Playback therefore begins ~70 ms later after a press than in Batch 09.
  - "Seeking restarts audio within 50 ms" is measured on the render clock (10.8-11.0 ms here). The device's output latency (46-53 ms in headless Chrome on this machine) delays everything heard equally, the start of play included, and is not the app's to shorten.
  - The peak meter scale (-60..+6 dBFS) and its release (24 dB/s) are not in the spec. The strip is a column right of the preview body, the full height between the panel header and the footer (§7.8: "vertical along the right edge of the preview panel").
  - Master volume and monitoring mute are global app settings (IndexedDB `settings.v1`), not project data: they only concern what is heard (§14).
  - `analysis.peaks` becomes "ready" through `DocumentStore.amend` (no undo step). An undo/redo that brings back a media record also brings back "pending", and the job marks it again (Batch 04 follow-up).
- follow-ups: [from Batch 10 -> Batch 16] video-track mute and the full header toggles; [from Batch 10 -> Batch 17] load the peaks for the waveforms; [from Batch 10 -> Batch 37] clip gain curves per scheduled chunk, audio scrub from the decoded audio; [from Batch 10 -> Batch 38] silence detection in analysis.worker; [from Batch 10 -> Batch 43] the export mixdown on the same graph; [from Batch 10 -> Batch 45] long non-MP4 audio decodes whole, display latency

### Batch 11: Selection and moving clips
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-15
- notes:
  - Selection (§6.7, `core/store/selection.ts` `clickSelection`):
    - Plain click: the clip and its linked partners (Linked selection on). Shift toggles the clip and its partners, Mod toggles the clip alone, Alt selects the clip alone. The clicked clip becomes the primary.
    - A press on a clip that is already selected waits for the release: a drag moves the whole selection, a click without a drag then applies (Batch 07 follow-up). A press on an unselected clip selects at once, so the drag moves the new selection.
    - Clips on locked tracks take no selection (§6.12); a press on one acts as on empty space.
    - Marquee: a drag on empty track space past the 4 px dead zone. It selects every clip it touches (intersect, not contain) on unlocked tracks, with their linked partners; Shift adds. The rectangle is on the overlay and the proposed selection on the content canvas; the session is written once, on release (the Properties panel subscribes to the selection, P1).
    - `selection.selectAll` (Mod+A: clips on unlocked tracks, the primary kept) and `selection.deselect` (Mod+Shift+A), timeline and preview scopes.
    - Undo restores the selection from before the move (the Batch 02 mechanism). Every move is dispatched with the moved clips (or the copies) selected, the dragged clip primary.
  - Pure edit (`timeline/edit/move.ts`, fully unit tested):
    - `moveClips(doc, ids, deltaFrames, trackMap, mode, { duplicate, newTracks, newId })` returns `noop`, `refused` or one `clip.move` command (one undo step) with the placed ids. The delta is clamped at frame 0. A move onto itself is a no-op (no undo entry), in both modes.
    - Overwrite: each stationary clip under a dropped one loses the covered part: trimmed, removed when fully covered, split when covered in the middle (three pieces for two separate covers). Media clips move in/out by the cut frames at their speed.
    - Insert: the moved block (earliest start to latest end) opens a gap at its start on every unlocked track. Clips crossing that frame are split and the right part shifts with the rest. Locked tracks never move.
    - Refusals: clips on a locked track (`lockedSource`) or a locked destination (`lockedTarget`), in both modes.
    - Duplicates get new ids; copies that shared a link group (or group) share a new one, a lone copy is unlinked. Moving clips never overwrite each other (they leave their place first); a copy may overwrite its original.
    - `sliceClip`: keyframes partitioned by frame and re-based (an edge that did not move keeps the keyframes past it); a new edge drops that side's fade, transition and text animation. Split pieces of one link group that start at the same frame (cut at the same frame, whatever their lengths) are linked to each other under a new group; a lone piece is unlinked.
    - Lanes (`laneOf`, `clampLaneDelta`, `laneTarget`, `mapLanes`): video and audio tracks numbered outward from the divider. A vertical move shifts every clip by the same lane delta within its kind, so V1 -> V2 takes A1 -> A2 (§6.8 "same track delta"). Each kind is clamped at its first lane; caption clips never change track. Lanes past the last track become new tracks (V3, A4..., in lane order, at the default places).
    - `applyMoveRequest` (lane delta -> track map -> `moveClips`), `nudgeClips`, `moveToAdjacentLane`.
    - Collision lookups: per-track `ends` (sorted, since clips never overlap) + `clipsOverlapping`, a binary search on the ends: O(log n + k) per clip.
  - Drag gesture (`timeline/view/gestures/moveClips.ts`, `MoveGesture`):
    - 4 px dead zone (`--timeline-drag-threshold`). The proposal (delta, lane deltas, mode, duplicate, ghosts, new track lanes, overwritten spans, insert frame, refusal) is recomputed only when its outcome changes; the overlay draws it. The document is untouched until the drop, which sends one `MoveRequest` to the controller (P2).
    - The anchor (pressed clip) follows the row under the pointer within its kind. Above the top video track (or below the bottom audio track) means a new track; the other kind's side clamps to lane 0. Shift keeps every clip on its track, Alt duplicates, Mod inserts. Modifier keys pressed or released mid-drag update the ghost at once (window key listeners while dragging; a lone Alt key is preventDefault-ed so Windows does not focus the browser menu).
    - Esc: `app.cancel` -> `TimelineView.cancelGesture()` (declined when nothing runs, so popovers still get Esc). A document edit under a drag (an undo key) cancels it.
  - Overlay (§6.17 order): new track rows (header with the name it will get), ghosts at 70% (kind colors, accent outline; red when refused), hatching over the overwritten spans, the insert line with an arrow, the marquee, the playhead, the `Δ +00:00:12` tooltip (mm:ss:ff).
  - Auto-scroll (§6.6) for scrub, move and marquee: within 24 px of the track area's edges or past them, 12 px per 60 Hz frame at the edge and up to 3x past it, scaled by frame time. A drag that proposes new tracks gets extra vertical room so auto-scroll brings their rows into view; the view settles back into range after the drag.
  - Keys: `edit.nudgeLeft/Right(5)` (Alt+Left/Right 1 frame, Alt+Shift 5: overwrite, coalesceKey `clip.nudge`, so a burst is one undo step; handled even with nothing selected because Alt+Left is the browser's Back). `edit.moveToTrackAbove/Below` (Alt+Up/Down): to the adjacent track if the spans there are free; the primary clip's kind sets the direction and linked audio follows with the same lane delta; no tracks are created.
  - Refusals are toasts: locked track (error), occupied adjacent track (info).
  - Dev: `__editor.tracks.list()` / `.update("V2", { locked: true })` (track flags for the checks until the Batch 16 header buttons).
  - IdleQueue: named pausers (`"playback"`, `"gesture"`), so one resume never undoes another's pause (Batch 09 follow-up). Scrub, move and marquee pause it.
  - Measured:
    - 714 unit tests in 87 files (+50 tests, +2 files: `move.test.ts`, `autoScroll.test.ts`), plus the perf project.
    - Build: 437.34 kB JS (143.79 kB gzip, +24.03 / +7.70 kB), 38.68 kB CSS (+0.24 kB); workers unchanged.
    - Setup: headless Chrome 155 over CDP (real `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`/`dispatchKeyEvent`, modifiers included), dev server, OPFS projects `b11-a1`..`b11-a5`, `b11-perf`; 1600x900.
    - Acceptance 1 (`b11-a1`): "short" (V2, 0..60) dragged onto the middle of "long" (V1, 0..300) at frame 120. Mid-drag: hatch [120, 180), 0 document changes. Drop: `long@0+120 short@120+60 long@180+120`, one undo step "Move clip". Ctrl+Z: `long@0+300`, short back on V2.
    - Acceptance 2 (`b11-a2`): V1 a/b, V2 locked (L 60..120), V3 c (30..90) and m (400..430), A1 a 20 s WAV bed. m dragged to V1 at 60 with Ctrl at the drop: V1 `a@0 m@60 b@120`, V3 `c@30+30 c@90+30` (split and shifted), A1 `bed@0+60 bed@90+540` (split, the gap opened), the locked V2 unchanged. - deviations:
  - Insert collisions with locked tracks: locked tracks never shift and nothing lands on them, so the only insert refusal is a locked destination (or source) track. It is reported by an error toast, as in overwrite mode.
  - Insert splits the clips crossing the insert frame on every unlocked track and shifts the right parts (Premiere's insert with sync locks on), so all unlocked tracks stay in sync. The gap is the moved block's span (earliest start to latest end).
  - Mod+click toggles the clip alone (§6.7 "add without linked partner"), so a second Mod+click removes it.
  - Alt on an already-selected clip keeps the selection, so Alt+drag duplicates all of it; Alt+click without a drag then selects only that clip (Premiere's Alt behavior).
  - A click on empty space clears the selection on release, not on press (a press there may start a marquee). Mod does nothing special for the marquee.
  - Keyframes are partitioned by frame on overwrite trims and splits, with no boundary keyframes: eases are opaque until Batch 35.
  - Alt+Up/Down never create tracks: each kind stops at its outermost existing track, and the move is refused when a destination span is taken.
  - Dragging above the top video track proposes the anchor's next lane (one new track for a single clip); a multi-track selection whose top clip is not the anchor may need more than one new track, all shown as rows.
  - The ruler scrub also auto-scrolls near the edges and pauses the idle queue (§6.6 lists the playhead; §3.4 pauses while dragging).

### Batch 12: Timeline snapping
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-15
- notes:
  - Snap index (`src/timeline/snap/snapIndex.ts`, replaces the `index.ts` stub, fully unit tested):
    - Candidates in the §6.9 priority order: playhead, clip starts and ends on every track (locked ones included), markers, the in and out points, frame 0. The playhead is passed in at query time; in the index it would need a rebuild per frame during playback. Keyframes and transition edges are `TODO(batch 35)` and `TODO(batch 36)`.
    - `buildSnapCandidates`: one pass over clips and markers into packed float64 keys (`(frame * 8 + kind) * 2^21 + entry`) and one numeric typed-array sort (no comparator calls), then frame, kind and ref arrays.
    - `SnapIndex.get(project, inPoint, outPoint)` rebuilds lazily: on the first query after `project.clips`, `project.markers` or the in/out points changed (compared by reference, the document is immutable). Never per pointer move, never on a document change by itself.
    - `resolveSnap(candidates, edges, { thresholdPx, pxPerFrame, exclude, playhead })`: a binary search per edge into the ±threshold window. The smallest screen distance wins, then the priority, then the earlier edge, then the lower frame. `exclude` takes clip (or marker) ids. `snapLabel` names the target: "End of b", "Playhead", "Marker: Drop", "In point", "Timeline start".
  - Clip drags (`MoveGesture.update(..., snap)`): the block's leading and trailing edges are tested at the raw fractional delta, and the closer one lands on the candidate. The delta is then clamped at frame 0; a trailing-edge snap that would push the block below 0 is dropped. The dragged clips are no candidates. While Alt duplicates, the originals stay put and are candidates, so a copy snaps right after its original. The proposal carries `snap`, and the ghost is drawn at the snapped position, so it sticks until the pointer leaves the threshold. A playhead move during a drag (playback) re-proposes.
  - Ruler scrub (§6.3): the playhead snaps only while Shift is held and snapping is on, to every candidate but the playhead. Shift or S pressed or released mid-scrub re-snaps at once. The wheel during a scrub now moves the playhead with the view, as auto-scroll does.
  - Toggle (`toggle.snap`: S and the toolbar magnet) flips session `snap` (persisted in session.json). The magnet is enabled and shows the state through its own one-flag subscription: one React commit per toggle. Holding S during any drag (clip move, scrub, marquee) inverts snapping until it is released, without touching the session (0 commits). The drag's window key listener reads S in the capture phase (see deviations). A key repeat (S pressed before the drag) does not hold.
  - Overlay: a 1 px `--accent` snap line through the full timeline height (ruler and tracks, not the header column) at the snapped frame, after the hover and before the ghosts (§6.17 order). The drag tooltip shows the target's name after the delta, in the caption UI font and `--accent`; a Shift scrub shows the name alone.
  - Fixed during the browser check: the binary search window lacked the distance test's float tolerance. A pointer exactly 8 px away (edge 62.666666666666686 for 60 + 8/3 at 3 px/frame) found no candidate. The window now uses the same epsilon; the unit test fails on the old code.
  - Test isolation: `TimelineView.test.ts` unmounts every view after each test (a drag left open kept its window key listeners into the next test).
  - Measured:
    - 743 unit tests in 89 files (+24 tests, +1 file `snapIndex.test.ts`), plus `snapIndex.perf.test.ts` in the perf project.
    - Snap index rebuild, 500 clips on 8 tracks + 20 markers (1023 candidates), Node: median 0.10 ms, cold 0.60-0.77 ms; one query 1.1 µs. In Chrome (`generate(500, 8)`, 1001 candidates): median 0.1 ms, p95 0.2 ms, max 0.7 ms (0.1 ms timer resolution).

Far away: no snap. React commits during the drags: none apart from the press's click selection.

- deviations:
  - During a drag the drag's window key listener reads S in the capture phase and stops it, so it never reaches the KeyDispatcher (§3.6: a single KeyDispatcher listens on window). Reason: S must act as a modifier while Shift (the scrub's snap key, the move's keep-track key), Alt or Mod is held, and Shift+S and Mod+S are other commands (linked selection, save). Key-ups pass on, so the dispatcher releases an S pressed before the drag. Outside drags S goes through the dispatcher (`toggle.snap`).
  - The drag matches S as the dispatcher does: by the letter typed, or by the key position when no letter comes (Option+S types "ß" on macOS).
  - While Alt duplicates, the originals are snap candidates. §6.9 excludes "the clips being dragged"; with Alt the copies move and the originals stay.
  - A scrub snap's line lies under the 2 px active playhead in the track area (both are on the same frame). The gold shows in the ruler above the playhead head and in the label.

### Batch 13: Trimming I: regular and ripple trims, trim to playhead
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-15
- notes:
  - Pure edit (`src/timeline/edit/trim.ts`, fully unit tested in `trim.test.ts`, 35 tests):
    - `planTrim(doc, clipIds, edge, { ripple, linked })` resolves the delta-independent part once per gesture: the trimmed clips (the given ones and, unless `linked: false`, their partners on unlocked tracks), the clips a ripple shifts, and the range of deltas every limit allows. `resolveTrim(plan, delta)` clamps the request into it and builds one `clip.trim` command (only clip records change; trims never reorder a track). `trimEdge(doc, clipId, edge, delta, { ripple })` is the two together; `applyTrim` gives the document the command leaves (the live preview and the overlay draw it).
    - Limits, each an interval of deltas, reported by reason (`mediaStart`, `mediaEnd`, `minDuration`, `neighbor`, `ripple`, `timelineStart`): the 1-frame minimum; the media bounds of video and audio clips (`headFrames`, `maxDurationFrames`, computed with `framesToSourceUs` so a trim and its reverse restore in and out exactly, also at speed != 1 within 1 us; none for images, text, solids, captions); frame 0; the neighbor clip (regular); the ripple collisions (ripple: the gap before the first shifted clip of every unlocked track); each partner's own (both stop when the partner hits its bound first). `mediaBound` says when a trimmed edge sits on its media bound (red edge).
    - Ripple: the in point keeps its position (the content slides under it), the clips after the edit point on every unlocked track shift by the change in duration; locked tracks never move.
    - Clip changes: in trims move `start` (regular) and `in`; out trims move `out` by the delta, capped at the media end; stills keep `in` with `out = in + duration`. Video and audio keyframes follow the source on in trims (out-of-range keys kept); fades are clamped to the new duration. ### Batch 14: Trimming II: roll, slip, slide, rate stretch, edit points
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-15
- notes:
  - Pure edits (`src/timeline/edit/trim.ts`, unit tested in `trim.test.ts`, +16 tests):
    - The plan is generalized to per-clip moves (`ClipMove`: `in`, `out`, `move`, `slip`, `stretchIn`, `stretchOut`) with the Batch 13 interval limits: an edge stops at the facing edge of its neighbor unless that edge moves with it, so a roll's two sides and a slide's neighbors never limit each other. `planTrim` keeps its signature and behavior (the 35 Batch 13 tests pass unchanged); ripple stays a trim option.
    - `planRoll`/`rollEdit(doc, leftId, rightId, delta)`: the left clip's out and the right clip's in (and their partners') move together; total duration unchanged; limited by both media bounds and the 1-frame minimum.
    - `planSlip`/`slip(doc, clipId, delta)`: `in` and `out` move by the same source delta (positive = later frames), keyframes stay on their source frames; video and audio clips only (`tailFrames` bounds the end).
    - `planSlide`/`slide(doc, clipId, delta)`: the clip (and its partners) move; the abutting previous clip's out and next clip's in trim by the same delta; a gap side takes the change, bounded by the clip beyond it or frame 0.
    - `planStretch`/`rateStretch(doc, clipId, edge, delta)`: the edge moves, `speed = speed * oldDuration / newDuration`, `in`/`out` unchanged, 0.25x..4x (`minSpeed`/`maxSpeed` limits), keyframe frames scaled, fades clamped; non-media clips trim.
    - Media bounds are per clip and side (`bounds`): a roll reports which side sits on its bound. `planEdit(doc, spec)` replays a gesture's `EditSpec` (the controller dispatches `TrimRequest`s of every kind through it). Commands `clip.trim`, `clip.roll`, `clip.slip`, `clip.slide`, `clip.rateStretch`: one undo step each ("Rolling edit", "Slip clip(s)", "Slide clip(s)", "Rate stretch clip(s)").
  - Hit testing: `junction` hits on the 6 px band centered on a cut between abutting clips on unlocked tracks (`HitResult.junction`: left, right, frame; `clipId` is the side under the pointer). Tools change what a hit does (§6.18): Select trims edges, rolls cuts with Mod+Alt (cursor switches while hovering), selects the edit point on a click on a cut; Slip (Y) and Slide (U) drag clip bodies (and edges); Rate stretch (R) drags edges, its bodies only select. `tool.select/slip/slide/rateStretch` set `activeTool`; the toolbar tool buttons show it (one-flag subscriptions). Razor and Hand stay for Batches 15 and 18.
  - Gesture: `TrimGesture` takes an edit kind (trim, roll, slip, slide, stretch). Edges and the slid clip's two edges snap (`resolveSnap`, excluding what the edit moves); slips follow the pointer as in Premiere (dragging right shows earlier frames). Alt edits one side of a link (except rolls, which Mod+Alt starts). One plan per (ripple, linked), one request at the release, Esc and document changes cancel, 0 React commits during the drag.
  - Previews: `TrimProposal.previewSplit`: roll = the left clip's new last frame | the right clip's new first frame, slip = the clip's new first | last frame, slide = the left neighbor's new last | the right neighbor's new first frame. `PreviewView` renders it through a second compositor, `LayerTextures.resolveSplit` (one pass over both panes, its own slots per pane, one scrub request per media so the panes never supersede each other) and `Renderer.drawPanes` (one render pass, each pane clipped to its half). Acceptance 3 by the `rateStretch` tests (doubled duration gives 0.5x, in/out unchanged, partners, 0.25x..4x) and `AudioScheduler.test.ts` (the voice restarts at playbackRate 0.5); pitch measured in the browser (222 Hz), manual check 3. My own probe (not committed): 400 random projects x 25 random trims, ripples, rolls, slips, slides and stretches (linked and Alt, off-grid media end, speeds 0.5 and 2) all left valid documents through a validating store, with the roll, slip and stretch invariants holding. Nothing from Do not build yet (no speed UI in properties; keyframes only scaled proportionally, `TODO(batch 35)`). No color literals; the junction band is a token (`--timeline-junction-zone`); the new cursors reuse the 24-unit SVG geometry noted in the Batch 13 review (listed under Design system gaps). One command per release (`clip.roll`, `clip.slip`, `clip.slide`, `clip.rateStretch`), integer frames (speed is not time), the split preview drawn in the scheduler's preview render in one pass, the edit point in session state (written deviation), tool buttons on one-flag subscriptions. Every TODO has a batch tag. The Batch 13 note on §6.10's hit-priority sentence now has its written deviation. Minor, not blocking: (1) speed is recomputed from the current speed on every stretch, so separate drags drift: 13 -> 23 -> 13 frames leaves speed 0.9999999999999999 (the clip then shows a `1x` badge), and a full stretch after that gives 0.24999999999999997, just under `MIN_SPEED`. Snapping near-integer speeds (or computing the speed from (out - in) / duration) belongs with the Batch 27 speed UI, which reuses this math. (2) A stretched linked pair with a sync offset gets the same frame delta on each side, so the two sides end up at different speeds.

  1. `src/timeline/edit/gaps.ts:183-191` (passive tracks), with `:152-182` (source tracks) and `:115-150` (the passive limit check): when gaps on different tracks do not overlap in time, every passive track moves by the sum of all the clusters' amounts, but each source track moves only by its own gaps. The content after the gaps then loses sync, and the summed amount also causes collision limits that should not happen. This breaks §6.11 ("closes the resulting gaps by shifting later clips on all unlocked tracks") and the module's own aim (lines 6-7: "keeping their content in sync with what moved"). I reproduced it with temporary Vitest probes (not committed); all tracks are targeted unless noted:
     - (a) V1 A 0+100, B 100+100, C 200+100, D 300+100, E 400+100; V2 F, G, H, I, J at the same frames; A2 K 500+100. `rippleDelete(["B", "I"])`: E and J now start at 300, and so does K. K used to start where E and J ended; now it overlaps them by 100 frames. Each source track closed 100 frames; A2 moved 200.
     - (b) The same layout with A2 Z 150+140 and K 450+100: `closed` is [100, 60] and `limit` is K on A2, so the toast says "Ripple delete stopped short". Moving K by 100 (what V1 and V2 each closed) fits in its 160 free frames. Instead K moved 160, more than any track closed.
     - (c) Compact (Shift+G) with A2 untargeted: V1 a 0+100, b 200+100, b2 300+300; V2 c 0+300, d 400+100, d2 500+100; A2 e 600+100. Afterwards b2 and d2 end at 500, but e starts at 400 (it used to start after both).
     - (d) A realistic case: delete a linked video/audio pair at 100..200 on V1/A1 and a title at 300..350 on V2, with a sound effect on A2 at 500 on the next video cut. The video cut moves to 400 and the sound effect to 350.
     `gaps.test.ts:105` ("gaps apart in time each move the other tracks by their own length") asserts this rule, but in a layout where no source track has content after the other track's gap, so the problem doesn't show. Fix: a passive clip must not move more than the source tracks have closed before it. For example, its shift could be the most that any one source track has closed in total before the clip's start; for overlapping gaps (acceptance 2) this gives the same result as today. The collision check (`room`) must use that amount. Add tests for (a)-(c), and update the module comment and the Global deviation "Ripple with gaps on several tracks".

Nothing from Do not build yet (no lift/extract, no delete-track UI; the clipboard rows are disabled placeholders with `TODO(batch 39)`). No color literals in the batch's files; the remaining `1px` borders and rings are the DS hairline and input focus ring, as elsewhere in the code. One dispatch per action, and label changes are one transaction. Every TODO has a `(batch NN)` tag, and no `TODO(batch 15)` is left.
  - Minor, not blocking: during Compact, a targeted track with no gaps of its own is a passive track, so it follows (and can limit) the other tracks' ripple. As soon as it has any gap, it is a source track and ignores them. Example: V1 a 0+100, b 200+100 and V2 c 0+200, d 200+200, both targeted. Shift+G closes nothing (limit d on V2). Add a 1-frame gap at 400 on V2 (e at 401) and V1 closes all 100 frames while d stays at 200. This follows the written deviation's rule; Batch 16 (compact on selected tracks, already a follow-up) should decide whether targeted tracks in a compact should ever limit each other.

### Batch 23: Canvas snapping, smart guides, proximity measurements
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-16
- notes:
  - Snapping (unit tested):
    - `render/preview/snap.ts` (`snap.test.ts`, 22 tests): `buildCanvasSnap` collects the candidates in the §7.4 priority order: the frame's center and edges, plus its thirds while the Thirds grid shows (priority 0); the safe rectangles on screen (1); the other visible layers' bounding box edges and centers (2); and equal spacing, the midpoint of the room between every two layers one after the other on an axis (3). Lines are sorted by value, and a query binary-searches the reach. `CanvasSnapIndex` keeps the candidates and rebuilds them only when its sources differ by value: the other layers' bounds, the frame, thirds and the safe rectangles. It counts `rebuilds` and `queries`.
    - Resolution: `nearestLine` takes the nearest line within reach of any tested value, and ties go to the higher priority. `snapMove` tests the moved box's edges and center on the free axes, x first. Equal spacing applies only when the box fits the room, both layers overlap it across the axis, and no other such layer sits between them. `snapHandle` snaps a scale handle on its free axes; a uniform corner takes the nearer target and the other axis follows the diagonal. `isAxisAligned` gates the scale snap. The box sticks while the raw position stays within reach.
    - Guides: `moveGuides` and `handleGuides` show lines across the frame for frame and safe targets. A layer line spans the box and the layers on it, with the distance to the nearest layer on each side, once per layer. Equal-spacing gaps are spans, and a layer-line distance they already show is dropped. `measureGuides` gives the four sides to the nearest layer in line, else to the frame edge. `formatDistance` labels in whole px, else one decimal.
    - `gizmo.ts` (+1 test): `moveDelta` holds the rounding and the Shift axis lock, and returns the free axes. `moveGesture` takes a `snap` offset added after the rounding. `scaleGesture` takes `snap` for the 100% snap (off when snapping is off). `canvasLayers.ts`: `CanvasLayer.muted`.
    - `CanvasEditInput.ts` (+7 tests):
      - `snapping` is the session's `snap`, inverted while S is held during a drag. S is read in the capture-phase modifier listener with `preventDefault`/`stopPropagation`; repeats are ignored and the key-up passes on, as on the timeline. `isSnapKey` moved to `core/keyboard/keys.ts`.
      - `updateDrag`: a move snaps through `snapMove` and keeps `moveGuides`. A scale aims the gesture at the snapped handle point and keeps `handleGuides`. Rotation keeps its Shift snap; anchor drags do not snap.
      - Candidates come from `snapCandidates(held)`: the frame, thirds while the grid is Thirds, `safeZoneOn(...).safe` plus title-safe and action-safe while shown, and the other non-muted layers while `preview.guides` is on.
      - `scene().guides` holds the drag's guides, or the measure mode: Alt over the canvas, no press or drag, a selection, Smart guides on. `snapStats` gives the counters. Alt entering or leaving the canvas redraws.

- deviations:
  - With Smart guides off, other layers and equal spacing are not snap targets and Alt measures nothing. The frame and safe targets still snap with the Snap toggle, and their lines are always drawn (§0 "every snap is visible").
  - Thirds are targets while the grid overlay shows Thirds: the Overlays menu's Thirds is §7.4's "thirds" toggle. Title-safe and action-safe edges are targets while shown, alongside the platform safe rectangle (the mask regions' own edges are not).
  - Layers are targets by the axis-aligned bounds of their visible quads, so a turned layer counts by its bounding box. Muted layers are not targets: they are out of the picture, though selectable. Layers on locked tracks are targets and measure neighbours (in the picture, though not selectable; fixed after the review).
  - The S toggle and hold-S also govern the §7.3 100% scale snap (one snap state). Shift's 45° rotation snap stays, since Shift is an explicit modifier, and is the only rotation snap (§7.4 "rotation (Shift)"). Anchor drags do not snap.
  - A snapped axis lands exactly on its target, which can be a fractional project px; unsnapped axes stay whole px (Batch 22).
  - A scale snaps the dragged edge only while the box is axis-aligned: no turn or a quarter turn, and group boxes. A uniform corner snaps along the nearer target's axis, and the other axis follows the aspect.
  - Equal spacing covers only the middle case (§7.4 "when moving the middle one"). The box is centered in the room between two layers that both overlap it across the axis, with no other such layer between them and gaps over 0. A series is not extended past its end.
  - Guides show every target the moved box meets exactly, including on an axis Shift holds. A layer line spans the box and every layer on it, with the distance to the nearest layer on each side (once per layer). A distance already shown by an equal-spacing gap is not repeated.
  - Measure mode: each side measures to the nearest layer overlapping the selection across it, else to the frame edge, so both are never drawn on one line. A box overhanging the frame gets a negative distance. A group measures from its box. It needs Smart guides on, and the anchor marker still shows with one layer.
  - Candidates are compared by value at each query and rebuilt only when the other layers' bounds, the frame or the overlays shown differ. Dragging another layer is a different candidate set, so it rebuilds once.

- deviations:
  - Proxy settings are global app settings (IndexedDB `settings.v1`), shown in the Project section: §5.2's `Project` type is kept verbatim (no settings field for them), and which footage is too heavy depends on the machine, not the project. The switch governs automatic proxies only; pending jobs still run when it is turned off, and Generate proxy works with it off.
  - Resume = start over: an MP4 being muxed cannot be continued, so the `.part` of an interrupted job is deleted on open and the pending video is made again from frame 0 (acceptance 3: "or restarts cleanly").
  - Jobs pause while the IdleQueue is paused: playback and also timeline drags, scrubs and trims (§9.5 names playback and export), so the scrub's decodes come first.
  - Auto asks for the full frame as soon as playback pauses or a scrub or trim ends (the proxy frame stays on screen until the full one is decoded), where §8 says "after 300 ms of inactivity"; a scrub held still is at rest after 300 ms (§7.5). Acceptance 2's "switches to full within 300 ms" holds up to about 45 frames past a keyframe in the 1 s GOPs of the 4K60 HEVC test file; deeper frames took 308-414 ms (the hardware decode rate, ~7 ms per frame, as measured since Batch 06).
  - The "more than 2 frames behind → proxy" rule (§8, the Build's automatic downgrade): Auto already plays the proxy of every video that has one, so a video with no proxy decision that falls behind gets one queued (`onBehind`); 1/2 and 1/4 switch a video that falls behind to its proxy for the rest of the playback; Full never switches.
  - H.264 Main is tried first, then High and Constrained Baseline for encoders without Main. Frames are scaled by successive 2x bilinear halvings (the Build's "pick the faster that keeps quality", numbers in the notes), and keep their coded orientation with the source's rotation in the proxy's track matrix.
  - Thumbnails: a video's LOD0/LOD1 sheets are made again on any source change, also back to the source file after Remove proxy (the index records one source); the shown sheets stay until replaced.
  - Export frame decodes each video's exact full frame at its own size (or twice its drawn size when drawn under half, at most 4096 px) instead of drawing the textures last shown.
