- deviations:
  - Field scrubs write ephemeral values (`liveEdit`) and commit one command on release. §11 asks for coalesced commands during the scrub; P2 (binding) keeps gestures out of the document, so a scrub neither autosaves nor renders the app bar. Either way a gesture is one undo step. Arrow steps coalesce (`properties.<prop>`, 300 ms).
  - Transform fields:
    - Position shows the stored numbers: project px from the frame center, so typing 100 sets exactly 100.
    - Scale has W and H fields in % with an aspect lock between them. The lock starts closed unless a selected layer is scaled unevenly; while locked, the other axis follows by the same factor. The range is 1% to 10000%.
    - Rotation is in degrees, anchor in %, opacity in %.
    - Anchor edits keep the picture in place (the gizmo's Alt anchor drag), instead of moving the layer.
  - Clip times:
    - End is the exclusive end (Start + Duration).
    - Start trims the in point (the end stays); End and Duration trim the out point; Source in/out trim by the typed source time at the clip's speed.
    - These are regular trims (no ripple). Linked partners follow while Linked selection is on. They clamp at media and neighbors, with the trim toasts.
    - With several clips, each is trimmed to the typed time, in one undo step.

  - Crop to frame (§11) keeps the transform. When the layer covers the frame, the visible area is the frame exactly; otherwise it is the largest area with the frame's aspect inside the part of the frame the layer covers (so a fitted 16:9 clip in a 9:16 frame is cut to its 9:16 middle and Fill then fills the frame exactly, acceptance 1). A turned layer gets the largest such rectangle centered in the turned frame, then inside the media (never outside either; not always the largest possible); the frame's aspect follows the nearest quarter turn. A layer outside the frame is left as it is.
  - Crop mode (§7.3 "crop handles as a gizmo mode"; Build "toggle in the Crop section header or double-click a video layer with the crop tool chip"): the header toggle and a double-click on a video or image layer enter it; the "crop tool chip" is a chip over the canvas while crop mode is on (Crop · Reset · Done). One layer at a time; a double-click selects it alone (a group's other layers leave the selection). It ends on Esc (after a running gesture), Done, a double-click on the layer, a selection that is no longer that layer alone, the clip leaving, or its track locking. In crop mode a body drag moves the layer (no dragging the media inside the crop window), Alt is the symmetric crop (no anchor marker, no measure mode), and the box has no rotate zones.
  - The aspect lock is the Crop section's toggle, shared with the canvas handles, and Shift inverts it during a handle drag (as Shift inverts the corners' uniform scale, §7.3). It keeps the current visible aspect in media px: a field or an edge handle moves the other axis around its center (shifted to stay inside the media); a corner scales from the opposite corner (or the center with Alt).
  - Crop edges snap to the frame's edges, center and thirds (the Build's "frame edges and thirds"), always including the thirds (moves and scales snap to them only while the Thirds grid shows, Batch 23), only while snapping is on and the layer is axis-aligned; no other layers or safe zones.
  - Crop units: media px of the media as shown (rotation metadata applied), or % of its side; px by default, the choice kept for the session (not persisted). A crop always leaves at least 1 media px on each axis (a crop to nothing would drop the layer from the picture and the canvas).
  - A crop handle drag writes `liveEdit.crops` (where Crop field scrubs write theirs), not a gesture-local map as transform gestures do: the Crop fields follow the drag live (acceptance 2 "fields match").
  - Crop fractions cut the sides as shown after the flips (Batch 08's compositor rule): flipping a cropped clip mirrors the picture inside the same crop window on screen.

### Batch 27: Speed, duration, freeze frame, punch zoom
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-16
- notes:
  - Engine (unit tested):
    - `core/document/types.ts`: `isFreeze(clip)`, a video clip with `speed = 0`. `validate.ts` allows speed 0 only on video clips and skips the duration x speed invariant for them (`out > in`, `out <= media` still hold).
    - New `timeline/edit/speed.ts` (`speed.test.ts`, 10 tests):
      - `setSpeeds(project, ids, speed | (clip) => speed, { link, ripple, linked })` is one `clip.speed` command ("Change speed").
      - The speed stays exactly as asked, clamped to 0.25x..4x. Linked (the default), `in`/`out` stay and the duration follows, rounded to whole frames; keyframes scale with the duration and fades are clamped. Unlinked, the duration stays and `out` follows from `in`. When the media runs out first, the clip is shortened and the result reports `mediaEnd` (§6.19 "clamp, warn").
      - A clip and its partners (with Linked selection, or when both are selected) change together, once. Groups are processed latest end first.
      - Ripple reuses the ripple trim's out-point plan (`planTrim(..., { ripple: true })`): what follows each member on its track, and what follows the clip's end on every other unlocked track. A shift to the left stops where a track would overlap (a gap stays, `ripple`). Without ripple, a slower clip stops at the next clip: the speed stays and the out point comes in (`neighbor`).
      - `setSpeedDurations(...)` ("Change duration") serves the Speed section's duration. Linked, it is a rate stretch of the out point; `planStretch` takes a `ripple` option (the Rate stretch tool still never ripples). Unlinked, and for freeze frames, it is a trim of the out point. Both ripple with the option.
      - Helpers: `clampSpeed`, `hasSpeed`.
    - New `timeline/edit/freeze.ts` (`freeze.test.ts`, 7 tests):
      - `freezeFrame(project, frame, selection, newId)` (`clip.freezeFrame`, "Freeze frame"):
        - Targets the selected video clips under the playhead, else the topmost enabled video under it on a targeted, unlocked, visible track.
        - Splits each target there together with its linked partners (always, so the sound stays in sync).
        - Inserts a `FREEZE_SECONDS` (2 s) clip between the halves: speed 0, `in` = the source time shown at the playhead, `out` = one project frame later. The freeze keeps the clip's look (name, label color, transform, crop, opacity) and drops the time-based parts (fades, keyframes, transitions, link, group).
        - Ripple: every clip from the playhead on, on every unlocked track, shifts right by 2 s. A clip spanning the playhead without being split (a music bed) stays where it is.
        - When the playhead is at a clip's start, nothing is split and the freeze goes before the clip.
        - A miss returns "none" or "notUnderPlayhead" (selected, but not under the playhead).
      - `punchZoom(project, frame, selection, factor, newId, { linked })` (`clip.punchZoom`, "Punch zoom"):
        - Targets the selected layers under the playhead, else the topmost video or image.
        - Splits them there (linked partners with them while Linked selection is on, as Split at playhead) and multiplies the right pieces' `scale` (and `scaleY`) by the factor around their anchor.
        - A clip that starts at the playhead is zoomed whole.
    - Freeze frames elsewhere:
      - `trim.ts` `hasSource` is false for them, so they have no media bounds; slip skips them; Rate stretch trims their edge; an in-point trim keeps `in`/`out`. Also exported here: `scaleKeyframes`, `editCommand`.
      - `move.ts` `sliceClip`: both pieces of a split freeze keep `in`/`out`.
      - `queries.ts` `linkOffset`: a freeze is in sync when it starts with its partner.
      - `clipProps.ts` `hasSourceRange`: no Source in/out rows for a freeze.
      - `AudioScheduler` never schedules a speed-0 clip.
      - The timeline's stretch tooltip shows 1x for clips without speed.
    - `PlaybackEngine`: no change needed. A freeze's source time is constant, so its prefetch window is one frame. The new test (`PlaybackEngine.test.ts`, +1) plays 80 frames through a freeze: one window `[2 s, 2 s]`, no drops.

- deviations:
  - Speed (§11, §14):
    - The speed is kept exactly as asked. Linked, the duration rounds; it is never derived back from a rounded duration.
    - Without ripple, a slower clip stops at the next clip and its out point comes in (Premiere's behavior), with a toast; a faster clip leaves a gap.
    - Ripple moves what follows as a ripple trim of the out point does. A shift to the left stops at the first overlap, and a gap stays.
    - (fix) A clip and its linked partners get the same speed, and each is retimed from its own start and source range, so it gets its own duration. Partners that differ (an L cut, a speed set with Linked selection off) keep their own `in`/`out`. Partners that start apart (a J cut) keep their starts, so the pair shows a sync offset afterwards; "Move into sync" puts it back.
    - (fix) Ripple shifts what follows by the largest change of duration among the members. The clips after them stay in sync and none overlaps. An L cut's overlap shrinks or grows with the speed, which can leave a gap on the sound's track.
    - (fix 2) A clip with less than one frame of media left after its `in` at the new speed keeps its speed, linked or not, and the change reports `mediaEnd` (toast "Limited by the media end"). Its partners still change. §6.19 asks to clamp and warn; a clamped `out` would leave `out - in` short of `duration x speed`, and a later rate stretch to a slower speed then breaks §5.2. A speed that fills the one frame was not used: it is always below the one asked and can be below the current one. So `out` always follows `in` exactly after a speed change.
    - The Speed section's options are per session (not persisted): duration link on, Ripple on by default, so a speed-up closes up on a short's timeline.
    - The Build's "ripple checkbox" is the DS switch.
  - Speed field scrubs show the value in the field and apply once on release. There is no live retiming of the timeline or the preview during the scrub (P1/P2); the Rate stretch tool is the live way.
  - The Speed section's Duration is a rate stretch of the out point when linked, and a trim of the out point when unlinked or for a freeze. Both ripple with the option. The Clip section's Duration stays a regular trim.
  - Freeze frame (Build "media clip with speed = 0"):
    - `out` is one project frame after `in`. Linked partners are always split, so the sound stays in sync even with Linked selection off.
    - The ripple covers every unlocked track from the playhead on.
    - The target is the selected video under the playhead, else the topmost targeted visible video. Selected clips that are not under the playhead get a toast instead of another clip being frozen.
    - Freeze frames trim like images (no media bounds), never slip, and stretch as a trim. A split gives two holds of the same frame.
  - Punch zoom:
    - The factor is the app setting `punchZoomScale` (1.2; 1.05..3), applied to `scale` and `scaleY` around the anchor.
    - Linked partners are split while Linked selection is on (as Split at playhead).
    - The target is the selected layers under the playhead, else the topmost video or image. A clip starting at the playhead is zoomed whole.
    - `punchZoomAnimated` is a reserved app setting (false, read by nothing).
  - "Speed..." in the clip menu opens the Speed section with its speed field focused (no dialog).

  1. `src/timeline/edit/speed.ts:111-122` and `:139` (`retimeGroup`): a group (a clip and its linked partners) gets one shared change of duration. That change is computed from the primary only (`:111`), then lowered to each member's media room at the new speed (`:115-120`), then raised again to every member's 1-frame minimum (`:122`). When the partners differ in duration or speed, `:122` can push a member past its media room. `:139` then clamps `out` to the media end, so `out - in` no longer matches `duration x speed`, and the document is invalid. Reachable in the UI: import a 10 s video with sound and put it on the timeline. With Linked selection off, select only the video and click 2x (video 150 frames at 2x, sound 300 frames at 1x). Turn Linked selection on, select the video and type 400 in Speed. Result (unit repro, `setSpeeds(p, ["v"], 4, { link: true, ripple: true, linked: true })`): the video collapses to 1 frame (out 133 333 us), and the sound gets 151 frames at 4x with out clamped to 10 000 000 us. `validateProject` reports `clip "a": out - in = 10000000 us, expected duration * speed = 20133333 us`, and a validating `DocumentStore` throws `DocumentInvariantError` (dev builds). `limit` is null, so no toast. Production builds would commit and save the invalid document. My probe (600 random projects x 12 random `setSpeeds` / `setSpeedDurations` / `freezeFrame` / `punchZoom` calls, 3846 commands through a validating store) hit this 72 times, every time in a linked group whose members differed in duration or speed. Partners whose spans differ also get their own source range changed (the sound's `out` moves) while "linked" promises in/out stay. Fix: retime each member from its own `in`/`out` (duration = round(member span / speed), each clamped to its own media with a `mediaEnd` limit), or write down and test a rule that keeps the pair's offset without breaking a member's source range or the §5.2 invariant. ### Batch 28: Text engine
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-16
- notes:
  - Model (`core/document/types.ts`, unit tested):
    - `TextContent = { value, box: { mode: "auto" | "fixed", width } }`: plain text with `\n` breaks, and its box.
    - `TextStyle`: family, weight (1..1000), italic, size, fill (`RGBA | Gradient`), stroke / shadow / background (each with `enabled`), case, letter spacing (px), line height (x), align, vertical anchor.
    - `Gradient = { from, to }` (vertical two-stop) is defined now; `isRgba` tells the fills apart.
    - `validate.ts` checks text clips: a string value, a box width > 0, a size, line height and weight the layout can use (+1 test). Fixture `makeTextClip`.
    - New `src/text/style.ts` (`style.test.ts`, 5 tests): `DEFAULT_TEXT_STYLE` (Inter 700, 96 px, white, centered; stroke, shadow and box off but preset), `DEFAULT_TEXT_BOX`, `applyTextCase` (title case not after apostrophes), `firstLine`, `isGradient`, `fillColor`, memoized `contentKey` / `styleKey`, `TEXT_LIMITS`.
    - New `src/text/fonts.ts` (`fonts.test.ts`, 7 tests): `fontShorthand` (with the DS body font as fallback), `quoteFamily`, `parseFaceStyle` ("Bold Italic" -> 700 italic), `nearestFace` (CSS font matching order), the project font manifest (`parseFontManifest` / `formatFontManifest`), `fontExtension` (sfnt tag), `usedFamilies`.
  - Engine (`render/text`, unit tested with an approximate measurer):
    - `layout.ts` (`layout.test.ts`, 11 tests): lines (explicit breaks; a fixed box wraps words, breaks words wider than the box between characters, drops the spaces at a wrap), slots `fontSize x lineHeight` with the em box centered, alignment, case, letter spacing (not after the last character), the content box (the block plus the background padding), per-line or block background boxes, glyph bounds per line (measured ink), and the raster rect (backgrounds, ink grown by the stroke, its shadow grown by 1.5 blurs, whole px + 1).
    - `layoutCache.ts`: `textLayout(content, style)` memoized per object pair (WeakMaps), a version bumped by `invalidateTextLayouts` (fonts loaded), the canvas measurer (`ctx.letterSpacing`, `fontKerning`, one `measureText` per run) or an approximate one without OffscreenCanvas, the fallback font from the theme.
    - `raster.ts`: `rasterizeText` (OffscreenCanvas at the scale; font size, spacing, stroke, padding, radius and shadow scaled by hand; lines measured once at that size and aligned; background boxes in one path; stroke drawn twice as wide with its inside cut away; fill solid or a vertical gradient over the text block; one shadow pass of stroke and fill through a scratch canvas; 4096 px cap) and `buildTextAtlas` (words or lines packed, each with stroke, fill and shadow, built for Batch 31).
    - `atlas.ts` (`atlas.test.ts`, 4 tests): `packShelves`, `atlasUnits` (word positions from prefix advances, rects with stroke and shadow).
    - `TextRasterCache.ts` (`TextRasterCache.test.ts`, 9 tests): GPU textures by content + style + scale bucket (`textScaleBucket`: 0.25..4, rounded up to 2^(1/8) steps; mipmaps only when drawn at under 2/3 of the raster), one slot per clip (identity checks: an unchanged clip costs no work), shared rasters for equal texts, a held raster while a font loads, a 128 MB LRU budget that never evicts what this or the last pass drew, re-raster after a lost device, `dropFamily` when project fonts change, `exact()` for Export frame. Stats: rasters, bytes, rasterizations, the clips rasterized by the last render and its time. New rasters use a layout measured now (a font that just loaded may not have reached the cached layouts).
    - `bundledFonts.ts`: 8 OFL variable families (Inter, Montserrat, Nunito, Oswald, Unbounded, Playfair Display, Caveat, JetBrains Mono), latin and latin-ext subsets, upright and italic where the family has one: 34 woff2 files (1.4 MB) in `render/text/fonts/<family>/` with each `OFL.txt`, from the Fontsource 5.3.0 builds; bundled as hashed assets through `import.meta.glob`.
    - `FontLibrary.ts`: installs the bundled FontFaces (unloaded until a text uses them), `source(family)` (bundled / project / system / missing: a family that measures like the generic fallbacks is missing), `ready(style, text)` (`FontFaceSet.check`, starts the load when not), `load`, project faces (`setProjectFaces` / `clearProjectFaces`), change events (loads, project faces).
    - `localFonts.ts` (dynamic import, 0.68 kB chunk): `queryLocalFonts` faces with weight and italic from their style names, grouped by family, cached for the session.
  - Compositor and preview:
    - `drawList.ts`: `TextCompositeLayer` (model of the layout box, text, style, the layer's own scale, its detail).
    - `Compositor.evaluate(..., texts)`: text clips become text layers (layout box matrix, flips mirror inside the box, fades, live texts of a scrub).
    - `LayerTextures`: text layers resolve through the raster cache at the render scale times the layer's scale, drawn over the raster rect with its crop; `resolveExact` (Export frame) rasterizes at project size; `stats.texts`.
    - `detail.ts`: a text layer's detail is its raster cap (4, 4096 px) over its scale, so a zoom re-rasterizes it (§7.1).
    - `PreviewView`: passes the render scale (lowered like the offscreen 4096 px cap) and the panes' view scale for a split; `texts` and `loadFonts` deps; Export frame waits for fonts and lays out again when it had to.
    - `Renderer.uploadImageBitmap` takes an `OffscreenCanvas` too.
  - Canvas (spec §7.2):
    - `layerContent` returns a text's layout box (the gizmo box, Fit / Fill / Center).
    - `canvasLayersAt(..., texts)`: text layers carry `hits`: each line's glyph bounds padded by `TEXT_HIT_PADDING` (4 project px) and the background boxes, flips included; `layersUnder` and marquees use them (`hitQuads`).

- deviations:
  - The text box lives in `TextContent` (`{ value, box }`): §5.2 keeps `TextClip`'s fields as listed and §10.3 keeps the box apart from the style (presets).
  - `Gradient` (`{ from, to }`, vertical) is defined in this batch for text fills; solids still draw plain colors only (Batch 34).
  - Vertical anchor (§10.1 "top/middle/bottom"): there is no fixed box height to align in, so the anchor names the edge that stays in place when the box changes size; the alignment does the same across. Text edits move the position to keep that point; center / middle (the default) grows evenly.
  - Raster scale = the render scale times the layer's own scale (larger axis), rounded up to 2^(1/8) steps, clamped to 0.25..4, then the 4096 px cap (spec: the detail factor clamped 0.25..4). Reason: a title scaled up on the canvas stays sharp. A text layer's detail (§7.1) is that cap over its scale.
  - Glyph hit testing pads by 4 project px and also hits the background boxes; marquees use the same areas.
  - Text layers snap (§7.4) with their content box, as their gizmo; glyph-bound and baseline snapping are a follow-up.
  - The Text section sits right after Clip (§11 lists it after Audio): it is where a text clip is edited.
  - Rasterization runs on the main thread inside the preview render (§3.1 lists the text rasterizer among the main-thread canvas classes; P5 covers media work), so an edit shows in the same frame. Rasters are GPU only; the optional `cache/text/` is not used.
  - System fonts are listed on a click ("Show system fonts": the permission prompt needs a user gesture) and kept for the session; favorites are an app setting.
  - Project fonts: only the face each clip's weight and italic pick is copied (not the whole family), described by `fonts/fonts.json`, registered under the family's name (so it wins over an installed font of that name) while the project is open. Read-only projects copy nothing.
  - Bundled fonts carry the latin and latin-ext subsets only; other scripts draw with the fallback font.
  - Typing in the content area commits per keystroke; keystrokes within 300 ms of each other are one undo step.
  - Stroke "outside": drawn twice as wide with the inside cut away, round joins. The shadow is one pass of the stroked and filled text; the background casts none. The gradient spans the text block. Per-line boxes cover each non-empty line's slot plus the padding; overlapping boxes fill once. Letter spacing is in project px.
  - Fonts load when a text needs them (that text appears a frame or two later); no IdleQueue font preloads (§3.4's example list).
  - The per-word atlas is built but drawn by nothing until Batch 31; backgrounds stay in the layer raster.

### Batch 29: Text UX: one-click titles and subtitles, inline editing, text tool
- status: done

- notes:
  - Engine (unit tested):
    - `render/text/layout.ts`: each `TextLine` has `start` / `end`, its place in the text as drawn (case applied, line breaks included); the spaces a wrap drops sit after `end`.
    - New `render/text/caret.ts` (`caret.test.ts`, 15 tests):
      - Caret stops are grapheme boundaries (`Intl.Segmenter`), measured the way the rasterizer draws: at the raster scale (font size times the scale, divided back), each line aligned by its width at that size as `raster.ts` aligns its runs.
      - A stop's x is where the next grapheme's advance starts, measured with the pair before it so kerning counts, less half the letter spacing.
      - Also: `caseMap` (source and display indices, grapheme by grapheme when a case changes lengths, "ß" upper is "SS"), `caretAt` (downstream at a wrap unless `upstream`), `selectionRects` (line slots, a sliver past a break), `indexAtPoint`, `verticalMove` (goal x), `lineEdge` (Home / End), `wordAt`.
    - `raster.ts`: `TextHighlight` (rects in content px, a CSS color) is drawn between the background boxes and the text; `rasterRect` grows the raster over it.
    - `TextRasterCache.resolve(..., highlight)`: a highlighted raster is the slot's own (no key, never shared, destroyed when the slot draws something else or ends). +1 test.
    - `TextCompositeLayer.highlight` and `LiveText.highlight` carry it through `Compositor.writeText` and `LayerTextures`. +1 test.
    - `PreviewView.textRenderScale`: the device px per project px the last render rasterized text at.
    - `text/style.ts` (`style.test.ts`, +3 tests):

      - `DEFAULT_SUBTITLE_STYLE`: Inter 600, 56 px, line height 1.3, a 70% black box per line (padding 24 / 10, radius 14), bottom anchor; `DEFAULT_SUBTITLE_BOX` is fixed at 900 px.

  - Inline editing: new `render/preview/InlineTextEditor.ts` (`InlineTextEditor.test.ts`, 11 tests, jsdom).
    - The textarea:
      - A transparent `<textarea data-scope="textEditing">` in the preview host, placed over the text block by a CSS matrix (content px to canvas CSS px, flips and turns included). It has the layout's font shorthand, line height, letter spacing, alignment and `pre` / `pre-wrap`.
      - It takes no pointer input and draws nothing (no text, caret, selection color or focus ring). It provides keys, IME, the clipboard and undo of the typing.
      - A capture scroll guard puts back the panels the browser scrolls to show its caret.
    - Draft and display:
      - The draft, selection and composition are the editor's. `live()` gives the draft over the clip's shown text (a field scrub's live values included), its box moved by `keepAnchored` and the selection highlight. It is memoized, so the preview and the canvas caches see stable objects.
      - The caret (blinking `--text-caret-blink` while focused, steady otherwise, hidden with a selection) and the IME underline are a `scene()` for the overlay, computed by `caret.ts`.
    - Keys: Up / Down / Home / End (Shift extends) follow the drawn lines through `caret.ts`, keeping a goal x and the end-of-wrapped-line affinity. Everything else is the textarea's own; `keyup`, `select` and `selectionchange` sync the selection.
    - Pointer: `press` places the caret (Shift extends; a second press within 500 ms and 4 CSS px selects the word, a third everything), `drag` selects, `release`.
    - Ending: `end(commit)` makes one "Edit text" `clip.text` command when the draft differs. A press or focus outside the textarea and the kept areas commits.
    - It also ends when the clip leaves the selection, the playhead leaves the clip or its track hides (committed), and when the clip goes or locks (no command).
  - Canvas (`CanvasEditInput`, `gizmo.ts`, `PreviewOverlayView`; `CanvasEditInput.text.test.ts`, 5 tests):
    - One selected text layer's gizmo has corner and side handles only (`hitGizmo(..., text)`, `scene.textBox`). Corner drags are `textSize` and side drags `textWidth`: live through `CanvasEditInput.texts` and the gesture transforms, then one `clip.text` command ("Resize text" / "Change text box width"). Multi-selections scale as before.

    - New `text/presets.ts` (`presets.test.ts`, 18 tests):
      - Sizes are stored for a 1080 px short side: `presetScale`, `presetLook` (style via `scaleTextStyle`, fixed box width, the position only when `applyPosition`); nothing is scaled on 1080 px projects.
      - `presetFromClip`, `presetUpdatedFromClip` (name, flags and creation kept), `presetDiffers` (style, fixed box width, animations; content and position are the clip's own).
      - `defaultPresetName` ("Oswald 140"), `thumbnailText` (the name, `Aa` over 12 characters), `uniquePresetName`, `duplicatePreset`, `sortPresets`, `searchPresets` (name, tags, family; every word), `favoriteChips` (8: global first), `mergePresets` (newer `updatedAt` wins).
      - Files: `sanitizeTextStyle` / `sanitizePreset` (every value checked, defaults for bad ones), `formatPresetsFile` / `parsePresetsFile` (an export, a list or one preset; newer versions refused), `presetFileName`, `exportFileName`.
    - New `text/starterPresets.ts`: 12 starters in the bundled fonts: Title and Subtitle (Batch 29's defaults, the default presets), Bold outline, Lower third (applies its position), Caption bold, Highlight, Minimal mono, Big number (gradient), Elegant serif, Handwritten, Neon glow, Breaking. Each has a position (the frame center; the Subtitle one line in the lower third), used once Apply position is on.
    - `timeline/edit/text.ts` (`text.test.ts`, +4 tests): `applyPreset` (`clip.applyPreset`, "Apply "Name"": style, box, animations and `presetId` on the unlocked text clips; content, timing and position kept, the position taken when the preset applies it), `linkPreset` (`clip.linkPreset`), `addTitle({ look, label })` (a preset's look, id and default duration; its position or the Title / Subtitle placement), `newTextClip` takes `presetId` and animations.
    - `timeline/edit/dropMedia.ts` (`dropMedia.test.ts`, +2 tests): a drop item is media or a text template (`TextDropItem`): a text clip on the video lane, through the same staging, ghosts, overwrite / insert rules and request.

    - App settings `defaultTitlePreset` / `defaultSubtitlePreset` (the starter ids; null = built-in; +1 test); session `mediaPanel.presetScope` (global / project, in session.json).
  - App (`app/presetController.ts`):
    - `presetLibrary` store: global presets from IndexedDB `textPresets.v1` (the starters put there on the first start), the open project's from `presets/text/` (attached and detached with the project; written while it is writable), the library folder state.
    - Library folder (handle in IndexedDB `presetLibraryFolder.v1`): choosing one merges both ways and writes every global preset as `<id>.json`; later changes are written; on start it syncs when the browser still grants access, else the strip asks for a click (Sync); Stop forgets the folder.
    - Actions: Save as preset (the primary selected text clip's look, a unique name, into the tab's scope, the clip linked: one undo step "Save preset "Name""), Update preset (toast: other clips keep their style until it is applied again), Apply (the selected text clips, else a new clip), Add (`addTitleClip` with the preset's look: at the playhead, edited at once), rename, duplicate, delete, favorite, apply position, default Title / Subtitle (T / Shift+T use them through `setDefaultTitleLook`), import / export (`showOpenFilePicker` / `showSaveFilePicker`, else an input and a download link).
    - Hover: a hovered card shows the preset on the selected text clips through `liveEdit` (texts, and transforms for Apply position); it ends on leave, scroll, a drag, a selection change, a click.
    - Drags: `presetDragSource` for `pressDragCard` (`mediaGestures.ts` now takes any `CardDragSource`): over the timeline the media drop ghosts, released there one "Add clip" command; over the canvas a new clip at the playhead centered on the point.

- deviations:
  - Project presets are files in `presets/text/<id>.json` (spec §9.7 and the Build), not entries of `Project.textPresetsLocal` (§5.2, kept and always empty): a preset library is not document editing, so like the global presets they are outside the undo history. Save as preset's link (`presetId`) and Apply are commands.
  - Preset sizes are stored for a 1080 px short side and scale with the project (Batch 29's defaults did so): a preset looks the same on a 4K project. A fixed box width scales by the same factor (Batch 29 sized the Subtitle's box from the frame width: on 16:9 the default subtitle box is now 900 px, was 1600).
  - `TextPreset` adds `applyPosition` (the spec's "apply position" option) and `updatedAt` (the library folder sync). `defaultDuration` is whole milliseconds (presets cross projects of any fps); nothing sets it yet.
  - Applying a preset replaces the box (auto / fixed width) with the style: the box is part of the look (§10.3 stores it).
  - Apply keeps the clip's position as it is (X / Y unchanged), not the anchored edge, unless the preset applies its position.
  - New clips from a preset (chips, a card with no text clip selected, a drop) say "Title" and are edited at once like `+ Title`; they use the Title placement (40 px under a selected text clip), or the preset's position. Shift+T keeps the Subtitle placement with the default Subtitle preset.
  - Save as preset names are made unique within their scope ("Name 2"); the preset goes into the tab's scope (global when the project is read-only or none is open).
  - Default Title / Subtitle are app settings by preset id; a missing one (deleted, or a closed project's) falls back to the built-in look. Choosing the default again turns it off (built-in).
  - The library folder sync is a union by id where the newer `updatedAt` wins; a preset deleted on one machine comes back from another machine's copy. It runs on start (when the browser keeps the access) and on Sync; it lives in a strip at the bottom of the Global scope until the settings panel (Batch 42).
  - Import puts presets into the shown scope; a preset with a known id replaces it (an export imported again changes nothing).
  - The Presets header (§17) keeps New from selection, Import and Export as icon buttons; the Global / Project toggle and the search are a tool row under it (the media panel header is too narrow for five controls next to the tabs).
  - Rename is in the card menu and edits in place; a double-click on a card applies twice (click = apply), so it does not rename.
  - The starters are seeded into the global presets once (first start), then the user's to change or delete; there is no restore yet (follow-up).

- review: rejected
  1. Preset card thumbnails are drawn outside the `FrameScheduler`. This breaks spec §3.4 and P3, both BINDING ("Nothing renders outside this loop", "All canvases render only when invalidated, through the single scheduler"), and no deviation is recorded for it. `src/panels/media/PresetsTab.tsx:67-80` (`PresetThumb`) calls `drawPresetThumbnail` (`src/render/text/presetThumbnails.ts:42-54`) straight from a `ResizeObserver` callback, once per card, and again from the effect on every preset or `fontsVersion` change. That call lays the text out, rasterizes it and draws it into the card's on-screen canvas. Every other on-screen canvas draws in the scheduler loop: the timeline, the preview overlay, the meters, and the Media tab's cards through `PosterPainter` (`src/panels/media/PosterPainter.ts:29`, `register("mediaThumbs", ...)`). In practice, opening the tab rasterizes every card at once in one observer pass. A splitter drag that resizes the grid re-rasterizes every visible card at each new size, outside the scheduler's one-render-per-frame rule. Fix:
     - Draw the thumbnails through a painter registered with the scheduler, as the Media tab does. The observer and the preset or font changes only record the canvas's size and preset, then call `scheduler.invalidate(...)` (for example `mediaThumbs`). `render()` draws each dirty card once per frame.
     - Add a unit test in the style of `PosterPainter.test.ts`: a burst of size changes draws once per frame, and a detached canvas is no longer drawn.
  2. `src/panels/properties/TextSection.tsx:49` still says `TODO(batch 30): Save as preset.` Save as preset is built (the quick row in `QuickActions.tsx`, and the Presets header), so this hook is stale and points at a finished batch. Remove it.
  - Not blocking (worth fixing with 1): see `src/app/presetController.ts:267-285` (`attachPresets`) and `:117-139` (`commit`). A project preset saved or imported before `attachPresets` has finished reading `presets/text/` is added to the empty list. The queued write then runs with a writer that already `know`s the files just read. It writes only the new preset and deletes the files of all the others. The read's `setLibrary({ project: ... })` (`:280`) also drops the new preset from the tab. The window is short (one folder read after a project opens), but the result is deleted preset files. Fix: make project commits wait for the read, or build the list inside the queued write from what the read found.
  - Checked and fine:
    - `npm run check` is green on my run: typecheck, lint plus the CSS color check, 1453 unit tests in 146 files, 3 perf tests, and a build of 831.49 kB JS (268.47 kB gzip) and 68.06 kB CSS, as the entry says.

      - `text.test.ts`: `applyPreset` keeps content, timing and position; `addTitle` with a preset's look; `linkPreset`.
      - `dropMedia.test.ts`: text drops. `presetFiles.test.ts`: the folder writer.
      - The UI paths are pending manual checks 1-5, with exact steps.
      - The Update tooltip (`UpdatePresetButton` in `QuickActions.tsx`) says what acceptance 2 requires: other clips keep their style until the preset is applied again.
    - Nothing from later batches was built:
      - Animations are opaque `TextAnim` values, copied as they are (Batch 31).
      - `applyPreset` takes text clips only (captions are Batch 32).
      - The library folder strip stands in for the settings panel (Batch 42), and that is recorded as a deviation.
    - No color, font or size literals. The new CSS uses tokens only (1px hairlines, as elsewhere), `--preset-chip-max-width` is in `tokens.css`, and the starter colors are content `RGBA` values (spec §10.3).
    - §3 and §4 otherwise hold:
      - The hover preview is ephemeral, through `liveEdit`. The entry measures 0 React commits, and the inline editor's draft stays on top (`liveTexts` in `previewController.ts`).
      - Apply, Save as preset's link and a card drop are one command each.
      - The toolbar chips select a string, so the toolbar renders only when the chips change.
      - `defaultDuration` becomes whole frames through `usToFrame`.
    - Every new TODO has a batch tag. This entry had no earlier rejection.
- fix-attempt: done (2026-10-16)
  1. Preset card thumbnails draw in the FrameScheduler loop (spec §3.4, P3):
    - New `src/panels/media/PresetThumbPainter.ts`, framework-free like `PosterPainter`, registered on `mediaThumbs`. `show(canvas, preset)`, `resize(canvas, w, h)` and `redrawAll()` (fonts) only record the card and call `scheduler.invalidate("mediaThumbs")`. `render()` draws each dirty card once, at its latest preset and size. A card with no size yet (or a hidden one, 0 x 0) is not drawn. `detach(canvas)` drops a card and its pending draw.
    - The instance is `presetThumbs` in `presetController.ts`. Its draw function calls `drawPresetThumbnail` with the device pixel ratio and margin read at draw time. A `fontsVersion` change calls `presetThumbs.redrawAll()` (subscribed in `installPresetController`).
    - `PresetThumb` (`PresetsTab.tsx`) draws nothing itself. Its ResizeObserver hands the size to `presetThumbs.resize`, an effect hands the preset to `presetThumbs.show`, and unmounting detaches the canvas. It no longer subscribes to `fontsVersion`, so a font load no longer re-renders every card through React.
    - New `PresetThumbPainter.test.ts` (5 tests), in the style of `PosterPainter.test.ts`:
      - A burst of sizes on two cards draws nothing outside the frame, then once each at the last size.
      - Nothing is drawn until both the preset and a size are known, and a hidden card is skipped.
      - A changed preset draws again, and `redrawAll` draws every card once.
      - A detached card is not drawn, even with a draw pending.
      - `dispose` unregisters.
  2. `src/panels/properties/TextSection.tsx`: the stale `TODO(batch 30): Save as preset.` is removed. No `TODO(batch 30)` is left in `src`.
  3. (non-blocking item) The project preset race in `presetController.ts`:
    - The read in `attachPresets` now merges what it found with the presets already in the list (`mergePresets`, the newer copy of an id wins). A preset saved or imported during the read stays in the tab.
    - The queued project write (`commit`) writes the list as it is when the write runs (`list("project")`), not the snapshot taken at commit time. The write after the read therefore holds the files just read and adds the new one, instead of deleting the others.
    - New `src/app/presetController.test.ts`, with the services mock of `projectController.test.ts`. It gates the project root's folder lookups so the read is pending, imports a preset into the Project scope, then opens the gate. The tab and `presets/text/` must end with all three presets. The test fails on the old code (the tab shows `[a, b]`) and passes with the fix.

### Batch 31: Text animations
- status: done

- notes:
  - Model (unit tested):
    - `TextAnim` in `core/document/types.ts`: `id` (the 12 of §10.4, `TEXT_ANIM_IDS`), `duration` (frames), `perUnit` (char / word / line), `stagger` (frames), `ease`. `PresetTextAnim`: the same in milliseconds, for presets.
    - New `text/anim.ts` (`anim.test.ts`, 15 tests):
      - Per animation: chip label, unit (block, char, word, line), own ease, first length (`TEXT_ANIMS`). Eases `TEXT_EASES`: linear, easeIn, easeOut, easeInOut. An out animation's own ease out becomes ease in.
      - `activeAnim`: the in animation from the clip's first frame (progress 0: nothing shown yet, as fades) and the out one to its last (progress 1). `animLength` caps each at half the clip, so they never overlap; under 2 frames nothing plays. Animations the engine cannot play (no id, no whole-frame duration) are ignored (`isPlayable`).
      - Units: the duration is the whole animation. Unit i starts `stagger` frames after unit i - 1 and plays `D - (n - 1) * stagger`. A stagger over D / n is cut to it; none gives D / (n + 1.5) (each unit overlaps 1.5 others). Out animations play the units last first. A typewriter types by count (`typedCount`) and erases from the end.
      - Shapes (`writeUnitShape`) from the eased presence `a` (1 = at rest):
        - fade and wordFade: opacity.
        - Slides: 0.6 em of travel. In comes from the far side, out leaves in the named direction (slideUp out moves up).
        - pop and wordPop: a back-out scale from 0.4, opacity reaching 1 by a third of the way.
        - scaleBounce: from 0 with two damped bounces.
        - lineReveal: slides a line's height inside its place (masked).
        - blurIn: a Gaussian blur of 0.2 em at the start, and the opacity.
      - `newTextAnim` keeps the previous animation's duration, stagger and ease. Also `sanitizeTextAnim` / `sanitizePresetAnim`, `toPresetAnim` / `fromPresetAnim` (ms <-> frames through `time.ts`; 29.97 rounds back to the same frames) and `sameAnim`.
    - New `timeline/edit/textAnim.ts` (`textAnim.test.ts`, 3 tests): `setTextAnims` (`clip.animation`, one undo step, coalescing key; null removes; locked, non-text and unchanged clips skipped; affects `clips` for the badge) and `animEdits` (per clip from its own animation).

    - `render/text/atlas.ts` (+2 tests): `char` units (graphemes, spaces left out), each unit's `offset` in its line and its middle (`originX/Y`, what a pop scales about); `lineStops` (each line's grapheme boundaries in content px).
    - `raster.ts`:
      - `rasterizeText(..., part)`: `backgrounds` draws the background boxes alone over the same rect.
      - `buildTextAtlas` draws each unit where the layer raster draws it: its line aligned at the raster size, its prefix measured at it. A text at rest looks the same from either.
    - New `render/text/animUnits.ts`: the units and stops cached per layout object (the compositor allocates nothing per frame).
    - `TextRasterCache` (+4 tests):
      - Parts besides the raster: `resolveAtlas` (a cell crop and rect per unit) and `resolveBackground`, keyed apart. `ResolvedText` gives `scale` (texture px per content px) and `units`.
      - `warm(clipId, part, ...)` makes a part ahead of time; its slot keeps it while passes warm it.
      - `exact(..., part)` for Export frame.
      - A clip's own raster slot is still keyed by the clip id alone.
    - `Compositor`:
      - Text layers carry `anim: TextAnimFrame | null`: `block` (one state moving the layer raster), or an atlas kind with one state per unit and the background opacity (the leading unit's).
      - A typewriter's characters use the line atlas, cut at the last typed grapheme (`cut`), so the glyphs are the static text's exactly.
      - A text edited inline (`LiveText.editing`) shows at rest. `evaluate(..., anims)` takes live animations (a field scrub).
      - `upcomingTexts(doc, frame, reach)` lists the text clips showing in the window and the parts they draw.
    - `LayerTextures`: a block animation draws the raster moved (scale about the block's middle, offset, opacity, blur in texture px); a per-unit one draws the background raster, then a pooled texture layer per cell. A masked line is cropped to its place; a cut line is cropped at its x. Export frame does the same with exact rasters. `resolve(..., upcoming)` warms the window's parts: all while idle, one per pass while playing or scrubbing (then it asks for another pass).
    - `TextureLayer.blur` (sigma, texture px); `DrawListSnapshot` compares it.
    - `WebGpuRenderer`: a blurred record is blurred first, in the draw's command encoder. Two passes of a separable Gaussian (`BLUR_WGSL`): horizontal into a pooled texture, then vertical into another; sigma is capped at 16 texture px (`MAX_BLUR_SIGMA`, 3 sigma reach). It is then drawn from the second texture with its quad grown by the reach. Pooled textures go in 64 px steps and are freed after 120 unused draws; the uniforms use their own 256-byte-slot buffer.
    - `PreviewView`: `anims` dep (live animations); text clips within `TEXT_LOOKAHEAD_SECONDS` (5 s) of the playhead are warmed.

- deviations:
  - Duration semantics (§10.4 `duration`, `stagger`): the duration is the whole animation, the units' delays included, so the field reads what plays. Without a stagger the units spread over it (each overlapping 1.5 others); a longer stagger than duration / units is cut.
  - "Clamped to half the clip duration when needed": each animation plays over at most half the clip (in and out never overlap), at playback. The stored duration stays as typed (a later trim or extend needs no rewrite), and the section shows a hint.
  - Out animations play the units last first (a typewriter erases from the end) and keep their names' direction (§10.4: slideUp out moves up and fades). Their default ease is the mirror of the in one (ease out -> ease in).
  - Easing ids are `linear`, `easeIn`, `easeOut`, `easeInOut`. An animation without one uses its own (Auto in the section); `EaseId` stays a string until Batch 35.
  - Whole-text animations (fade, slides, pop, blurIn, scaleBounce) move the layer raster, backgrounds included; the per-word and per-line ones use the atlas (§10.1).
    - Under per-unit animations the background boxes are a raster of their own, at the leading unit's opacity, not moved (the atlas leaves backgrounds out, §10.1). Shadows are per unit, so overlapping shadows of neighboring words darken a little while they animate.
    - A typewriter reveals graphemes by count, spaces included, with no fade. Its characters are cut out of the line atlas cells, so the glyphs (kerning, strokes) are exactly the static text's; per-char atlas cells would let a thick stroke overlap the previous letter.
    - `perUnit: "char"` on other animations uses character cells (model only: the section does not choose units; the word and line variants are their own chips).
  - Shapes: slides travel 0.6 font sizes; pop goes from 0.4 with an overshoot; bounce from 0 with two damped bounces. The blur starts at 0.2 font sizes, capped at 16 texture px in the renderer (§10.4 "cap the blur radius").
  - Presets store animation times in milliseconds (`PresetTextAnim`), as `defaultDuration` does; they come back in the project's frames.
  - Starter animations (Lower third, Caption bold, Neon glow, Breaking). Starters stored before this batch and never changed take them on load (`upgradeStarters`, date kept).
  - Preview on click: an out animation plays from 10 frames before it to the clip's end (§10.4 names the in case). Choosing the active chip again previews without a command; None removes without a preview.
    - Duration, stagger and easing commits replay the animation, so a change shows at once even with the playhead off the clip. A label scrub shows live at the playhead.
    - A chip or field during inline editing commits the edit first.
  - Durations are shown in seconds (two decimals, a frame per step) and stored in frames.
  - Pre-rasterization (P11 "pre-rasterizes per word/line once"): text clips within 5 s of the playhead get their raster, atlas and background parts ahead: all at once while idle, one per pass while playing or scrubbing. So playing into an animation rasterizes nothing; a clip more than 5 s ahead of where playback started is rasterized during playback, before it shows.
  - A text edited inline shows at rest; the gizmo, canvas hit testing and snapping use the text at rest.
  - Animations that cannot play (from older builds or files) are ignored at evaluation rather than reported by `validateProject`; preset files are sanitized.
  - The Animation section follows Text (§11 lists it after Text).

- deviations:
  - Caption track data (§5.2 "style + cue ids"): `captionTracks[trackId]` holds the style only; the cue ids are the track's `clipIds`, so the order and membership have one source of truth. A caption track without data draws in the default style.
  - Cue selection (§3.3 kind `cue`): cues are selected as clips (kind `clips`), so move, trim, delete, split, label and the Clip section work on them unchanged; the `cue` kind stays in the type (session files) and is never made.
  - Word timings are frames relative to the cue's start (as keyframes), so a moved cue keeps them; in trims re-base them and words outside the new span are kept (a trim back shows them again).
  - "No overwrite and no push on this track" (§10.5): an overwrite move or a nudge of cues stops at the cues that stay; an Alt-drag copy goes to the nearest free spot no further than the copied block's length from the drop, else the drop is refused (`occupied`, red ghost); a dragged cue's trims are always regular (Ripple mode and Mod ignored). Insert moves (Mod) and ripples started on other tracks (ripple trims, ripple delete, Q / W) still shift the caption track like any other unlocked track, splitting a cue that crosses the insert point, so captions stay in sync with the picture.
  - Splits: Enter splits by the share of characters (§10.5); when the cue has word timings on both sides it splits at the first right word's start instead. A timeline split (razor, Mod+K) cuts the text where the first right word starts, or at the space nearest the frame's share of the characters; a single word stays whole on both sides. Merges join the texts with a space.
  - Cue list keys (§10.5 lists Enter, Mod+Backspace, Delete, Tab): Shift+Enter inserts a line break; Shift+Tab goes to the previous cue; Esc puts the text back and leaves the field (the Number field's Esc); blur commits. Typing is a live draft (`liveEdit.cues`, shown on the canvas at once) committed as one "Edit caption" step, not one step per key.
  - `+ Cue at playhead`: when the playhead is inside a cue the new cue starts at its end (and after the cues touching it), and it is at most 2 s, up to the next cue; it reads "Caption", selected in the list (typing replaces it, as `+ Title`).
  - Import (§10.5 "create cues"): the file's cues replace the track's cues (one undo step; the toast counts the replaced ones); times go to the nearest frame (at least one frame long); a cue starting inside the previous one cuts it there, two starting on the same frame become one (their texts on two lines). VTT inline timestamps (karaoke) are read as word timings. Export: one button; SRT, or VTT when the chosen name ends in `.vtt` (the save picker offers both); times to the nearest ms; empty cues are left out.
  - Caption layout (§10.5 max width, max lines): a cue keeps an auto box up to the max width (its background fits the text), wraps at the max width beyond it, and is drawn smaller (10% steps, down to half size) when it has more lines than the max.
  - Positions: Bottom puts the caption's bottom edge at 78% of the frame height (the Subtitle's place), Top its top edge at 18%, Center its middle at the center, Custom its middle at Y (project px from the center). Choosing Custom starts it where the preset showed a one-line caption.
  - Word highlight (§10.5 "draws the active word from the atlas"): the other words take the inactive color in every mode; Color and Both draw the active word in the highlight color; Box puts a box in the highlight color behind it (square corners until Batch 34's shapes), the word in the text's own fill; Scale and Both grow it 1.15 x about its middle. The cue is drawn from two word atlases (the other words' look and the active word's) over its background boxes. Between words, and while its text is being typed, nothing is highlighted.
  - The Caption style section shows for a selection with cues and for a selected caption track, after Clip (or Track); it has no vertical anchor (captions sit at their position). Style (the Captions header) selects the caption track unless cues are selected, opens the section, scrolls to it and focuses it.
  - Applying a preset to the caption track (Apply or hover with cues or the track selected and no text clip) replaces its text style only: position, max width, lines and highlight stay; the preset's box width is not used.
  - Clear all asks nothing (§0 one click); Undo brings the cues back.
  - Cue list virtualization (P1 "no React renders on scrolling"): the list renders the rows in view and a block around them, and renders again when the view crosses a block of 16 rows, not on every scroll step; the cue under the playhead is marked through the DOM, so playback renders nothing. The row whose text has the focus stays rendered while the list scrolls away from it (its field keeps the focus and the draft), and a row that goes away while its text is edited (the Media panel's tab switch, its cue removed) commits the text (added by the fix-attempt).
  - Caption cues are not on the canvas (no selection or gizmo; Batch 53 adds it).

- review: rejected
  1. A cue's typed text is lost, and the preview keeps showing it, when its row unmounts while it is being edited. This breaks acceptance 2 (the canvas shows text the document never gets) and P2 (the ephemeral draft is never committed or cleared). In `src/panels/media/CaptionsTab.tsx:65-149` (`CueRow`), the draft is committed only by `onBlur` (`:137-141`) and the Enter / Mod+Backspace / Tab / Esc keys. There is no cleanup when the row unmounts, and `onBlur` does not run when the focused textarea is removed. Two ordinary actions remove it:
     - Scrolling the list: the virtualized slice (`CaptionsTab.tsx:265-267`) drops a row more than one block of 16 rows outside the view.
     - Switching the media panel tab: `src/panels/MediaPanel.tsx:23` unmounts `CaptionsTab`, and the PanelTabs buttons prevent mousedown, so the field never blurs.
     - In both cases `liveEdit.cues` (set by `draftCue`, `src/app/captionController.ts:78-80`) stays set. The compositor draws the draft (`Compositor.writeCaption` reads `live.texts`) while the document keeps the old text, with no undo step. This lasts until another cue is typed into. Export (Batch 43) would render the document's text, so the output would differ from the preview.

  1. A cue's typed text is no longer lost when its row unmounts while it is edited (`src/panels/media/CaptionsTab.tsx`):
    - `CueRow` keeps the typed, uncommitted text in a ref (`pending`). It is set on every change and cleared by blur, Enter (split), Mod+Backspace (merge), Tab and Esc. An effect cleanup keyed on the cue's id and on whether the cue still exists commits a pending text with `commitCue(id, text)`. So when the field goes away with no blur (the Media panel's tab switch unmounts the list, or the cue is removed while it is typed into), the text becomes one "Edit caption" step and `liveEdit.cues` is cleared. A removed cue's draft is just dropped (`setCueText` gives no command, the live text is cleared).
    - The row whose text has the focus stays rendered outside the virtualized slice (`editing`, set by the list's focus / blur of a text field). Scrolling far away therefore keeps the field, its caret and the live draft, and typing goes on. The kept row is placed first among the rows, so React never moves its node (a move would blur it).

    - New `media/transcribe/resample.ts` (`resample.test.ts`, 5 tests): windowed-sinc resampling (Blackman, 16 zero crossings, a table of 128 steps per sample), cutoff at 90% of the lower Nyquist: speech bands keep their level and pitch, 9-20 kHz are below -50 dB at 16 kHz; a minute of 48 kHz converts in about 0.3 s.
    - New `audio/mixdown.ts` (`mixdown.test.ts`, 5 tests): `renderMixdown(project, range, { sampleRate, channels })`, the timeline's audio mix of a frame range rendered by the playback code itself (`AudioScheduler` voices -> `AudioMixer` track gains with mute/solo -> mix bus) on an `OfflineAudioContext`: the segments the range plays are loaded first and held while rendering, a stand-in clock steps the scheduler through the range, context times run 50 ms ahead (no late voice), the monitor volume stays out. `heardClips`. - deviations:
  - Transcribe opens a dialog (spec §0 "one click"): the first run downloads 120-590 MB and the language matters, so the model's size and cache status, the language and the range are shown first; Enter starts with the remembered choices.
  - Review step (Goal) = the confirmation of §10.6: the result is always reviewed before it goes in (Add N captions, or Replace N cues when the range has cues); Discard or Esc drops it. Nothing is dispatched before, so a cancel or a discard leaves the project unchanged.
  - Replacing (§10.6 "replacing cues in the range"): every cue overlapping the range is replaced, also one that crosses the range's edge (the review counts them; Undo brings them back).
  - The mix (§10.6 "16 kHz mono from an OfflineAudioContext") renders at 48 kHz mono; the worker resamples it to 16 kHz with a windowed sinc. Chrome's buffer sources resample by linear interpolation, which folds 8-24 kHz into the speech band.
  - Language auto-detect: transformers.js has none (it assumes English); the worker detects it with one decoder step on the first 30 s.
  - Word times are moved 0.15 s earlier (`WORD_LEAD_US`): Whisper's cross-attention word starts trailed the speech by a median 0.20 s (voice 1) and 0.17 s (voice 2), measured against the synthesizer's word positions. After the shift the median lag is 0.03 s.
  - Lines per cue follow the caption track's max lines (§10.6 says max 2; the default style has 2), about 32 characters per line.
  - The ONNX Runtime WASM (26.9 MB, asyncify build) is bundled as a hashed asset instead of transformers.js's default jsDelivr URL: no third-party CDN at run time, and the app works offline once a model is cached.
  - Speed (P14 has no transcription budget): Base on WebGPU transcribes 59 s in about 30 s on this laptop (~0.5 x realtime), Tiny in ~20 s. ONNX Runtime's WebGPU decoding costs about 65-100 ms per token here (fp32 and q4 decoders alike, warm or cold); WASM runs single-threaded (the app is not cross-origin isolated), Tiny in ~16 s.
  - The progress toast is not updated while playback runs (P1: no React commits while playing); it catches up when playback stops.
  - (fix-attempt) Line widths are counted in columns, a wide character (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) as two (§10.6 "max ~32 chars per line" counts Latin characters): about 16 CJK characters per line, which fits the caption box like 32 Latin ones. - review: rejected
  1. Chinese, Japanese, Thai, Lao and Burmese captions get a space between every piece of text. The dialog offers these languages, and auto-detect picks them.
     - The cause: transformers.js 4.3.1 cuts these five languages into pieces with no spaces (`node_modules/@huggingface/transformers/src/models/whisper/tokenization_whisper.js:501-503`, `combineTokensIntoWords` -> `splitTokensOnUnicode`). In every other language, a word chunk starts with a space (`splitTokensOnSpaces`).
     - `wordsFromChunks` (`src/text/transcript.ts:51`) trims each chunk and so loses that space. `cueText` (`:157`) then joins every piece with " ", and `lineBreaks` / `widthOf` (`:91`, `:117`) count a space between every two pieces.
     - Reproduced page-side with `%TEMP%/b33/rev_cjk.mjs` (`wordsFromChunks` + `cuesFromWords` on chunks shaped like the library's). Japanese gives "今日 は いい 天気 です ね。" and "パスタ を 作り ましょう。". Chinese gives "我们 今天 做 意大利 面。". English (" Welcome", " to", ...) gives "Welcome to the editor.", as it should.
     - Fix: keep on each timed word whether its chunk began with whitespace. Put a space before a piece only when it did, and count line widths the same way. `wordRanges` (`src/text/captions.ts:107`) searches with `indexOf`, so the highlight still finds pieces with no spaces between them. Add unit tests with chunk texts as the library gives them for ja/zh and for en.
  2. When two transcribed cues land on the same frame, they are merged into one, and the second cue's word timings are lost.
     - When a word ends a sentence with zero length and the next word starts at the same time, `cuesFromWords` (`src/text/transcript.ts:206-208`) gives the first cue 1 µs. Whisper's alignment does produce zero-length words, and `wordsFromChunks` keeps equal starts (`:76`).
     - `transcribedCues` (`src/timeline/edit/captions.ts:346`) passes the cues to `cuesFromSubtitles`. That function joins two cues on the same start frame and keeps only the first cue's words (`captions.ts:272-275`).
     - The result: the merged cue's other words have no timing, so the highlight never lights them. The merged text can also have more lines than the style's max (a 1-line cue plus a 2-line cue = 3 lines).
     - Reproduced with `%TEMP%/b33/rev_merge.mjs`. The chunks " Yes." [1.0, 1.0], " Okay" [1.0, 1.3], " let's" [1.3, 1.5], " go." [1.5, 1.9] give the cues "Yes." (850000-850001 µs) and "Okay let's go.". They are placed as one cue, "Yes.\nOkay let's go.", with one word timing ("Yes.").
     - Fix: transcribed cues should never share a frame. Either give a phrase too short to stand alone to the next cue when they fit together in max lines (in `cuesFromWords`), or have `transcribedCues` move a colliding cue to the next free frame instead of merging it. Add a test with zero-length words.
  - Not blocking:
    - `startTranscription` returns early on a locked caption track (`src/app/transcribeController.ts:152-155`) and on an empty timeline (`:156-159`) without `workerPool.stop("transcribe")`. The worker that the dialog's status request started stays alive with transformers.js loaded until the next run ends (P13).
    - Whisper Base on WebGPU is not deterministic on this laptop. I ran Base nine times on the same 59 s mix. One run (my first `acc1.mjs`, right after `acc2.mjs`) heard 155 words, with word starts 4-6 frames later: median lag 0.184 s against the synthesizer, p90 0.328 s. That fails acc1's 0.1 s check. The other eight runs gave 156 words with "Welcome" at 0.270 s, as in the build run (median lag 0.029 s). So on some runs the highlight can trail the voice by about 0.2 s; worth a line in the docs. The mix itself is exact: the speech starts at 0.1383 s in both the mix and the WAV (`rev_mix.mjs`). Detecting the language or giving it makes no difference (`rev_mix2.mjs`, `rev_ctrl.mjs`).

- fix-attempt: done (2026-10-17)
  1. Chinese, Japanese, Thai, Lao and Burmese captions no longer get a space between every piece (`src/text/transcript.ts`):
    - `wordsFromChunks` keeps on each timed word whether its chunk began with whitespace: a chunk without a leading space is `attached: true` to the word before it (`TimedWord` now extends `SubtitleWord` with the optional flag; English chunks, which all start with a space, give no flag).
    - `lineBreaks`, `phraseCues` and `cueText` take words with that flag (`CueWord`). They put a space before a word only when it is not attached and count line widths the same way (`widthOf`, `joinWords`). A space Whisper did write stays ("これは iPhoneです。").
    - Line widths are in columns: a wide character (Han, kana, Hangul, CJK punctuation, full-width forms) counts two, so a line holds about 16 Chinese or Japanese characters instead of 32 (32 would be twice as wide as an English line, past the caption box's 900 px wrap width at the default 64 px size).
    - The cue words stored in the document are plain `{ text, startUs, endUs }` (the flag stays in the transcript). `wordRanges` finds pieces with no spaces between them, so the highlight works.
    - Tests (`transcript.test.ts`, +6): the review's ja/zh/en chunk shapes ("今日はいい天気ですね。", "パスタを作りましょう。", "我们今天做意大利面。", "Welcome to the editor."), the attached flags, the column widths (16 wide characters per line, "abcd ef"), a long Japanese sentence in two cues of lines of at most 16 characters, every piece found by `wordRanges`.
  2. Transcribed cues no longer share a frame, so no cue is merged and no word timing is lost:
    - `cuesFromWords` (`src/text/transcript.ts`): a cue the next one would leave on screen for less than `MIN_ALONE_US` (0.2 s) joins the next one when they fit together in the style's max lines. The review's " Yes." [1.0, 1.0] + " Okay let's go." now gives one cue "Yes. Okay let's go." with its 4 word timings. 0.2 s is too short to read, and it is at least 4 frames at 23.976 fps, so cues further apart never round to one frame.
    - `transcribedCues` (`src/timeline/edit/captions.ts`): when cues still land on one frame (a short cue that does not fit with the next one), the later cue moves to the frame after the one before it, with its words (relative to its new start), instead of going through the import's merge in `cuesFromSubtitles`. The import keeps its rule (two SRT cues on one start frame become one).
    - Tests: `transcript.test.ts` (the zero-length words joined; a pair that does not fit one line stays apart), `captions.test.ts` (+1: two cues on frame 30 placed at 30 and 31 with all their word timings; three on one frame at 30, 31, 32; Whisper's chunks end to end).
  3. (non-blocking item) `startTranscription` stops the transcribe worker on its early returns too (a locked caption track, an empty timeline), so the worker the dialog's status request started does not stay alive with transformers.js loaded (P13).
  4. (non-blocking item) Whisper Base on WebGPU is not deterministic here (on one of the reviewer's nine runs the word starts trailed by about 0.2 s): added to the docs note.

- notes:
  - Model (no schema change: §5.2's `SolidClip` already has every field): `SOLID_SHAPE_IDS` / `SolidShape` in `types.ts`; `validate.ts` checks solids (a known shape, a positive size, a radius >= 0, a color or a two-stop gradient; `validate.test.ts` +1). Images show their picture for any length (a still holds it, an animation loops).
  - Solid edits, new `timeline/edit/solid.ts` (`solid.test.ts`, 8 tests): `addSolid` (`clip.addSolid` "Add solid": a white rounded rectangle 60% x 30% of the frame's short side, 5% corners, centered, 5 s at the playhead on the top video track when it is free there, unlocked and shown, else on a new track above), `setSolids` (`clip.solid`: shape, fill, size, radius and the transform a size handle drag moves; whole px within `SOLID_LIMITS`; one undo step, arrow steps coalesce; redraws the timeline only when the shape or fill change), `withShape` (a box turned into a line gets 1/135 of the short side as thickness, a line turned back half its length as height), `drawnRadius` (rounded rects and line ends, at most half the shorter side). `layerContent` gives every shape its size's box (gradients and ellipses included).
  - Drawing (spec §9.4 "solids to geometry"): `SolidLayer` gains `to` (a gradient's bottom color) and `shape` (`SolidGeometry`: box or ellipse, size, radius). `SOLID_WGSL` mixes the vertical gradient premultiplied and cuts the shape by its signed distance in the layer's own px (rounded box; ellipse by f / |grad f|), anti-aliased over one screen px with `fwidth`; `WebGpuRenderer` grows a shaped quad by one target px (UV past 0..1) so the edge's outer half is drawn. Layer uniforms grow to 8 vec4 (128 bytes, the 256-byte stride is unchanged). `Compositor.writeSolid` draws every shape and gradient (flips mirror the fill), with the live looks of a field scrub or a size drag (new `evaluate` parameter `solids`). `DrawListSnapshot` compares the gradient and shape. The caption word highlight box is now a pill (`CaptionHighlightFrame.box.radius`, half its height).
  - Animated images (spec §9.1, §9.3): new `media/decode/animation.ts` (`animation.test.ts`, 6 tests: the browsers' 20 ms / 100 ms frame rule shared with the probe, `keptFrames` within a byte budget, `frameAt`, `loopTimeUs`, `imageTimeUs`) and `media/decode/animatedImage.ts` in decode.worker: `decodeAnimation` reads the durations, keeps the frames whose textures fit 128 MB (every k-th past it), at most 2048 px, and posts each as a transferable bitmap after the kept start times; `animationStrip` makes the timeline's filmstrip (up to 48 frames, 144 px tall). `ImageService` keeps one pooled texture per kept frame keyed by its start time (`frameKey(mediaId, timeUs)`), redraws the preview as frames arrive (`onChange`), decodes again only the frames the pool let go of, and `release`s a removed media (textures, frame list). The compositor's image time is the clip's in point plus the elapsed time, looped; `LayerTextures` draws the frame at that time (holding the last one while a frame loads; Export frame waits for all of them). An in trim moves an animated image's `in` with the edge (wrapped).
  - SVG (spec §7.1 detail): an SVG counts as vector in the source detail (`vectorDetailSize`: its raster can reach the 4096 px cap), so zooming renders finer; `LayerTextures` rasterizes it again at rest at the size it is drawn at (`vectorLongEdge`, half-octave steps) when its raster is under 0.9x or over 2x that size (`ImageService.refine` replaces the pool texture; a load never shrinks a refined raster). `detail.test.ts` +2, `ImageService.test.ts` +3, `LayerTextures.test.ts` +2.
  - App: new `app/graphicsController.ts`: `add.solid` (`+ Solid`, selected after) and `add.image` (`+ Image`: `importFromPicker` with images only, then placed like a canvas drop at the playhead, centered and fitted, 5 s, in the import's undo step "Add image"); `editSolids` / `previewSolids` (live: `liveEdit.solids`). Both toolbar buttons enabled.

Number fields scrub live outside React; a color dragged in the picker shows live.

  - Gradient fills are vertical two-stop gradients (the Batch 28 `Gradient` type, as text fills), over the solid's box and turning with it; flips mirror them. No angle: the type is shared with text and the batch asks for "solid or two-stop gradient".

Choosing Line makes the solid 1/135 of the short side thick (8 px at 1080), leaving Line half its length tall; otherwise a 648 x 324 box would become a fat bar.
  - Animated images always loop from the clip's in point (GIFs that play once in a browser loop too: a sticker on a short is expected to keep moving). An in trim moves `in` with the edge (wrapped into one loop) so the frames left keep playing as they did; splits continue the animation; images still have no slip, speed or media bounds.
  - Memory (Build "capped memory, lower fps if needed"): frames are at most 2048 px (a GIF's own size in practice) and each animation's kept frames fit 128 MB of textures (mips included); past it every k-th frame is kept, each shown until the next kept one, so the animation keeps its length and timing. The frame list is not persisted: the worker reads the durations again each session (two ImageDecoder passes: durations, then the kept frames).
  - SVG detail: the raster follows the size the SVG is drawn at both ways (re-rasterized at rest when under 0.9x or over 2x of it, in half-octave steps), not only up: a big raster sampled far down blurs, and it holds memory. It is capped at 4096 px (§7.1's cap), so a logo wider than 1024 project px reaches the cap before 400% (a full-width one renders at 3.79x there).
  - `+ Solid` and `+ Image` make 5 s clips (§6.14 gives images 5 s; titles are 3 s, solids get the images' length). `+ Image` places like a drop on the canvas (§6.14: topmost video track or a new one, centered, Fit as §6.19) and its picker offers images only.

- deviations:
  - Keys of a section share their frames (CapCut-style "simple keyframes"): the stopwatch and every edit write all of a section's properties at the playhead (Transform: x, y, scale, scaleY, rotation; scaleY keyed with scale so the aspect lock stays plain). A key inserted inside an eased segment therefore splits it for the properties that did not change (their curve between the neighbours changes shape, not their values at the keys). Reason: spec §11 has one stopwatch per section, and the acceptance needs the lane (whose default property is `transform.scale`) to show the keys of a move.
  - The lane chooser ("Show keyframes for") lists sections (Transform, Opacity), not single properties: a section's properties share their frames, so per-property rows would show the same diamonds. Volume comes with Batch 37's lane and rubber band.
  - Selecting a diamond shows its values by moving the playhead to it on a click (spec §6.4 "selecting a diamond shows its value in the properties panel"); a drag leaves the playhead where it is (so the keys can snap to it, §6.15). A press elsewhere on the timeline or the canvas drops the selected keys (otherwise Delete would keep deleting keys after the clip body was clicked).
  - No lane on S tracks (their label bar is the whole clip, spec §6.4: no body) and none on caption or audio tracks this batch.
  - Splits keep the motion exact instead of always adding a key at each new edge (the Batch 11 follow-up): inside an eased segment a key at the edge would change the curve, so the key beyond the edge is kept outside the piece (like trims keep out-of-range keys, Batch 13) and shapes it; elsewhere (linear, hold, past the last key) a key with the value at the edge is added.
  - Edits with the playhead outside a clip key its nearest frame (`clipRel`); the stopwatch off keeps the look at the playhead; deleting the last keys keeps the look of the first deleted key.
  - An anchor moved on a keyed layer and the anchored-point move of a text whose content or style changes shift every position key by the delta at the playhead (exact while scale and rotation are not keyed).
  - The reserved `punchZoomAnimated` setting (false, read by nothing since Batch 27) is renamed `punchZoomAnimate` and defaults to true, so a value stored before this batch does not keep the animated zoom off. A piece that already has Transform keys gets the cut-in zoom on its scale keys instead of the ramp (its own motion stays). There is no settings switch until Batch 42.
  - A keyed text layer's raster is made at the largest scale its keys reach (P11: no re-rasterization while a zoom plays), drawn smaller with mipmaps in between.
  - The animated punch zoom's second key is at frame 6 of the piece, or its last frame when it is shorter.

Solids fade. `fadeFactor` holds the edge frame's value outside the clip.
  - Renderer: `DissolveLayer` is now two sides (texture, matrix, crop, opacity each) over a frame quad; the dissolve shader maps the quad onto each side's unit quad (`mapA` / `mapB`, per-layer uniforms 13 vec4 = 208 bytes) and counts a side only where it covers the point, so pictures of different sizes dissolve as they draw. LayerTextures resolves both sides (Export frame too: `exactMedia`); DrawListSnapshot compares both sides; the source detail counts both.
  - Playback engine: a transition's partner clip is fed with the clip under the playhead; windows, the lookahead (from `extendedStart`), the preroll check and top-ups run over each clip's extended span; frame positions outside a clip use `handleTimeUs`.

- deviations:
  - Transitions are `{ id, kind, before, after }` (frames on each side of the cut); the Transition section's duration and alignment are derived (center, start, end; a one-sided drag is a custom split, no chip pressed). Reason: one-sided end drags (§6.15 Alt) make any split, and both halves stay plain integers.
  - One invariant keeper (`reconcileTransitions` in DocumentStore) instead of transition code in every edit: every command that touches clips keeps transitions valid in its own undo step. A side that fitted its handle is shortened to what an edit leaves of it, and the transition goes when a side's handle is used up (§6.10 "removes it if the handle disappears"); a side already repeating edge frames keeps its length. A split through a transition's frames removes it; moves and deletes that break the cut remove it.
  - End drags stop at the handle (`Media start` / `Media end`, the trim look) unless that side already repeats frames, then at the clip. New transitions repeat edge frames only when the cut has no handle at all (§6.15).
  - Hit order: fade handles first, then junctions, then the transition block's ends and body within the block's band (the label bar), then trim zones (the HitTester header said transitions after edges): a block is grabbable at any zoom. Corner fade handles sit over a cut's top; the junction stays reachable under them.
  - Solids get an optional `fades` (§6.15 lists them among the fading clips; §5.2 has no field); no schema change (an absent field is no fade).
  - Audio: equal-power fades and crossfades. Sound has no repeated frames: a crossfade's ramps fit the audio there is (the outgoing clip silent by its media end, the incoming one rising from its media start, 10 ms at least), so a no-handle crossfade dips. Audio transitions are crossfades whatever the picture's kind (a dip does not darken sound).
  - Dips draw the color in the clip's own quad (a picture-in-picture dips alone, lower tracks stay), over the clip at its opacity.
  - Media bounds count within 2 us (`BOUND_SLACK_US`) and trims / slips / speed changes clamp `in` and `out` to the media: rounded frame times left `in` a microsecond off the grid after a trim (433333 - 266667 = 166666 for frame 5), and trims stopped a frame before the media start.
  - The quick row's transition chips are always enabled (a drag onto a cut needs no selection); a click applies at the selected edit point, else the selected transition (its kind changes), else the primary clip's cut nearest the playhead, else the cut nearest the playhead. The quick Fade in / out is a toggle (pressed when every target has it). A new transition is selected.
  - The clip menu's fade presets and Add transition are inline choice rows (a new ContextMenu entry kind; the menu has no submenus).

  - Scheduler (`audio/scheduler/envelope.ts` +2 tests, `AudioScheduler.ts` +3 tests): the fade node carries the automation (fades and crossfades times the keyed gain: `automationAt`, `automationRegions`, `automationCurve`, `keyedGainAt`); it is written per 50 ms step, AUTOMATION_AHEAD_SECONDS (1 s) ahead, as `setValueCurveAtTime` curves over the parts where it moves (a chunk continuing a curve starts one sample after it; FakeParam refuses overlaps as browsers do). The clip GainNode holds the gain of a clip without keys and mute (`clipGain`: 1 for a keyed clip), ramped on change; a change of a playing clip's volume keys restarts its voice (`sameVolumeKeys`). Voices' envelope and fade nodes start at their first values (no one-sample spike from a GainNode's default 1 when a source starts a hair before its first event). `audioLimits` exported. The offline mixdown (transcription, the export later) is the same code.
  - Audio scrub (`audio/scrub/AudioScrubber.ts`, 5 tests): a grain per call for each clip `heardClips` gives at the frame, GRAIN_SECONDS (40 ms) of its decoded segment from the frame's media time at the clip's speed and level (gain, keys, fades), a 4 ms rise and fall, 30 ms ahead of the render clock, through the track inputs (mute, solo, meters); a new grain fades the previous ones out on a release node of their own (no cancelled ramps); missing segments are asked for. `app/audioController.ts`: `audioScrubber`, `scrubGrain` (Audio scrub on, nothing playing, at most one per animation frame), `toggle.audioScrub`; TimelineView `onScrub` (each frame a ruler scrub shows, the press too) and PlaybackEngine `onStep` (frame steps: arrows, K+J / K+L).
