- deviations:
  - Volume keys only on audio clips (Batch 35 allowed video clips): a video's sound plays through its linked audio clip (spec §14), so its own gain is never heard; the Audio section and the audio actions edit the audio linked to a selected video.
  - The keyed gain and the fades share one automation on the voice's fade node (spec §14 names one clip GainNode for "clip gain + fades + keyframes"; the Batch 36 fade node is kept so a plain gain change still ramps on the clip GainNode without touching the curves). It is written per 50 ms step as the spec asks, but one second ahead instead of the sources' 200 ms: a main-thread stall shorter than that never leaves a chunk to start in the past (which jumps). An edit of a playing clip's volume keys restarts its voice (10 ms out and in) instead of re-writing scheduled curves.
  - No Volume row in the keyframe lane chooser: audio tracks have no lane; the rubber band is where volume keys show and are edited (the Batch 35 follow-up listed a lane row).
  - Rubber band scale: a cube-root amplitude curve (-60 dB at the bottom, +12 dB at the top, 0 dB at about 60%), a DAW fader's feel; the spec gives no scale. A drag of the line of a keyed clip moves the two keys around the pointer (Premiere's segment drag); before the first or after the last key, that key. A key moves in time between its neighbours and in value; Shift on the press adds it to the selection (the lane's rule), Shift during the drag keeps its frame. Values step by 0.1 dB.
  - Mod+click on the line adds the key and moves the playhead to it (the lane's Alt+click does the same).
  - Normalize's peak: the peaks pyramid's quantized level 0 (spec "uses peaks"), refined from the decoded samples of the few buckets that may hold the peak when they are in memory (no decode is started for it); measured +11.041 dB for a 0.25 tone (exact). A keyed clip shifts all its volume keys so its keyed peak lands at -1 dBFS. Fades are ignored (they only lower the level).
  - Auto-duck dips by 12 dB relative to the music's own gain curve (spec "keyframes at -12 dB": the same for a 0 dB music clip), so a second run ducks again; voice clips closer than two ramps make one dip; voices are audio clips on unmuted audio tracks above the music's track (closer to the divider), enabled and not muted. One click: the Audio section's Auto-duck button, the clip menu's Auto-duck music, and the audio track menu's Auto-duck music.
  - Detach audio: the linked audio already sits on its own audio track in this model, so Detach unlinks the pair; a video whose media has sound and no audio clip gets one (the first audio track free over its span, else a new one), unlinked. A link with a locked member is left alone.
  - Audio scrub grains play at the clip's speed (what playback sounds like there; spec "pitched 1x" read as the transport at 1x), 30 ms ahead of the render clock (Chrome renders blocks up to ~21 ms ahead of `currentTime`: a source started inside one began after its envelope's rise, a click, in the first browser runs). Grains also play for frame steps (arrows, K+J / K+L) and the press on the ruler.
  - Audio scrub has no key: spec §18 lists none (Batch 40 follow-up).

- deviations:
  - Peaks precision: the analysis reads the 8-bit peaks (spec §14 "from the peaks"; the 2 s budget), which round levels up to n/127, so a threshold acts as the largest n/127 at or below it (-40 dB finds windows at or below -42.1 dBFS; -36 dB and -37 dB act alike) and nothing below about -42 dBFS is told apart from digital silence. Rounding up keeps the cuts conservative: a cut never takes sound above the threshold. The threshold range is -60..-10 dB.
  - The minimum silence and the padding are playback time (a 2x clip plays a 1 s pause in 0.5 s); a silence at a clip's start or end goes up to its edge (no padding at the edge: dead air before the first word and after the last is cut down to the padding next to the speech only); cut frames are rounded inward (never into the padding).
  - Linked partners always follow (with Linked selection off too), so video and audio never drift; a link group with a member on a locked track is left out (the button is disabled for it alone); several analysed members of one group (two audio clips on one video) cut only where all are silent; the cuts stay inside the frames all members cover (a J or L cut's lead-in is never cut, the tracks would ripple apart).
  - The parameters are remembered app settings (the spec names them only); the settings panel shows them in Batch 42. Defaults -40 dB, 500 ms, 150 ms (functional defaults: the spec gives none).
  - Apply with an analysis still running shows "Still analysing" instead of applying a partial plan; with nothing found, "No silence to remove" and the row stays open.
  - Esc closes the row (spec §18's Cancel); the quick row's button toggles it; a selection with no sound closes it. No key of its own (spec §18 lists none; Batch 40 palette).

- deviations:
  - Paste targets (spec §6.12 Target, Batch 39 "on the targeted tracks keeping relative track offsets"): each kind's lowest copied lane lands on the lowest targeted, unlocked track of that kind (V1 / A1 when everything is targeted, the default), the other lanes above or below it, missing tracks created; with no targeted track of a kind its clips keep their own lanes; a lane that falls on a locked track refuses the paste with a toast. Cues go to the caption track (created with the copied style when missing).
  - Reading the system clipboard: Mod+V / Mod+Shift+V let the browser run its paste (the action declines the key), so the paste event brings the text without a permission prompt; the system clipboard's payload wins and becomes the tab's clipboard, any other text pastes the tab's own copy (a write to the system clipboard can fail, e.g. without focus). Menu rows and Mod+Alt+V (no browser paste) use the tab's copy, or read the system clipboard (Chrome may ask once) when the tab has none.
  - Paste moves the playhead to the end of the pasted clips (Premiere's paste: repeated pastes go back to back) and selects them.
  - Pasted cues never overwrite cues (spec §10.5): an overwrite paste with cues moves the whole block to the nearest frame where the cues fit, within the block's length (as an Alt-drag copy), else it is refused ("No room for the captions").
  - Another project's media: found by name, else by file name, of the same kind and at least as long as the pasted clips' source ranges need (spec "present by name"; a shorter file of that name would break the clips); else the copied record is added as an offline item (no analysis, no proxy; fix-attempt: its file is `{ handleKey: "", pathHint: <the copied path> }`, a reference that resolves nowhere, because the copied `media/<name>` can be another file of this project) and a toast names it: the slate and Relink are Batch 41's. A second paste of the same clips reuses that item (found by name).
  - Across frame rates the paste is refused with a toast: the frame conversion is Batch 42's (`TODO(batch 42)`).
  - Cut is Copy + Delete in one step ("Cut"): gaps stay, linked partners go with Linked selection (Delete's rule). With keys selected Copy and Cut take the keys (Cut deletes them), and Paste pastes keys while keys were copied last; the clipboard and its system mirror carry keys as a payload too.
  - Duplicate in the timeline (spec §11, §18) takes the selection with its groups and, with Linked selection, linked partners: the copies keep their offsets and land at the first offset of at least the selection's length where every copy fits on its own track. In the preview (Mod+D in the preview scope, the canvas menu) it copies the selected layers only (a video's linked audio is not copied, so the sound is not doubled) at the same frames on the video track above each, or on a new track inserted there, +20 px with every position key; with no layer selected it does the timeline's duplicate.
  - Paste attributes: the spec's list (transform, opacity, crop, speed, text style, animations, audio gain, fades) plus Keyframes (the Batch 35 follow-up). Each group comes from the first copied clip that has it, the primary first (a copied video gives the picture groups, its linked audio the audio gain). Keyframes on (default) brings the copied clip's keys of each pasted animatable section, cut to the target's length with the motion exact at its end, and replaces the target's keys of that section (removes them when the copied clip has none); off pastes the values at the copied clip's first frame and removes the target's keys of that section. Text style takes the preset link along and keeps the target's anchored point (unless Transform comes too). Audio gain includes mute. Speed goes through the Speed section's link and ripple options (one transaction with the rest). Every group starts checked; the ones the user unchecks stay unchecked for the session.
  - Action ids: `canvas.duplicate` for the canvas menu's Duplicate (the same handler as Mod+D in the preview); the quick row's Duplicate does the timeline duplicate (the properties panel is no canvas).

  1. A clip pasted from another project can bind to the wrong file in this project, even though the toast says it stays offline.
     - The cause: `resolveMedia` (`src/timeline/edit/clipboard.ts:227`) adds the "offline" record with the copied `file` unchanged. Media paths come from file names (`copyIntoMedia`, `src/project/mediaFiles.ts:102-114`: `media/<file name>`), so two projects that each imported an `Interview.mp4` both have `media/Interview.mp4`.
     - When this project's `Interview.mp4` is too short for the pasted source ranges (the case the deviation says "would break the clips"), the record gets the same `relPath` as this project's own file. The preview, audio and posters open files by `relPath` (`src/app/previewController.ts:351`, `src/app/audioController.ts:32`, `src/app/mediaController.ts:146`, `src/media/PosterStore.ts:154`). So the "offline" clips decode this project's other, shorter file, with ranges past its end. The toast (`src/app/clipboardController.ts:154`) says they "stay offline until the media is relinked". Batch 41's missing-media check would not flag them either, because the file exists.
     - Reproduced with a throwaway unit test (deleted): project A's 10 s `Interview.mp4` (`media/Interview.mp4`), clip at 5-6 s, pasted into project B whose `Interview.mp4` is 2 s at `media/Interview.mp4`. `result.offline[0].file` equals B's file `{ relPath: "media/Interview.mp4" }`. `clipboard.test.ts:171` misses this because the fixtures use `media/<id>.mp4`.
     - Fix: never let an added offline record point at a path that can resolve in this project. For example, give it a reference that cannot resolve (e.g. `{ handleKey: "", pathHint: <file name> }`, or a `relPath` that no project file uses), keeping the name for Batch 41's relink. Add a test where both projects use the same `media/<name>` path.

  - rev1, 11/11: Mod+J on Split and Alt+Shift+V on Add video track (no default key) survive a page reload and work after it. Export, then Reset all, then import restores both (265 commands in the file). Next frame (a held key's command) run from the palette steps exactly one frame.

  - Note: the shortcut editor stores whatever `recordChord` returns (`src/panels/SettingsDialog.tsx:108-112`) without checking it with `isValidKeys`. A key the keymap cannot name (an IME composition's "Process", media keys, PrintScreen) becomes a working chip for the session, and `sanitizeKeymap` (`src/project/appSettings.ts:123`) drops it silently on the next load. Refusing such a key while recording (keep waiting, as for a bare modifier) would be consistent.
  - Note: `importKeymap` stores the whole file in the app settings (`src/app/commandController.ts:184`, about 265 entries), while the live keymap keeps only the entries that differ from the defaults. Stored entries equal to today's defaults would pin those keys if a later batch changes a default (until the next edit in the shortcut editor stores the filtered map). Storing `keymap.getOverrides()` after the import would avoid this.

- notes:
  - Schema 2 (`core/document/types.ts`, `project/projectFile.ts`, tests): `Project.bins` (`{ id, name }[]`, strip order) and an optional `MediaItem.size` (the source's bytes at import, for relinking folders); migration 1 -> 2 adds `bins: []` (a schema 1 project opens unchanged otherwise, tested). `validate.ts`: unique bin ids with names, a media `binId` names a bin, an integer size; a media clip whose media record is gone is an offline clip (no media bound checked: the Batch 02 follow-up).
  - Commands (`core/commands/mediaCommands.ts`, 9 tests): `removeMedia(ids, "keep" | "delete")` ("Remove from project": used media leave their clips offline; "Remove and delete clips": the clips go too, on every track, one undo step, a shared transition with them), `clipsOfMedia`, `relinkMedia` (file and probe fields, several in one step), `addBin` / `renameBin` / `removeBin` (its media stay, in no bin) / `setMediaBin`, `nextBinName`, `cleanBinName`.
  - Media sources (`project/mediaSources.ts`, 6 tests with fake handles; `app/mediaOffline.ts`): one resolver for every media file: a copy (`relPath` in the project folder) or a linked file (`handleKey`: a `FileSystemFileHandle` in IndexedDB under `media-handle:<key>`; an empty key, Batch 39's pasted offline record, resolves nowhere). Statuses `missing`, `permission` (read access not granted again yet) and `failed` (the preview cannot decode it) in the `mediaStatus` store; `removed` when the record is gone. `checkAll` on open, `check` for new media (imports, pasted records, undone removals), every failed `file()` marks its media; `requestAccess` (a user gesture) and media that come back online `refreshMedia` every service (frames, images, audio, posters, sheets, peaks). The preview, the audio, the thumbnail sheets, the proxies and the posters resolve through it (the `TODO(batch 41)` of Batches 06, 08, 17, 24 resolved).
  - Reference import (`media/MediaImporter.ts`, 2 tests): with Settings > Media on "Link to the original files", files that come with a handle (the picker, dropped files and folders) are linked: the handle is stored (key = the new media id), the item gets `{ handleKey, pathHint }` (the path inside a dropped folder, else the file name). Pasted images are copied. Every new item records its size. On open the read permission is asked for in the opening click when the browser still counts it as a user gesture, else the Media tab's Allow access does it.
  - Missing media: a toast on open ("2 media files offline"), a notice strip under the tool row (N files need your permission · Allow access; N files offline · Relink folder…), a red badge on cards (Offline / No access / Can't play) with a Relink… (or Allow access) button over the thumbnail, the badge as a button in list rows. Relink… (`media.relink`): a file picker of the media's kind for the selected offline item; the file must be of that kind and hold the clips' source ranges (probed); a copied item gets a new copy in media/, a linked one a new handle key, a pasted offline record follows the import mode. Relink folder… (`media.relinkFolder`): the selected offline items (all offline items when none is selected) matched in a picked folder (recursive, up to 20,000 files) by file name (the item's own path's, then its panel name) and size when the item has one (else a single name match, the probe checking kind and length), relinked in one undo step, "Relinked 1 of 2 offline files" (`project/relink.ts`, 2 tests). A relinked file that differs (size or duration) drops the media's caches (sample index, sheets, poster, peaks, proxy) and takes the new probe fields; the same file keeps them.
  - Offline slates: the compositor (`OfflineSlates`, 2 tests) draws an offline video or image clip as a solid in `--offline-slate` over the visible part of where the media would be (its size, crop and transform; the frame's size without a record) and a text layer with the media's name and the reason ("Media offline", "Media offline: no access", "Media can't be played", "Media removed") in `--offline-slate-text`, its raster keyed `clipId#offline`; in a transition an offline side has no picture. The label is cached per clip (no allocation per frame). Undecodable media reach it through `LayerTextures` `onFail` -> `markFailed` (the `TODO(batch 41)` of Batch 08). The timeline draws offline clips in `--clip-offline-body` / `--clip-offline-label` with no filmstrip or waveform and an `Offline` badge (danger text in the sync badge's chip).
  - Remove dialog (`app/DialogHost.tsx`): "Remove from project" (always; used media keep their clips as offline slates), "Remove and delete clips" (when clips use the media), and "Also delete the copied file(s) from the media folder" (a checkbox when copies are among them; not undoable: an undo brings the media back offline). The Batch 04 wording that named batch numbers is gone.
  - Bins (`panels/media/BinStrip.tsx`): a left strip of chips: All, Video, Audio, Images (virtual, with counts), then the project's bins with counts; a click shows a bin (`mediaPanel.bin` in session state; a bin that is gone shows All); New bin in the header (`media.newBin`, named Bin / Bin 2..., its name edited at once); a bin chip renames on double-click and has a menu (Rename, Delete bin); cards dragged onto a bin chip move into it (`mediaGestures`, the chip marked with a data attribute while under the pointer); the media menu's Move to bin row (a chip per bin and None, `media.moveToBin` with the bin as argument; menu chips got a `command` field).

Cards and rows hidden by the bin, the chips or the search stay mounted (a layout effect sets `hidden`): no card re-renders or remounts while typing. A "No media here" state with Clear filters (`media.clearFilters`). Mod+A in the Media tab selects what it shows (`selection.selectAll` gains the media scope).

No earlier rejection to recheck. Problems:
  1. Undo or Redo of "Relink media" leaves the offline status wrong (acceptance 1: "relink restores everything").
     - The cause: statuses only change through `MediaSources.file/check/forget`. The document subscription (`src/app/mediaController.ts:271-277`) checks only media ids that were added, and a relink resets statuses only inside `applyRelinks` (`:859-860`). A `file` changed by Undo or Redo is never checked again. The preview releases its decoders on a file change, but the compositor draws a slate for any media with a status and never asks for its frames (`src/render/compositor/Compositor.ts:325`), so nothing reads the file again.
     - Reproduced in headless Chrome (`%TEMP%/b41/rev_undo.mjs`, 5181 restarted): a linked video moved away, the project reopened (missing), Relink… to the moved file (online). Ctrl+Z with the clip at the playhead: missing (the preview read the old handle). Ctrl+Shift+Z: the media's `file` is the relinked handle again, but the status stays `missing`: the preview keeps the slate (71, 85, 105), the card keeps Offline + Relink…, still after a playhead move and 5 s. Second case (fresh project, playhead at 300, off the clip): Relink…, then Ctrl+Z: `file` is the moved-away handle, but the media stays online (no badge, no notice, Relink disabled).
     - Fix: in that subscription, take the ids in both `prev.media` and `state.media` whose `file` differs and run `sources.forget(ids)` then `sources.check(ids)` (so `refreshMedia` reloads the ones that come back). While there (found by code reading, not reproduced): `dropMediaCaches` is not undoable and the poster and proxy caches carry no file stamp (`src/media/PosterStore.ts:178-188`, `proxyPath`), so after an undone relink to a different file the poster (and a proxy made since) can be the other file's; keep them consistent with the restored record. Add a test for Undo and Redo of a relink.
  2. Removing an offline media leaves its status behind: the notice and Relink folder… stay.
     - The cause: `MediaSources.update` drops the statuses of media that left the project (`src/project/mediaSources.ts:182`) only when some later update runs, and nothing runs one on a removal (a "Media removed" slate reads no file). `OfflineNotice` counts `mediaStatus` (`src/panels/media/MediaTab.tsx:118-121`), and `media.relinkFolder` is enabled while `mediaStatus.getState().size > 0` (`src/app/mediaController.ts:997`).
     - Reproduced (`%TEMP%/b41/rev_removed.mjs`): a copied video whose file was deleted from media/, the project reopened ("1 file offline · Relink folder…"), the card selected, Delete, Remove from project. The media list holds only the other item, but `mediaStatus` still has the removed id, the notice still says "1 file offline · Relink folder…", and Relink folder… answers "No offline media to relink".
     - Fix: drop the removed ids from the status store in the same document subscription (for example `sources.forget(removed)`), with a test.
  3. Media hidden by the bin, a filter chip or the search stay selected, and Delete, Move to bin and card drags act on them (acceptance 2's workflow).
     - The cause: `setMediaSearch`, `toggleKind` and `showBin` (`src/app/mediaController.ts:587`, `:596`, `:602`) never trim `mediaPanel.selection`. `requestRemove` (`:506-509`), `selectedMedia` (`:472`: Move to bin, Reveal in folder) and the card drag (`src/app/mediaGestures.ts`) take the whole selection. Imports made while a bin, a chip or a search hides them arrive selected and hidden too.
     - Reproduced (`%TEMP%/b41/rev_hidden.mjs`): three copied videos, `used.mp4` on V1. Click `used.mp4`, click the Unused chip (the card hides but stays selected), Ctrl+click `spare1.mp4`, Delete: "Remove 2 media files from the project? Used by 1 clip…". Remove from project removes the hidden `used.mp4` too, and its clip becomes a "Media removed" slate.
     - Same cause: Reveal in media panel (`revealSelectedMedia`, `:940-946`) selects a card the bin, the chips or the search hide, so nothing is revealed.
     - Fix: keep the selection to what the tab shows when the bin, the chips or the search change (or act on the shown part of it), and make Reveal show the media (All or its bin, chips and search cleared). Add tests.
  4. "Remove from project" deletes a transition when the removed media's clip is its outgoing side.
     - The cause: `removeMedia(ids, "keep")` (`src/core/commands/mediaCommands.ts:54-73`) affects `clips`, so `DocumentStore` runs `reconcileTransitions`. With the record gone, `handleOf` measures the tail against the clip's own out point (`src/core/document/transitions.ts:74`: `project.media[clip.mediaId]?.durationUs ?? clip.out`), the tail becomes 0, `sideAfterEdit` returns null and the pair is deleted (`:261-263`). The incoming side keeps its transition (a head does not depend on the media). The dialog, the docstring ("a transition shared with a removed clip goes" only for delete) and the deviation (`docs/PROGRESS.md:329`) do not say this, and the batch draws "an offline side" of a transition, so it was meant to stay.
     - Confirmed by a throwaway probe test (deleted) and the code path: c1 (media m) then c2 (media n) with a 5 + 5 frame dissolve; `removeMedia(["m"], "keep")` leaves neither `c1.transitionOut` nor `c2.transitionIn`; `removeMedia(["n"], "keep")` keeps it.
     - Fix: a media clip whose record is gone keeps its handle in `handleOf` (for example `Infinity`), so removing the record changes no transition. Add `mediaCommands.test.ts` cases for both sides.
  5. The search matches the `media/` folder of every copied item: `mediaMatcher` searches the name and `mediaPath(item)` (`src/panels/media/mediaList.ts:89`), which is `media/<file>` for every copy, so any word inside "media/" ("dia", "medi", "edi", "media") shows the whole library (searching "dia" for "Diaries.mp4" narrows nothing). `src/panels/media/mediaList.test.ts:124` (`search: "media/"` gives every item) locks it in. Fix: match the file name (and a linked file's hint folders), not the project's `media/` folder, and change the test.
  6. `.heading` is defined twice in `src/panels/SettingsDialog.module.css` (`:70`, Batch 40's shortcut headings, and `:212`, the new Media tab). CSS Modules merge the two rules: the Media tab's "Import" heading (`src/panels/SettingsDialog.tsx:189`) gets the shortcut headings' padding and hairline bottom border, and the shortcut `h3` headings get the new `margin: 0`. The design-gap entry (`docs/PROGRESS.md:175`) describes a plain overline heading. Fix: a class of its own for the Media tab's heading.

Earlier reviews rejected the same kind of value (Batch 15 swatch ring, Batch 21 2 px menu gap, Batch 25 2 px picker ring). - fix-attempt: done (2026-10-18)
  1. Undo and Redo of "Relink media" now leave the right offline status and nothing made from the other file:
    - `MediaSources.attach(document)` (`src/project/mediaSources.ts`) follows the document: new media and media whose `file` changed (a relink, its undo or redo: `sameFile`) are checked again, with `failed` reset. A check whose media's file changed again before it ended is dropped, so a quick undo and redo end on the last file's status. `file()` writes a status only while the record still names the file it read. `whenChecked()` resolves once the checks so far are done. The controller's own `added` check is gone, and `applyRelinks` no longer forgets, checks or regenerates by itself: it dispatches and awaits `whenChecked()`.
    - `filesChanged` (`src/app/mediaController.ts`, the document subscription) handles media whose file changed. When the file holds other content than before (`sameContent`: size when both records know it, duration, picture size), what was made from the other file goes at once and is made again. That is the image poster (`PosterStore.regenerate`: the bitmap closed, the cached poster deleted, made from the file), the sheets (`ThumbnailStore.replace`: dropped, made again without the cache), the peaks (forgotten), and the proxy (`ProxyJobs.filesChanged`: a ready or failed proxy becomes pending, a running job starts over, "none" stays; the session's failure of the other file is forgotten for any changed file). Media online before and after get `refreshMedia` once their check ends; for the others a status change does it. So an undone relink to a different file leaves no poster, sheet or proxy of the other file. A proxy made since the relink is made again from the restored file, and fails on a missing one.
    - Tests: `mediaSources.test.ts` +3 (relink, undo, redo and quick undo/redo sequences on a `DocumentStore`; a removal; `sameFile` / `sameContent`), `ProxyJobs.test.ts` +1, `PosterStore.test.ts` +1, `ThumbnailStore.test.ts` +1.

### Batch 43: Export engine
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-18
- notes:
  - Engine (`src/export/`, 7 test files, 50 tests):
    - `presets.ts`: the Reels preset (1080x1920, 30 fps, H.264, 12 Mbps, keyframes every 2 s, AAC 192 kbps), `exportFormat` (the long edge capped, never scaled up, even sides; the project's rate divided down to the cap), `fillFileName` (`{project}-{preset}-{date}.mp4`).
    - `plan.ts`: exported frames, exact integer timestamps (no drift at 29.97), project-frame sampling, the keyframe cadence, the audio length, the chunk counts for the muxer, the video timescale.
    - `codecs.ts`: encoder configurations best first, the first `isConfigSupported` accepts wins. H.264 High, then Main, then Baseline, at the lowest level that holds the size, rate and bitrate. HEVC Main and AV1 Main levels, falling back to H.264. AAC-LC, else Opus.
    - `eta.ts`: a 5 s moving-average rate; paused time does not count.
    - `pipeline.ts` (`runExport`): render, then encode once `encodeQueueSize < 4`, with a keyframe every `keyInterval`. The audio is fed in 100 ms AudioData blocks interleaved with the frames (silence past the mix). A pause gate, abort, encoder errors, flush and finalize; the encoders are always closed and every frame is closed after its encode.
    - `inputs.ts` (`exportNeeds`): the media and text a range draws, transition handles included.
    - `exportFile.ts` (`ExportFile`): positional writes in cache/export-temp/<id>.mp4, then the move into exports/ under a free name, or discard; `clearExportTemp`.
  - Worker: `media/workers/export.worker.ts` (WorkerKind `export`; protocol methods `exportVideo` with `started` / `frames` / `bytes` progress, and `pauseExport`, immediate).
    - `export/ExportRenderer.ts` builds its own stack: GpuDevice, WebGpuRenderer, a TexturePool at 30% of the budget, FrameService (full lod, uploads at the size each frame asks for), ImageService, `FontLibrary(self.fonts)` with the bundled and project faces, TextRasterCache, `LayerTextures.resolveExact` (the Export frame path), and `Compositor` with offline slates. It draws into an OffscreenCanvas of the export size, turned into `new VideoFrame(canvas, { timestamp, duration })`.
    - Its decoders are its own: `media/workers/decodeHandlers.ts` (decode.worker's handlers, now shared) served in-thread by `media/workers/loopback.ts` (test).
    - `export/browserCodecs.ts`: VideoEncoder and AudioEncoder wrappers, planar AudioData, and the mp4-muxer `StreamTarget` with fast start reserved and 4 MiB chunks.
  - Main thread (`app/exportController.ts`, `app/exportState.ts` + test):
    - `app.export` (Export button, Mod+E) runs the Reels preset on [0, content end). It takes the document snapshot, then the files and cached sample indexes, SVG rasters, the project's font faces (`projectFontFaces`), the offline labels, the slate look (`slateLook`, shared with the preview) and the stereo `renderMixdown`. Bytes are written as they come.
    - The progress toast has a live line and bar (a `live` store written to the DOM, no React render) and Pause / Resume and Cancel. The success toast gives the path, size, frame size and frame count; cancel and failure toasts.
    - Commands `export.pauseResume` and `export.cancel` (catalog + palette). `app.export` left `planned.ts`, which is now empty.

      - The bound is the hardware encoder: H.264 at 1080x1920 runs at about 58 fps whatever the latency mode or queue depth (2-32), against 146 fps for drawing alone.
      - Container (read with mp4box through the app's `readMp4`): `ftyp, moov, free, mdat` (moov first), avc1.640428 (High 4.0) 1080x1920, 1800 frames with one cts delta of 1/30 s (timescale 90000), keyframes 2.0 s apart.
      - Audio: AAC-LC 48 kHz stereo; both tracks start at 0.
      - Chrome's `<video>`: 60.01 s, 1080x1920, plays and seeks, 0 dropped frames.
      - Content: decoded frames carry their source codes (0, 30, 450, 884, 895, 899, 905, 916, 930, 1799), and the flashes fall on the right frames.
      - While it ran: the texture budget was 563.7 of 805.3 MB, zero React commits in 4 s of playback during the export, and the live toast line `10% · 185 / 1800 frames · 0:46 left`.

      - Video: exactly 18000 frames of 1/30 s, 600.000 s.
      - Audio: 28,800,000 samples, also 600.000 s.
      - The flashes decode on frames 30, 9000 and 17970 exactly, and the clicks at samples 48000, 14,400,000 and 28,752,000 exactly. The A/V offset is 0.000 ms at 1 s, 300 s and 599 s, so the drift is 0.000 ms.
      - Every click lands within 0 samples of its second. The click at 0 s sits under the voice's start ramp at the clip's first samples, as in the preview.

     - Fix: have the worker start in the job's current pause state (for example a `paused` field in `ExportJobParams` that the handler passes to `gate.set`, and no `pauseExport` before the job is posted), or hide or disable Pause until `started`. Add a test for a pause before the job starts.

### Batch 44: Export UX
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-18
- notes:
  - Engine (`src/export/`, unit tested):
    - `presets.ts`: TikTok and Shorts beside Reels, and `ExportSettings` with these fields: codec, resolution scale 100/75/50, long-edge cap and the 4K cap, frame rate cap, bitrate mode, target and peak (or "auto"), keyframe interval, AAC bitrate, hardware preference.
      - Functions: `exportFormat` for them, `autoBitrate` (YouTube's rates), `fpsChoices`, `customFrom` (a preset's output as Custom settings), `estimateBytes`, `formatSummary`, `withExtension`, `presetSlug`, and the sanitizers of settings and of one's own presets.
    - `queue.ts` (`ExportQueue`): jobs one at a time in order, with a store of the queued and running jobs.
      - Cancel: a queued job leaves at once; the running one aborts and the next starts.
      - Outcomes: done, cancelled or failed (a failed write aborts with its reason).
    - `log.ts`: `ExportRequest` (kind, preset, settings, audio file type, range, template, destination), the log (the last 20, newest first) and its session.json sanitizers.
    - `audioExport.ts` + `wav.ts`: Export audio in export.worker, as WAV (16-bit PCM, 1 s blocks) or M4A (AAC-LC, else Opus, in an audio-only MP4 with the moov at the front), with pause and abort between blocks.
    - `support.ts`: codec support per format (a cached `isConfigSupported`).
    - `codecs.ts`: the format's bitrate mode and hardware preference, and the level chosen to hold the peak.
    - `exportFile.ts`: a picked file as the target (`ExportFile.toPicked`, `pickedFile`), `saveExport` for small files, and temp files with any extension.
    - `exportCues(project, range)` (`timeline/edit/captions.ts`) cuts the cues to the range and times them from its start.
  - Worker: the `exportAudio` method (protocol + export.worker).
  - App (`app/exportController.ts`, `app/exportState.ts`):
    - `app.export` (the Export button, Mod+E) opens the Export tab (the `exportTab` store: open, active, focus). Esc (the last step of `app.cancel`) or the tab's X (`export.close`) returns to Edit Properties.
    - The queue (`exportQueue`) keeps a runtime per job: a live store, the ETA and an `ExportPauseSync`. The pinned progress toast shows the running job only while the tab is hidden.
    - The tab's choices are app settings: `exportPresetId`, `exportCustom`, `exportPresets`, `exportFileTemplate`, `exportDestination`, `exportAudioFormat`, `exportCaptionFormat`. The range choice and the log are session state (`exportRange`, `exportLog`, in session.json).
    - Commands, in a new Export category of the catalog and palette:
      - `export.start`, `export.close`, `export.audio`, `export.captions`, `export.copyFrame`, `export.again`, `export.openFolder`, `export.savePreset`, `export.deletePreset`.
      - `export.pauseResume` and `export.cancel`, which now take a job id argument.
      - `preview.exportFrame` moved here (`exportFrameNow`), with `renderFramePng` in `app/previewController.ts`.
  - UI (`panels/properties/ExportTab.tsx`, `ExportJobs.tsx`, `ExportTab.module.css`; `PropertiesPanel.tsx` shows both tabs while Export is open):
    - The top rows:
      - Preset chips (Reels, TikTok, Shorts, one's own, Custom), with the format summary under them.
      - Range chips (Whole timeline / In to out, dimmed without marks), with the range readout.
      - The file name template, with the resulting name.
      - Save to chips (exports folder / Choose file…).
      - The primary Export button, focused whenever the tab opens (Enter exports), with the size estimate.
    - Sections:
      - Queue: job cards with a live bar and line, Pause/Resume, and Cancel (Remove from the queue while waiting).
      - Settings: Codec (unsupported codecs marked), Resolution, Frame rate, Bitrate mode, Target / Max, Keyframes, Audio, Encoder; Save as preset…, Delete preset.
      - Extras: Export frame, Copy frame, Export audio with WAV/M4A chips, Export captions with SRT/VTT chips.
      - Log: the last 20 jobs, each with Export again and Open folder.

### Batch 45: Performance pass
- status: done
- date: 2026-10-18
- notes:
  - Measurement tooling (dev builds; `src/core/perf/` unit tested):
    - `core/perf/perfMath.ts`: `RateCounter` (events per second over a sliding window), `percentiles` (nearest rank), `SampleRing`, `LongTaskLog`, `frameSummary` (rAF intervals: fps, the longest, p95, frames over 1.5 vsyncs). `core/perf/formatPerf.ts`: the overlay's text from a `PerfSnapshot`.
    - `app/perfMonitor.ts` gathers:
      - React commits (a `<Profiler>` around `<App/>`, dev only), content and overlay redraws and preview draws per second, decode latency p50/p95/p99 (first frame shown, exact frame), dropped frames;
      - GPU memory: the new `WebGpuRenderer.textureCounts` (every texture the renderer allocated and has not destroyed), the texture pool, text rasters, decoded audio;
      - open VideoFrames (main and worker), decoders, queue depths (`WorkerPool.inFlightByKind()`, the decode worker's waiting jobs: new `queued` in `WorkerDecodeStats`, idle tasks), main-thread long tasks (PerformanceObserver, `takeRecords` before reading), the JS heap.
    - Overlay: `dev.togglePerfStats` (palette, and an Activity button before Settings in the app bar, dev builds) shows `PerfStats`, a fixed chip at the bottom left (over the start screen too), written in the scheduler loop on the new `devStats` flag four times a second, never by React. The worker's counters are fetched only while the decode worker runs (a request would start it).
    - Benchmarks (`app/perfBench.ts`; commands `dev.benchTimeline`, `dev.benchScrub`, `dev.benchExport`, `dev.benchStartup`, `dev.benchMemory` in the palette; `__editor.perf.bench.*`): the report goes to the console as JSON and a toast sums it up. Synthetic pointer and wheel events on the timeline canvas (pointer capture stubbed meanwhile).
      - timeline: 500 clips on 8 tracks (one undo step), then Ctrl+wheel zoom, wheel scroll, a clip drag (undone) and 3 s of playback.
      - scrub: the longest video clip fitted to the view, a 600-frame ruler sweep, then 40 moves within one held drag (the exact frame while scrubbing, then the full frame after the 300 ms rest).
      - export: 60 s (or the timeline) with the chosen preset into exports/.
      - startup: reloads with `?bench=startup`.
      - memory: the counters with the project open and 3 s after closing it.
    - Startup marks in every build: `app:start`, `app:gpu`, `app:interactive` (the first idle moment after the app's first commit), `editor:interactive` (after the editor's).
    - `FrameService`: p50/p95/p99 of the last 128 latencies, `latencySamples`, `resetLatencies`, `onLatency`. `projectController.closeProject()` (dev: the memory benchmark): closes to the start screen over an empty placeholder document.
  - Fixes (all from measurements):
    - Import long task: `DecodedAudio.atMostStereo` mixed a 5.1 decodeAudioData buffer down in one pass inside the import's last task (with the cards' render: 67-70 ms in 2 of 3 runs). It is async now, 2^18 frames per slice with a yield between slices, also for the probe's buffer (`put` keeps the media's layout at once and loads wait for the mixdown).
    - P13 on project close:
      - `DecodedAudio.reset` closes decode.worker's parsed audio tracks (and opens that land after the close), the Batch 10 follow-up.
      - The renderer destroys its spare video-frame textures and pooled blur textures (`releaseCaches` in `detachPreview`): 4 textures (8-14 MB) stayed per closed project.
      - `closeCurrent` stops the decode, analysis and proxy workers: 2.2-2.6 MB of heap each stayed, with their sessions.
    - Thumbnails starving proxies: the eager LOD0/LOD1 sheets of a long 4K video decoded from the source while its proxy job ran, on the same hardware decoder, and were made again from the proxy afterwards. Every TODO in `src` is tagged. No earlier rejection to recheck. Problem:
  1. After a mouse click on a switch or a text button, Space (and Enter) press that control again instead of running the shortcut: §18's Space = Play/Pause breaks for mouse users, and an edit can be silently undone.
     - The cause: the new `isNativeKeyTarget` (`src/core/keyboard/KeyDispatcher.ts:54`, used at `:161`) hands plain Space / Enter to any focused `button`, `[role="switch"]`, etc. The doc comment (`:51`) and the Batch 46 deviation in Global deviations ("Space and Enter on a control reached with Tab ..." line) assume "a pointer click never leaves a button focused". That holds for `IconButton` (`src/ui/IconButton.tsx:53`, `keepFocus`), `MenuButton`, `Swatches`, `Knob` and the Export chips. It does not hold for `Toggle` (`src/ui/Toggle.tsx:19`) or `Button` (`src/ui/Button.tsx:29`): neither prevents focus on mouse down, and Chrome focuses a clicked `<button>`.
     - Reproduced (`%TEMP%/rev46/focus2.mjs`, `focus5.mjs`, real CDP mouse and keys). With the text clip selected, a click turns Drop shadow on, Space turns it off again, and playback does not start. The same happens with Clip enabled. With clip A selected, click Crop's Reset or Crop to frame, then Space: no playback (`activeElement` is the button). On HEAD~2 the same steps play and leave the switch alone.
     - Fix: make `Toggle` and `Button` keep the focus where it was on mouse down, as `IconButton` does. Do the same for the other raw panel buttons with this gap (`src/panels/media/MediaTab.tsx:186` offline badge, `:196` relink button, `src/ui/ColorField.tsx:59` swatch). Alternatively, `isNativeKeyTarget` could act only on `:focus-visible` targets. Add a test that fails today (for example: a Toggle / Button mousedown is default-prevented, or the dispatcher keeps Space = play for a focused switch that is not focus-visible). Then correct the deviation line and the doc comment.
- fix-attempt: done (2026-10-18)
  1. Space and Enter after a mouse click on a switch or a text button run the shortcut again (Space plays); the control is not pressed a second time.
     - Done in the dispatcher, not in each button: `KeyDispatcher` hands plain Space / Enter / the navigation keys to a focused control only when the keyboard focused it (`src/core/keyboard/KeyDispatcher.ts`, `handleKeyDown`). `attach` adds three capture listeners: a Tab keydown (so a widget that stops Tab, like the More tools menu, still counts), a `pointerdown` and a `focusin`. A focus that follows a pointer press is a pointer focus, one that follows Tab is a keyboard focus, and a focus a script moves takes the kind of the last of the two. A press on the focused control makes it a pointer focus. A key that the control's widget already handled (`defaultPrevented`: a color square's arrows) is left to it whatever the origin, so a clicked slider never steps frames on top of its own move.
     - Why not the review's first option (Toggle and Button preventing focus on mouse down): Toggle and Button (used across the panels) and 15 raw buttons take the focus on a click (the media offline badge and relink button, the color swatch, the font picker's button, star and system-fonts row, the project name, Settings' tabs and General radios, the Transcribe model radios, the Paste attributes checkboxes, the start screen's recent projects, the Delete files checkbox), and the next new button would bring the bug back. Preventing focus on a `Button` would also stop a commit-on-blur field (a TextField in commit mode) from committing before the button's click runs (Export after typing a file name). The `:focus-visible` option does not work in Chrome: measured on a clicked switch, `:focus-visible` is false after the click and already true inside a capture keydown listener of the first key press (even Shift), so the dispatcher would still see a "keyboard" focus.
     - The doc comment of `isNativeKeyTarget` and the Batch 46 line in Global deviations are corrected.
     - Tests (`KeyDispatcher.test.ts` +4, real `pointerdown` / `focusin` / Tab events through `attach(window)`): a clicked switch plays on Space (default prevented, so Chrome does not toggle it on key-up) and a clicked tab steps on ArrowRight; a switch reached with Tab takes Space, and a press on it gives Space back to play; a focus a script moves after a press is a pointer one (Space plays), after Tab a keyboard one; a key a clicked slider's widget handled runs no shortcut. The first three fail on HEAD (3 of 24 red), all pass with the fix.
     - Browser (headless Chrome 155, real CDP mouse and keys; a snapshot of the tree on 5197, the review's origin and profile, project `rev46-a`; probes in `%TEMP%/fix46` plus the review's `focus2.mjs` / `focus5.mjs`):

       - `probe2.mjs`: click the project name, type a new name, Enter: the focus is back on the name, and Space plays (the rename field stays closed). Renamed back after.
       - `kbd.mjs` (Batch 46's keyboard probe): Tab onto Snap shows "Snap S", Space turns it off and Enter on again. `probe.mjs`: Tab onto Drop shadow (focus-visible), Space toggles it and does not play.
       - `fv.mjs`: the `:focus-visible` measurement above.

Browser checks in headless Chrome 155 over CDP (9353, own profile) on my snapshot server (5211; helpers in `%TEMP%/b47`: `setup.mjs` with `localFile` (a file of this machine into the page through a file input) and dialog auto-accept, `page.js` with `__b47.captureNext/watch/stopWatch/exportFrameStats`, and `hdr.mjs`, `hdrshots.mjs`, `hdrproxy.mjs`, `hdrexport.mjs`, `kill.mjs`, `corrupt.mjs`, `exportloss.mjs`, `cycles.mjs`, `longaudio.mjs`, `strip.mjs`; regression copies in `%TEMP%/b47reg`).
  - Tests (`src/timeline/edit/fuzzKit.ts`, test-only): a seeded PRNG (mulberry32, now shared by `undoFuzz.test.ts` and `speed.test.ts`), `randomProject` (valid by construction through a validating store: locked tracks, linked A/V pairs, groups, transitions, fades, keyframes, speeds, a freeze, text, solids, cues, markers, bins, offline clips), about 110 operations over every edit builder (moves, trims, roll / slip / slide / stretch, Q / W / E, splits, deletes, gaps, lift / extract, links and groups, tracks, keyframes, transitions, fades, speed / freeze / punch zoom, volume / normalize / auto-duck / detach, Remove silence, copy / cut / paste / paste insert / duplicate / paste attributes with payloads from other projects, crop / transform / opacity, solids, text / presets / animations, captions, bins / remove / relink, markers), and `documentChecks` (every number finite, clips of locked tracks untouched, ...).
    - `fuzz.test.ts` (29 tests): one property suite per area of the Batch 34-42 follow-ups (solids, keyframes, transitions and fades, audio, silence, clipboard, bins / remove / relink, frame rate conversions 30 -> 60 -> 30 and templates of random documents), locked tracks, captions and a mixed run with undo / redo interleaved: valid after every step, undo back to the original exactly, redo to the final.
    - `fuzz.perf.test.ts` (acceptance 1): 10,000 operations over all areas, every step validated, then all undone to the original and redone: 10,000 ops in 11.3 s (888 ops/s, 6425 changed the document, 200 clips at the end), undo + redo of everything 8.7 s, 19.9 s in all (budget 60 s).
    - `editMatrix.test.ts` (142 tests): every builder on one fixture with a locked track (holding a clip linked to an audio clip and grouped with an unlocked one), linked pairs, a group, a cross dissolve, transform / opacity / volume keys and fades and a caption track: valid, the locked clips untouched, transitions and keys valid, undo exact, plus per-family expectations (linked edits on both partners, groups together, keys shifted by splits and speed).
    - Edge cases: `subtitles.test.ts` (a seeded SRT / VTT round trip with Unicode, RTL marks, `&<>`, digit-only lines and `-->` in VTT text; hours over 99; CR-only files; whitespace lines; header only; 10,000 cues), `time.test.ts` (24000/1001 and 60000/1001 round trips, random large values, monotonic floor, timecode round trips), `projectFile.test.ts` (random documents through serialize / parse, a UTF-8 BOM, truncated files, odd schema versions, unknown top-level fields kept).
    - Bugs the fuzzing found, each fixed with a regression test that fails without the fix: audio pasted from another project could take a same-named media without sound (`clipboard.ts`, `resolveMedia`); a rate stretch of a source range off the frame grid (a converted clip, a paste from another rate) broke the §5.2 in / out rule, which a production build would have saved (`trim.ts`, `stretchRange`); cue copies dragged with other clips could put those before frame 0 (`captions.ts`, `clampCueDelta`); a freeze frame converted to a lower rate ended past its media (`fpsConvert.ts`, `fitSource`); a rubber band key moved past the clip's end landed on the key before it (`volume.ts`, `clampKeyShift`); project.json with a UTF-8 BOM did not open (`projectFile.ts`); -0 positions and key frames (`text.ts`, `keyframes.ts`).
  - Error boundaries: `app/PanelBoundary.tsx` around each of the four panels (`App.tsx`), the fallback in the panel's frame with Reload panel; `app/panelErrors.ts` (faults and reload epochs per panel, `panel.reload`: the named panel, else every failed one, else the panel that had the keyboard; `app/panelController.ts` registers it); `FrameScheduler.onViewFailure` after `VIEW_FAILURE_LIMIT` (3) failed renders in a row of one view, mapped to its panel by its flags; `app/FatalScreen.tsx` (`AppBoundary` around the app in `main.tsx`, and a failing `start()`), Reload saves first (`saveBeforeReload`).
  - Worker crash recovery: `WorkerCrashError` and `isWorkerCrash` (protocol), ping / pong and a dev `exit` message (`WorkerHost` answers at once); `WorkerPool`: the error event's file, line, column and error logged (the Batch 46 follow-up), `messageerror` logged, `onCrash` listeners, crash counts, the watchdog (`WATCHDOG_TICK_MS` 100; the decode worker: ping after 400 ms of silence while requests wait, crashed 800 ms later; a request cancelled and asked again at once keeps the clock; a tick after a main-thread long task decides nothing; `watchdogEnabled` for debugging), `exitForTest`. Retries: `FrameService` (open, frame, prefetch: once, without breaking a proxy), `DecodedAudio` (a crash is no failure of the media), `LayerTextures` (asks again 500 ms later after a second crash), `PlaybackEngine` (the stream asks again), `ThumbnailStore` (a sheet once more), `ProxyJobs` (the job once more).
  - Decode errors: a `configure()` that throws although `isConfigSupported` said yes marks the video undecodable (`VideoDecodeSession`); playback reports an undecodable media at once (`PlaybackEngine.onFail` -> the slate and the "Can't play" badge); the export draws the slate for a video refused partway (the frame drawn again) instead of failing; failed imports (`app/failedImports.ts`, `Refusal.container`, the Media tab's `FailedImports` rows, `media.dismissFailedImport`); the damaged-MP4 reason in plain words (`mp4Probe.ts`).

  - `render/gpu/drawRecords.ts`: the CPU side of a draw, moved out of `WebGpuRenderer` and shared by both backends so they draw the same quads. It covers:
    - pooled records per pane, with the frame and pane scissors;
    - the border edges;
    - the shaped-solid growth;
    - the dissolve side maps;
    - the blur region and quad growth (`blurRegionInto`, `showBlurred`).
    `WebGpuRenderer` uses it unchanged in output: all 25 WebGPU captures of the parity scenes equal HEAD's pixel for pixel (A/B on the same origin).
  - `render/gpu/backend.ts`:
    - `RendererBackend`, the `RenderDevice` interface (GpuDevice and GlContext: state, generation, restores, start, dispose, `loseForTest`), `BackendRenderer` (Renderer + backend, texture counts, `releaseCaches`).
    - `forcedBackend`: `?renderer=webgl2` puts WebGL2 first (WebGPU stays the fallback); `?renderer=webgpu` allows WebGPU only.
    - `chooseBackend`: a WebGPU adapter, else WebGL2 on the GPU, else none.
    - `render/gpu/createBackend.ts` makes a backend's device and renderer.
  - `render/gpu/GlContext.ts`: the WebGL2 context on its own OffscreenCanvas (`GL_ATTRIBUTES`: no alpha, depth, stencil or MSAA, `failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat`). `webglcontextlost` is prevented and `webglcontextrestored` is a new generation; `recover: false` fails instead (export); `webgl2Available()` is the startup probe.
  - `render/gpu/glShaders.ts`: GLSL ES 3.00 ports of the WGSL. They cover the textured layers (footprint taps, `u_mipmapped`), the dissolve, solids (SDF box / ellipse, gradient), the full-frame scale pass and the blur pass, with the same 13-vec4 layer layout as `packLayer` and quads from `gl_VertexID`.
  - `render/gpu/WebGl2Renderer.ts`, uploads and targets:
    - RGBA8 textures; premultiplied uploads (`UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL`; Chrome's default ImageBitmaps, PNGs and ImageDecoder frames arrive premultiplied: measured); `generateMipmap`; spare video-frame textures as on WebGPU.
    - Video-frame textures have mutable storage and take each frame with `texImage2D`: `texSubImage2D` into immutable storage held the decoder's buffers longer (see acceptance). Other textures are immutable (`texStorage2D`).
    - A scaled upload goes whole into a scratch texture of the frame's visible size (what a VideoFrame upload writes: measured), then through the scale pass. HDR frames go through the shared `toneMapToCanvas` (hdr.ts).
    - Offscreen targets are framebuffers drawn top row first (the view's y turned), so sampling and readback match WebGPU.
    - Canvas targets: the context's own canvas is drawn directly (the export); another canvas is presented through `bitmaprenderer` (`transferToImageBitmap`).
  - `render/gpu/WebGl2Renderer.ts`, draws: uniforms go through `uniform4fv(location, data, offset, length)` out of one array, so a draw allocates nothing on our side. The two blur passes run into pooled framebuffers. Texture counts and `releaseCaches` work as on WebGPU, and nothing is drawn on a context lost before its event.
  - `render/gpu/SwitchRenderer.ts`: the app's one `renderer` and `gpuDevice` (`renderer.device`). It forwards to the backend chosen at startup, because `FrameService`, `ImageService`, `TextRasterCache` and `PreviewView` are created at module load before the choice is made.
  - Startup and the unsupported screen:
    - `main.tsx` calls `chooseBackend` and `startGpu(choice)`.
    - `app/compat.ts`: the requirement reads "WebGPU (navigator.gpu) or WebGL2"; without either GPU renderer the screen lists "A GPU renderer: WebGPU or WebGL2 on a supported GPU with hardware acceleration turned on".
    - The dev stats line names the backend ("GPU ready · WebGL2 · device 1").
    - Dev globals: `__editor.backend`, and `__editor.gl` (the WebGL2 context, `loseForTest(ms)`); `__editor.gpu.loseForTest()` works on both backends.
  - Export: `ExportJobParams.renderer` is the preview's backend. `ExportRenderer` makes it with `recover: false`, and a WebGL2 context lives on the frame canvas. In Chrome 155 a VideoFrame cannot be made from a `bitmaprenderer` canvas nor from a WebGL canvas's ImageBitmap, only from the WebGL canvas itself (measured).
  - `PreviewView.render` returns at once while the renderer is not ready (a lost device). Renders during a loss used to throw (text raster uploads), and three in a row while playing would put the preview in its Batch 47 error state while a context is restored.

- deviations:
  - §1.4 is amended as the batch asks: WebGPU or WebGL2. WebGL2 counts only when it runs on the GPU (`failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat`): software rendering is still "no degraded mode".
  - The backend is chosen once at startup (no switch at runtime). The URL flag works in every build: it is harmless, and it lets a user whose WebGPU driver misbehaves use WebGL2.
  - WebGL2 presents the preview through `bitmaprenderer` from the context's own OffscreenCanvas: textures cannot be shared across contexts, and the preview canvas is remounted with its panel. The export draws into the context's canvas (the VideoFrame limits above).
  - WebGL2 textures are capped at 8192 px, WebGPU's default limit, so both backends upload the same sizes.
  - Measured, not fixed: 4K at Full quality without a proxy drops 0-18 of ~157 frames on WebGL2 against 1-2 on WebGPU. WebGL has no external textures, so the whole 4K frame is copied to RGBA before it is scaled. Auto quality plays the proxy (equal on both). The first playback after a page load drops more on both, more on WebGL2 (42-123).

  - Demuxer (own implementation, no dependency):
    - `media/demux/ebml.ts`: variable-length integers (unknown sizes included), element headers, values, `children` of a master in memory, and `WindowReader`, which serves a scan from 4 MB windows read straight from the file (`blobReader`: a full scan must not evict the decoders' chunks from the shared 64 MB cache).
    - `media/demux/webm.ts`: `readWebm` walks the EBML header (DocType webm or matroska), the Segment (known or unknown size), Info (TimestampScale), Tracks (the first enabled video and audio tracks; a video track with ContentEncodings is refused) and every Cluster (an unknown-size Cluster ends at the next top-level element), with SimpleBlocks and BlockGroups (Block, BlockDuration, ReferenceBlock). It keeps each video frame's payload offset, size, time and key flag, and each audio packet. A recording cut short ends at its last complete block. Laced video blocks are refused. `webmVideoTable` / `sampleIndexFromWebm` make the Batch 06 sample index: times in TimestampScale ticks (microseconds when 1e9 / scale is not whole), decode times = the sorted presentation times (H.264 B-frames), durations to the next frame shown. `webmProbeResult` / `probeWebm`, `webmAudioPlan` (Opus for decode.worker) and `webmAudioLeadUs`.
    - `media/demux/webmCodecs.ts`: WebCodecs strings. VP9: `vp09.PP.LL.DD`, profile and bit depth from the first key frame's uncompressed header (WebM VP9 has no configuration record), level from the VP9 level table (size and rate). AV1: `av01.P.LLT.DD` from the av1C in CodecPrivate, which is also the description. VP8: `vp8`. H.264: `avc1.PPCCLL` from the avcC. Other codecs are refused with their CodecID.
    - `media/demux/container.ts`: `isEbml` (the first 4 bytes), `probeVideoFile` and `parseSampleIndex` choose MP4 or WebM by content, not by name. Used by the decode worker's probe, `DecodeSessions` (preview, thumbnails in analysis.worker, the export's loopback sessions) and the proxy worker's `loadSampleIndex`. The index file format and `INDEX_VERSION` are unchanged.
  - Audio: Opus is decoded in decode.worker by `AudioTracks` from `webmAudioPlan`, the same range decodes as MP4 audio (media time 0 = the first frame, packets placed by their times). Vorbis, laced audio and Opus without a WebCodecs decoder read as unsupported, with `leadUs` (the first audio block after the first frame). `DecodedAudio` then decodes the file whole with decodeAudioData, pads or cuts the buffer by the lead, and closes the worker's track at once. See deviations.
  - Import: `.webm` maps to container `webm` (`video/webm`, in the Video picker types). The worker probes it; the failed-import row uses the Film icon. A `.webm` that is neither container gets "Not a readable WebM file: it is damaged or is not a video". Codec labels: VP9, AV1, VP8, Opus, Vorbis.

- deviations:
  - Audio: the batch says "decodeAudioData continues to handle audio". Opus (what browsers, screen recorders, YouTube and ffmpeg write) decodes in decode.worker like MP4 audio (Batch 10). Two reasons:
    - decodeAudioData holds the whole file as PCM: about 1.4 GB for a 60-minute recording, and non-MP4 audio over 45 minutes has been refused since Batch 47.
    - Its output starts at the first audio block. Measured on a Chrome screen recording: the audio would play 33-36 ms early; with the packet times it lands where the source has it.

    Vorbis, laced audio and Opus without a WebCodecs decoder still use decodeAudioData, placed on media time by the worker's `leadUs`. The export puts the clicks where the source has them on both paths (7-8 ms after the flashes).
  - The index comes from a scan of every Cluster, at the probe and at the first open (then from cache/index/), not from Cues. Cues list key frames only, and live recordings have none. Measured on a 10-minute recording: 0.44-0.47 s per scan, reading the file once.
  - Codecs: VP8 and H.264 in WebM are accepted besides VP9 and AV1. Chrome's MediaRecorder writes VP8 by default and H.264 into .webm with `codecs=h264`, and each costs one line. Other video codecs (HEVC, Theora) are refused at import, by CodecID. An AV1 track without its required av1C gets `av01.0.LLM.08` (Main, 8 bits, the level from the size).
  - `.mkv` stays refused by name (§9.1 lists `.webm`). Matroska content inside a `.webm` is read. Since the container is told by content, a WebM named `.mp4` also opens.
  - Not handled:
    - Rotation: Matroska files carry none in common use, so 0.
    - VP9 alpha (BlockAdditions): decodes opaque.
    - A recording whose size changes midway (a window resized while recording) is laid out at its first size (PixelWidth/Height).
    - Opus pre-skip (6.5 ms): Chrome's decoder handles it.
  - Frame rate snapping for jittery tick times (see notes) applies to every container. MP4 files with fine timescales are unchanged (half a tick is below the 0.03% tolerance there), and all earlier fps tests pass.
